# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) ## ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller & Motion Subsystem **Subsystem**: Lithography & Metrology Stage Electronics **Action Classification**: 🛒 BUY (COTS Qualified Component) **Target Processor**: ESP32-WROOM-32D (Dual-Core 240MHz Xtensa, 520KB SRAM, 4MB Flash) **Actuation Mode**: Closed-Loop Hardware Quadrature Decoding ($4\times$ PCNT) with PID Feedback --- ### 1. Hardware Pinout & Closed-Loop Architecture Schematic ```text ESP32 Closed-Loop System Block Diagram ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ ESP32-WROOM-32D Core Controller │ │ │ │ [ Core 0: Comm & Telemetry ] [ Core 1: 1kHz PID Loop ] │ │ - I2C OLED Display (GPIO 21/22) - PCNT Quad Decode (34/35) │ │ - UART Host Link (GPIO 1/3) - MCPWM Motor Drive (18/19) │ │ - E-Stop Interrupt (GPIO 4) - Limit Sw Input (GPIO 25/26)│ └────────┬──────────────────────┬──────────────────────┬─────────────────┘ │ │ │ ▼ ▼ ▼ ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ I2C Display │ │ Optocoupled │ │ Optical │ │ SSD1306 OLED │ │ Gate Driver │ │ Encoder │ │ (Status Mon) │ │ (TMC2209/DRV) │ │ (HEDS-9700) │ └──────────────┘ └────────┬────────┘ └──────▲───────┘ │ │ ▼ │ ┌─────────────────┐ │ │ NEMA 17 Stepper │─────────────┘ │ (0.9 deg, 400s) │ (Mechanical Coupling) └─────────────────┘ ``` #### Inline Technical SVG Pinout & Wiring Diagram:
![ESP32 Official DevKit Pinout Reference](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/02/ESP32_Pinout.png/640px-ESP32_Pinout.png) --- ### 2. Hardware Bill of Materials (BOM) & Reagent Specs | Component Class | Part Number / Model | Supplier / Vendor | Key Specification | Cost (USD) | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Microcontroller** | ESP32-WROOM-32D | Espressif Systems / DigiKey | 240MHz Xtensa LX6, 4MB Flash | $3.80 | | **Motor Gate Driver** | TMC2209 SilentStepStick | Trinamic / Watterott | 2.0A RMS, 256 microstepping, UART | $9.50 | | **Optical Encoder** | Broadcom HEDS-9700-E50 | Broadcom / Mouser | 500 LPI differential quadrature | $18.20 | | **Position Scale** | Linear Glass Scale ($100\text{ mm}$) | Ditron / AliExpress | $1.0\,\mu\text{m}$ grating resolution | $45.00 | | **Isolated DC Supply** | MeanWell LRS-75-24 | Mean Well / DigiKey | 24V DC @ 3.2A, Low Ripple $< 120\text{ mV}$ | $16.50 | --- ### 3. Step-by-Step COTS Qualification & Commissioning Protocol 1. **Hardware Power-On & Voltage Rail Verification**: - Apply $24.0\text{ V}$ DC from isolated linear power supply to motor driver rail. - Measure $3.30\text{ V} \pm 0.05\text{ V}$ rail on ESP32 3V3 pin with digital multimeter. 2. **Quadrature Pulse Counter (PCNT) Unit Calibration**: - Connect encoder Channel A to GPIO34, Channel B to GPIO35. - Configure ESP32 hardware **PCNT** unit in $4\times$ quadrature counting mode: ```c pcnt_config_t pcnt_config = { .pulse_gpio_num = 34, .ctrl_gpio_num = 35, .channel = PCNT_CHANNEL_0, .unit = PCNT_UNIT_0, .pos_mode = PCNT_COUNT_INC, .neg_mode = PCNT_COUNT_DEC, .lctrl_mode = PCNT_MODE_REVERSE, .hctrl_mode = PCNT_MODE_KEEP, .counter_h_lim = 32767, .counter_l_lim = -32768 }; ``` - Rotate motor shaft by hand exactly 1 turn; confirm register reads $2000 \pm 2$ counts ($500 \times 4$). 3. **1 kHz High-Priority FreeRTOS PID Loop Task**: - Pin dedicated PID control loop to **Core 1** running at strictly $1000\text{ Hz}$ ($1.0\text{ ms} \pm 20\,\mu\text{s}$). - Execute positional control algorithm: $$u(t) = K_p \cdot e(t) + K_i \sum e(t) \Delta t + K_d \frac{e(t) - e(t - \Delta t)}{\Delta t}$$ - Anti-windup threshold clamping at $[\pm 100\%]$ PWM duty cycle. 4. **Safety E-Stop Verification**: - Assert hardware emergency stop push-button (GPIO4 pulled LOW). - Verify motor driver `EN` pin disables within $< 250\,\mu\text{s}$, dumping inductive current to ground. --- ### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA) - **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Motor driver step/dir pulses must synchronize with closed-loop optical encoder feedback before commanding optical alignment moves. Hardware emergency stop and limit switches must be fail-safe. - **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Kinematic positioning resolution for Gen 1 (mm) must achieve < 0.1 mm (Gen 1) or < 1 um (Gen 2). Vibrational resonance damping must settle stage within <= 150 ms after step command. - **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: TMC2209 silent stepper drivers, NEMA 17/23 motors, and linear ground guide rails are standard COTS. Buy off-the-shelf; Make is strictly restricted to stage brackets, anti-backlash nut fixtures, and firmware. - **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 24 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: MEDIUM (Backlash and thermal expansion in lead screws degrade positioning repeatability). **Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**: 1. Mechanical lead-screw backlash exceeding 5 um during bidirectional fine step motion. 1. Stepper motor missed steps caused by microstepping resonance or driver thermal throttling. 1. Ground loop noise on encoder quadrature lines causing position loss. ### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench) | Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `TC-MCU-COTS-01` | **Stage Motion Repeatability & Anti-Backlash Bi-Directional Sweep** | Digital Dial Indicator (Mitutoyo 0.001 mm resolution) & Heidenhain Optical Linear Glass Scale | 1. Command stage to advance 10 mm forward in 100 um increments. 2. Reverse motion 10 mm back to initial origin coordinate. 3. Record position hysteresis gap between forward and reverse passes over 10 consecutive cycles. | `Positioning repeatability <= 1.0 um (Pass); Backlash hysteresis <= 2.0 um (Pass); Travel jerk < 0.05 m/s3 (Pass).` | | `TC-MCU-COTS-02` | **Driver Closed-Loop Thermal & Jitter Stability Stress Test** | FLIR Thermal Imaging Camera & 4-Channel Logic Analyzer on Step/Dir Pins | 1. Monitor motor driver heatsink temperature throughout continuous 2-hour exercise run. 2. Capture step pulse jitter and motor coil inductive flyback voltages. 3. Verify zero missed step flag triggered on controller interrupt line. | `Driver heatsink temp <= 65°C without fan throttling (Pass); Zero missed steps over 72,000,000 pulses (Pass).` | ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes - **Hazard Classification**: `Low` - **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD grounding wrist strap (1 MOhm safety resistor), Impact-resistant safety glasses, Close-toed cleanroom shoes - **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Flush eyes with eyewash if IPA splashes. Mechanical pinch point: isolate 24V power supply and mechanically release leadscrew. - **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom HEPA laminar flow bench (ISO Class 5). - **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent lint-free wipe disposal in approved self-closing oily waste bin. **Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**: | Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade 99.9% | `Precision stage guide rail degreasing` | ### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints - **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24.0 hours` - **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Clean dry substrate or mechanical component fixture. - **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Processed and inspected assembly node. - **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Particulate accumulation exceeding cleanroom ISO Class 5 limits. ### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done) **Exit Objective Summary**: > Completion of ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller: Precision kinematic stage drive motion achieves specified closed-loop positioning accuracy, bidirectional repeatability, and mechanical resonance damping. **Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**: - [ ] `Laser_interferometer_calibration_certificate.csv` - [ ] `Step_response_vibration_settling_FFT.png` - [ ] `Safety_limit_and_estop_interlock_log.pdf` **Quantitative Completion Assertions**: | Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `ASSERT-01` | **Bidirectional positioning repeatability** | `<= 50 nm (Gen 3) / <= 1.0 um (Gen 2) / <= 0.1 mm (Gen 1)` | +/- 10% of target value | Renishaw Laser Interferometer / Linear Optical Glass Scale | | `ASSERT-02` | **Resonance settling time post-motion pulse** | `<= 150 ms` | Upper threshold to settle within +/- 50 nm | Piezoelectric 3-axis accelerometer and dynamic signal analyzer | | `ASSERT-03` | **Holding position jitter / RMS drift** | `<= 20 nm RMS` | Measured over 10-minute stationary hold | Optical quadrature encoder high-speed counter telemetry | **Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**: > Continuous 10,000-cycle back-and-forth travel endurance test completed with zero lost microsteps; motor driver temperature stabilizes <= 55°C under continuous holding torque.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Automated Parametric Retention & March C- Diagnostic Test Firmware

Firmware architecture and algorithmic execution of industry-standard memory test patterns to isolate cell defects, sense amplifier offsets, and retention decay.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Saw-diced wafer mounted on UV dicing tape, clean and dry with zero particulate or water residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation of exposed aluminum/copper bond pads degrades thermosonic ball bond adhesion, inducing high electrical contact resistance or catastrophic non-stick bond pad lifts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of Automated Parametric Retention & March C- Diagnostic Test Firmware: BEOL metallization, electrical die sort (EDS), wafer backgrinding/dicing, and wirebond plastic encapsulation successfully yield JEDEC-qualified DRAM packaged units.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Electrical_Die_Sort_Wafer_Yield_Map.csv`
- [ ] `Wirebond_Ball_Shear_And_Pull_CPK_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `JEDEC_TSOP54_Final_ATE_SpeedBin_Report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Wirebond ball shear strength** | `>= 18.0 gf` | Minimum failure load >= 15.0 gf across 30 samples | Dage 4000 micro-tester lateral ball shear per MIL-STD-883 |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) wafer array functional yield** | `>= 90.0%` | Minimum yield >= 85.0% on prime wafers | Automated wafer probe array test with March C- diagnostic patterns |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Packaged DRAM package coplanarity & lead pitch** | `<= 0.08 mm coplanarity` | JEDEC TSOP-54 mechanical envelope tolerance (+/- 0.05 mm) | Optical 3D coordinate measuring machine (CMM) metrology |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% passing electrical continuity and JEDEC parametric DC checks; destructive wirebond shear CPK >= 1.67 with zero package voiding or delamination detected under scanning acoustic microscopy (C-SAM).

# SOP: ESP32 DRAM Low-Level Timing & Command Bus HAL Implementation

The actionable Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been authored and recorded in the repository documentation at [docs/sop_esp32_dram_low_level_timing_command_bus_hal.md](./docs/sop_esp32_dram_low_level_timing_command_bus_hal.md).

---

### Key Highlights of the SOP

#### 1. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure
1. **GPIO Pin Assignment & Fast Register HAL Setup**: Direct bit-level mapping to ESP32 register sets (`GPIO.out_w1ts` / `GPIO.out_w1tc`) bypassing high-latency APIs to handle row/column address multiplexing and strobes ($\overline{\text{RAS}}$, $\overline{\text{CAS}}$, $\overline{\text{WE}}$) matched to the $360\text{--}400\text{ nm}$ bitline/wordline pitch.
2. **Bus Timing Parameter Configuration**: Configure timings based on physical cell parameters—access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), minimum row activation $t_{RAS}$, precharge equalization time $t_{RP}$ to $V_{DD}/2$, and $t_{RCD}$ strobing delay.
3. **Low-Level Command Sequence Implementation**: Accurate execution of Read, Write, and Equalization sequences ensuring access transistor activation, charge redistribution $Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{BL})$, and latch sensing.
4. **Distributed Auto-Refresh Timer Engine**: High-resolution hardware timer (`esp_timer`) scheduling row refresh cycles to meet the retention requirement at $85^\circ\text{C}$ against sub-threshold/junction leakage ($\le 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$).

---

#### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target Metric | Unit | Physical Context / Verification Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Cell Capacitance Handled ($C_s$)** | $\ge 25.0 \text{ to } 28.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Stacked crown/cylinder capacitor ($Ta_2O_5 / Al_2O_3$ or ONO stack, $\kappa > 15$, $\text{EOT} = 3\text{--}4\text{ nm}$) |
| **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance Limit ($C_{BL}$)** | $\le 250.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Folded bitline array capacitance supported during signal development |
| **Differential Signal Window ($\Delta V$)** | $\ge 100.0 \text{ to } 150.0$ | $\text{mV}$ | Signal development window prior to sense amplifier latch strobe ($\Delta V = [C_s / (C_{BL} + C_s)] \cdot \|V_{\text{cell}} - V_{DD}/2\|$) |
| **Maximum Retention Refresh Window ($t_{REF}$)** | $\ge 64.0$ | $\text{ms}$ | Full array refresh interval window at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ with leakage $\le 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ |

---

#### 3. Citations & References
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; minimum capacitance $28\text{ fF/cell}$ ($\kappa > 15$); leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Bitline equalization to $V_{DD}/2$; charge dump $Q_s = C_s \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{BL})$; differential signal development $\Delta V = (C_s / (C_{BL} + C_s)) \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{DD}/2) \approx 100\text{--}150\text{ mV}$ for $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$, $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: Capacitance $25\text{--}30\text{ fF/cell}$; data retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; $\text{EOT} = 3\text{--}4\text{ nm}$; bitline/wordline pitch $360\text{--}400\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Using an ESP32 microcontroller GPIO matrix or dedicated SPI/parallel bus engine to emulate or interface with 180nm DRAM asynchronous/synchronous command timings introduces severe jitter vulnerability from FreeRTOS interrupts, dual-core cache misses, and APB peripheral clock divider granularity. To meet nanosecond-scale RAS-to-CAS delay (tRCD) and precharge time (tRP) without violation, timing-critical command pulses (/RAS, /CAS, /WE, /CS) must be synthesized via hardware state machines such as the ESP32 RMT (Remote Control), I2S parallel DMA mode, or dedicated SPI peripheral rather than software bit-banging.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm planar/stacked COB technology with ~28 fF cell capacitance and ~250 fF bitline capacitance, sensing margins yield a differential Delta V of only 100 mV to 150 mV. If the HAL fails to guarantee exact minimum tRAS (active-to-precharge time) during March C- execution, the sense amplifier cross-coupled latch cannot fully restore charge into the storage cell before precharge equalization (VDD/2), causing destructive soft bit flips and false retention degradation reports.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying COTS commercial ESP32-WROOM-32 modules (Action Type: Buy) requires strict verification of vendor silicon revision (V1 vs V3) and flash SPI mode. Batch-to-batch GPIO pad drive strength and slew rate differences (nominal 10 mA to 40 mA drive settings) directly impact signal integrity and capacitive bus loading over interposer wiring to the 180nm test socket.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: While buying commercial ESP32 development modules accelerates firmware deployment, software HAL validation must not slip the critical path milestone for the wafer-level automated test fixture. Firmware deliverable signoff requires reproducible oscilloscope capture logs and regression suites before mounting the 180nm packaged dies.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. GPIO switching jitter exceeding tRP (precharge time) causing sense amplifier incomplete equalization to VDD/2 and adjacent-cell coupling readout errors.
1. Inadvertent tri-state floating of /RAS or /CAS lines during ESP32 boot/reset sequence inducing spurious auto-refresh or uncommanded bank activations.
1. DMA FIFO underrun during burst March C- write sequences leading to invalid write cycles and unrefreshed cell data decay.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Deploy HAL firmware binary executing continuous /RAS assert -> tRCD delay -> /CAS assert -> tRAS hold -> Precharge sequence (100,000 cycles). 2. Attach oscilloscope probes to GPIO pins configured for /RAS, /CAS, /WE, and Address lines. 3. Configure scope infinite persistence and trigger on /RAS falling edge. 4. Measure minimum, maximum, and root-mean-square (RMS) pulse width of tRAS and tRP across 100,000 continuous trigger acquisitions. | `Measured tRAS mean must equal 45.0 ns with peak-to-peak jitter <= 1.2 ns; tRP mean must equal 20.0 ns with peak-to-peak jitter <= 0.8 ns; zero runt pulses below 18.0 ns allowed.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-1-02` | **ESP32 DMA-Backed March C- Algorithm Timing Bus Integrity Test** | Tektronix TLA7012 Logic Analyzer with 68-channel P6417 probes, Keithley 2450 SourceMeter monitoring VDD supply current. | 1. Execute complete March C- diagnostic pass: (w0), up(r0,w1), up(r1,w0), down(r0,w1), down(r1,w0), (r0) across 64 Kbit address space. 2. Capture all bus transactions on logic analyzer at 500 MHz sampling. 3. Monitor data setup time (tDS) and data hold time (tDH) relative to /WE and /CAS transitions. | `100% compliance with zero timing violations: tDS >= 8.0 ns and tDH >= 4.0 ns for all cycles; zero bus contention glitches; continuous execution completed without DMA FIFO underrun flag.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified ESD-safe anti-glare safety glasses, Class 0 static-dissipative nitrile cleanroom gloves (surface resistivity 10^6 - 10^9 ohms/sq), ESD wrist strap with 1 megohm series resistor connected to verified earth ground
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA inhalation, move personnel to fresh air immediately. For eye contact, flush eyes with deionized water for at least 15 minutes at eyewash station. In case of localized low-voltage electrical contact, disconnect bench power supply and assess for thermal burns.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics benchtop localized laminar fume extractor (minimum 100 CFM airflow) active during board solvent contact and soldering operations.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes must be placed into a dedicated, sealed, flame-resistant flammable waste container for hazardous waste pickup. No drain disposal allowed.

| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | Type 1 / ASTM D1193 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100%` |

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly desoldered or ultrasonic-cleaned gold-plated interposer socket contacts, free of flux residue and oxides.

# Standard Operating Procedure: March C- Diagnostic Engine & Fault Mapping Algorithm Implementation

**Category**: Firmware & Software | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The ESP32 firmware running the March C- engine (6N complexity: ↕(w0); ⇑(r0,w1); ⇑(r1,w0); ⇓(r0,w1); ⇓(r1,w0); ↕(r0)) must execute deterministic GPIO bit-bang or dedicated SPI/parallel bus timing directly against the 180nm DRAM test vehicle pads without FreeRTOS task preemption jitter. Any context-switch latency (>12.5 ns jitter) risks violating DRAM tRAS (active time), tRP (precharge time), and tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay) specifications, producing false positive pattern failures across row/column boundary transitions.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Fault mapping algorithms must explicitly distinguish between cell-level stuck-at faults (SAF0/SAF1), transition faults (TF), inversion/idempotent coupling faults (CFin, CFid), and bitline/wordline address decoder faults (AF). In a Gen 2 planar/quasi-planar test array, retention decay overlaps with March C- timing; therefore, March C- execution time per 1k-cell subarray must be constrained strictly below the minimum data retention window (tRET < 64 ms at 85°C) to prevent thermal leakage from masquerading as physical bridging or stuck-at defects.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: The ESP32 microcontroller modules (ESP32-WROOM-32E) and external high-speed level shifters (e.g., TI TXS0108E / SN74LVC8T245 for interfacing 3.3V COTS logic to 1.8V/3.3V DRAM I/O) are standard commercial off-the-shelf components, but pin-to-pad breakout fixture PCB turnaround in Vietnam and precision spring pogo-pin arrays (0.5mm pitch) face a 10-14 day fabrication lead time if customs clearance is delayed.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain Gen 2 schedule alignment, the firmware test harness must decouple hardware probe station bring-up from algorithm verification by utilizing an ESP32 hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) FPGA or high-speed SRAM mock fixture. Delivering the algorithm verification on hardware mocks before physical wafer probe delivery mitigates critical path risks and allows immediate 2D fault bitmap rendering upon wafer contact.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Address decoder fault misclassification caused by non-monotonic address sequencing during descending March elements (⇓(r0,w1) and ⇓(r1,w0)), masking open-circuit wordline bridge defects.
1. GPIO bus ringing and impedance mismatch on 180nm DRAM data I/O pins exceeding VIL/VIH thresholds, triggering spurious dynamic coupling fault (CFdyn) flags.
1. Internal memory exhaustion on ESP32 SRAM when allocating uncompressed physical fault bitmap arrays for arrays larger than 64 kbit, triggering FreeRTOS watchdog panic resets.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-2-01` | **March C- Deterministic Algorithmic Sequence and State Transition Verification** | ESP32-WROOM-32E DevBoard, Saleae Logic Pro 16 Logic Analyzer (500 MS/s digital sampling on 8-bit bus + control signals), Keysight InfiniVision DSOX3024T Oscilloscope, 50-ohm active probe adapters. | 1. Connect Saleae Logic Pro 16 probes to DRAM control pins (CS#, RAS#, CAS#, WE#) and Address line A0. 2. Trigger execution of March C- diagnostic routine: Element M0 ↕(w0), Element M1 ⇑(r0,w1), Element M2 ⇑(r1,w0), Element M3 ⇓(r0,w1), Element M4 ⇓(r1,w0), and Element M5 ↕(r0). 3. Capture all digital transitions across 10 complete algorithm iterations. 4. Log cycle time between consecutive read/write access strobes and parse automated address sequence increment/decrement vectors. | `Total algorithm complexity must measure exactly 10N memory operations ±0 ops (N=8192 words). Pulse-to-pulse strobe jitter across all March elements must be < 4.0 ns. Zero missed operations or inverted address counter steps detected across 10 iterations (Pass: 10/10 runs with 100% March C- protocol compliance).` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-2-02` | **Real-Time 2D Physical Fault Bitmap Compression and Mapping Accuracy** | ESP32 DevKit connected via USB-UART (CH340/CP2102 at 921600 baud) to Host PC running Python Diagnostic GUI/Bitmap Parser, Hardware Fault Injection Interposer board introducing controlled SAF0, SAF1, and adjacent-cell bridge shorts. | 1. Execute full March C- test pass over the 64-kbit address space. 2. Stream diagnostic fault telemetry and RLE compressed bitmap packet over UART to host console. 3. Reconstruct the 2D Cartesian fault coordinate matrix using host parser. 4. Cross-compare reconstructed coordinates and identified defect types (SAF, TF, CF) against injected ground truth matrix. | `100% detection and spatial localization accuracy for all injected physical defects (3 out of 3 faults correctly pinpointed at exact row/column coordinates). Total UART telemetry transmission latency < 250 ms. ESP32 heap utilization for bitmap management must remain strictly < 32 KB.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/impact safety glasses, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat (surface resistivity 10^6 - 10^9 ohms/sq), Class 100 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (powder-free, 4 mil), Continuous grounding heel straps and ESD wrist strap with 1 megohm inline resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately flush contaminated skin with copious amounts of DI water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated apparel. Eye contact: Rinse eyes at emergency eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Relocate personnel to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if irritation, dizziness, or respiratory discomfort persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation of PCB solvent cleaning and aerosol flux removal must occur within a certified laminar flow clean bench or ducted chemical fume hood providing minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s). Ambient test bay HVAC must maintain ISO Class 7 air quality with 20-30 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA solvent and wipe consumables must be collected in closed, grounded, explosion-proof hazardous solvent waste carboys labeled 'Flammable Solvent Waste - Isopropanol'. Zero drain disposal. Waste disposed of through licensed industrial chemical reclamation contractors.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI H2O)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: 180nm DRAM test die or packaged test coupon post-solvent-degrease (IPA ultrasonic clean, dry nitrogen blow-off), wire-bonded/packaged, with contact pads free of native oxide film, organic residues, and particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Die/coupon pads inspected post-test for probe scrub witness marks; surfaces decontaminated, dried under ionized N2 gun, and loaded into sealed antistatic conductive waffle packs under inert ambient.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the 30-minute ambient air exposure window promotes rapid atmospheric moisture condensation and galvanic corrosion on exposed 180nm aluminum/copper bond pads, causing probe contact resistance (Rc) to spike above 5 ohms and generating false March C- continuity fail alarms.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified, deterministic March C- diagnostic engine firmware deployed on ESP32 microcontroller architecture, capable of executing full 10N test sequences on 180nm DRAM test vehicles within physical retention constraints, generating real-time RLE-compressed 2D fault bitmaps with exact defect classification.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `march_c_diagnostic_firmware_v2.1.0_build.bin`
- [ ] `dram_fault_mapping_engine_verification_report.pdf`
- [ ] `physical_2d_defect_spatial_bitmap_dataset.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **March C- operation count compliance over tested memory array** | `10` | ±0 operations/cell (strictly 10N operations) | Automated logic analyzer bus transaction decoding via Saleae Python API across full address space. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total execution time for full 64-kbit subarray March C- pass** | `42.0` | ±3.0 ms (must remain strictly < 50.0 ms to preserve retention integrity) | High-precision hardware timer benchmark logged over ESP32 64-bit cycle counter (esp_timer_get_time). |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Physical address-to-defect coordinate localization accuracy** | `100.0` | 0.0% error margin across known injected fault test vectors | Automated software cross-correlation script comparing serial telemetry bitmap against injected physical fault map. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal engineering sign-off requires 100 consecutive automated March C- execution passes across a calibrated 64-kbit DRAM test vehicle with zero timing violations, zero false-positive defect calls, complete RLE fault map generation under 32 KB RAM usage, and written sign-off from the Systems Engineer and Lead Firmware Architect.

# Standard Operating Procedure: March C- Algorithmic Sequence Generator & State Machine Architecture

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The March C- algorithmic state machine partitioning across an ESP32 host firmware and the 180nm CMOS memory controller interface introduces clock-domain crossing and bus-turnaround latencies that can obscure true 180nm dynamic timing faults. If the state machine executes sequentially in software over GPIOs without dedicated cycle-accurate shift-register hardware or DMA/SPI serializer, transition delay faults (such as slow write recovery t_WR or sense amplifier overdrive failure) will be masked by millisecond-scale test loop overheads. The architecture must guarantee deterministic cycle-level assertion of {Uparrow(w0); Uparrow(r0, w1); Uparrow(r1, w0); Downarrow(r0, w1); Downarrow(r1, w0); Downarrow(r0)} without jitter exceeding +/- 1.2 ns.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: March C- has a complexity of 10N and provides 100% fault coverage for address decoder faults (AFs), stuck-at faults (SAFs), transition faults (TFs), and inversion/idempotent coupling faults (CFin, CFid). However, on 180nm 6F^2/8F^2 stacked-capacitor over bitline (COB) topologies, adjacent cell parasitic capacitive coupling (C_bitline and C_cell-to-cell) creates intense pattern-sensitive faults (PSF) and write disturb failures that simple linear addressing misses unless the address generator supports both physical topological scrambler mapping (X-Fast, Y-Fast, and diagonal marching) and alternating data background generation (solid 00/FF, checkerboard, and stripe topologies).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing automated test fixtures using commercial off-the-shelf ESP32 microcontrollers interfaces cleanly with low-cost open-source parametric test boards. However, high-speed custom level-shifters (3.3V LVCMOS to 1.8V 180nm Core I/O) and surface-mount pogo-pin test sockets are single-sourced with lead times exceeding 8 to 12 weeks. Ensuring PCB-level availability of high-bandwidth discrete buffers (e.g., TI SN74AVC4T245) and ESD-protected socket interposers is the critical supply chain bottleneck for deployment.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable schedule risk centers on firmware-hardware co-verification. Developing the FSM in ESP32 firmware while the 180nm discrete MOSFET and test inverter logic arrays are undergoing physical Stage 3 Reality Gate verification causes serial blocking. The diagnostic state machine sequence generator must first be validated against an RTL gate-level simulation (Verilog testbench) using synthetic fault injection before physical wafer-level probe card touchdowns begin.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Address Decoder Stutter/Glitch: Transient race conditions in address multiplexing logic causing simultaneous wordline (WL) assertion during March element 2 Uparrow(r0, w1), triggering unrecoverable multi-cell destructive overwrite.
1. Write Recovery Violation (t_WR): Insufficient precharge setup timing between the consecutive read and write operations in Uparrow(r0, w1) leading to pseudo-pass reads followed by incomplete stacked capacitor charging (< 28 fF target charge level).
1. Bitline Coupling False Diagnostic: Bitline-to-bitline crosstalk triggering erroneous adjacent cell flip, causing the state machine to misclassify physical capacitive dielectric leakage as an algorithmic coupling fault (CF).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-2-1-01` | **Cycle-Accurate March C- State Sequence & Address Directional Transition Test** | Keysight MSOX6004A Mixed Signal Oscilloscope (4 GHz, 20 GSa/s), logic analyzer probe pod (16 channels digital), 50-ohm active differential probes. | 1. Configure ESP32 diagnostic state machine to run full March C- sequence across 1024-word physical test macro. 2. Arm Keysight MSOX6004A to trigger on Start-of-Test (SOT) GPIO high edge. 3. Monitor Wordline Address lines (A[9:0]), Column Select (CS), Write Enable (WE_n), and Data In/Out bus. 4. Execute Phase 0: Uparrow(w0); Phase 1: Uparrow(r0, w1); Phase 2: Uparrow(r1, w0); Phase 3: Downarrow(r0, w1); Phase 4: Downarrow(r1, w0); Phase 5: Downarrow(r0). 5. Record cycle timing, transition jitter, and state machine status flag registers upon End-of-Test (EOT). | `Total March operation count strictly equals exactly 10N = 10,240 cycles. Zero missing address steps (strictly monotonic 0 -> 1023 on Uparrow and 1023 -> 0 on Downarrow). State machine cycle-to-cycle clock jitter must remain < 650 ps RMS, and WE_n to Address setup time t_AS >= 3.5 ns.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-2-1-02` | **Deterministic Synthetic Fault Injection & Diagnostic Classification Verification** | Tektronix AWG5200 Arbitrary Waveform Generator, Keysight 3458A 8.5-Digit Digital Multimeter, Agilent 16702B Logic Analysis System. | 1. Reset March C- state machine diagnostic engine and zero fault logging SRAM. 2. Arm AWG5200 to inject synthetic transient ground clamp (forcing SA1) at cell address 0x00A5 during Phase 1 Uparrow(r0, w1) read phase. 3. Arm AWG5200 to inject transition block on cell address 0x02F0 during Phase 2 Uparrow(r1, w0). 4. Trigger full March C- diagnostic sequence execution from ESP32 master firmware. 5. Extract diagnostic error map register via high-speed UART/JTAG at 921600 baud. 6. Compare logged error vector against expected synthetic fault coordinates. | `Fault detection rate must be exactly 100% (2/2 injected faults captured). Fault classification vector must accurately tag Address 0x00A5 as 'SAF1' at Step 1 and Address 0x02F0 as 'TF0' at Step 2 with 0 false positive detections across the remaining 1022 addresses.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 2 Cleanroom ESD-safe nitrile gloves (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV and impact safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative polyester-carbon blend lab coat with grounded wrist strap, Closed-toe ESD-protective static dissipative footwear (< 35 MOhm resistance)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA skin contact: Wash thoroughly with water and mild soap for at least 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush immediately with emergency eye wash station water for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologic medical attention. Inhalation: Move victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. For nitrogen-induced displacement/asphyxiation risk: Evacuate area immediately to open atmosphere and administer CPR if pulse ceases.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop testing must occur within a certified laminar flow hood (ISO Class 5) maintaining face velocity of 90 to 110 FPM with localized active exhaust port for solvent cleaning of probe pins; cleanroom continuous air turnover minimum 45 changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA wipes and solvent rinses in designated hazardous solvent waste containers with dedicated flame arrestors and secondary containment. Do not drain into sanitary sewers; dispose of through certified Class 3 flammable waste collection contractors.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (Semiconductor IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP 5.0) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: WLCSP or wire-bonded open-cavity package contacts cleaned via UHP N2 blow-off and zero visible oxide or organic film (contact resistance R_c < 0.25 ohms/pad).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Probe-tested pads inspected post-test for probe scrub mark depth not exceeding 20% of M6 aluminum pad thickness (no bare silicon or barrier layer exposure).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes ambient atmospheric oxidation and moisture adsorption on wire bond pads and pogo pins, increasing parasitic contact impedance > 1.5 ohms, yielding false write-recovery margin failures and erratic algorithmic test loop aborts.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable delivery of the synthesizable RTL/firmware state machine core executing the full March C- 10N algorithmic sequence on the ESP32 diagnostic controller, fully verified against a 180nm open-source DRAM macro array testbench with deterministic hardware timing and bit-accurate fault mapping capabilities.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `march_c_fsm_timing_verification_report.pdf`
- [ ] `injected_fault_classification_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `pogo_pad_post_test_scrub_profilometry.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Algorithmic execution cycle overhead per cell** | `10.0` | +/- 0.0 cycles/cell | Logic analyzer hardware cycle trace counting from SOT to EOT assert flags |
| `ASSERT-02` | **March C- algorithmic state transition clock frequency** | `20.0` | +/- 1.0 MHz | Direct oscilloscope measurement on test clock strobe line using Keysight MSOX6004A |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Synthetic memory fault detection recall rate** | `100.0` | 0.0% | Automated regression suite comparing injected bit failure logs against firmware UART diagnostic report |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit signoff requires 100 consecutive error-free executions of the 10N March C- diagnostic sequence across the physical 180nm DRAM test macro, confirmation of ASSERT-01 through ASSERT-03 within nominal specs, zero pogo scrub penetration > 20% pad thickness verified by optical profilometry, and formal approval by both Systems Engineer and Lead Domain Expert.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## March C- Algorithmic State Machine (FSM) Micro-Architecture & Sequence Specification

**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Open-Source DRAM  
**Target:** 1T1C Folded Bitline Array Diagnostic Engine & BIST Sequence Generator  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. FSM Micro-Architecture & March C- Sequence Flow

The March C- algorithmic state machine executes a sequence of 6 March elements totaling $10N$ array operations ($\{\updownarrow (w0); \Uparrow (r0, w1); \Uparrow (r1, w0); \Downarrow (r0, w1); \Downarrow (r1, w0); \updownarrow (r0)\}$) across all active rows/columns to detect address decoder faults (AF), stuck-at faults (SAF), transition faults (TF), inversion coupling faults (CFin), and idempotent coupling faults (CFid).

```text
┌───────────────┐
│               │
│   M0: ⇕ w0    │
│               │
└───────┬───────┘
        │
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────┐
│               │
│  M1: ⇑ r0 w1  │
│               │
└───────┬───────┘
        │
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────┐
│               │
│  M2: ⇑ r1 w0  │
│               │
└───────┬───────┘
        │
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────┐
│               │
│  M3: ⇓ r0 w1  │
│               │
└───────┬───────┘
        │
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────┐
│               │
│  M4: ⇓ r1 w0  │
│               │
└───────┬───────┘
        │
        │
        ▼
┌───────────────┐
│               │
│   M5: ⇕ r0    │
│               │
└───────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Implementation Procedure

#### Step 1: Array Topology & Physical Parameter Initialization
- Configure the algorithmic address generator according to the array block organization:
  - **Access Transistor:** Gate length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, channel width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
  - **Array Layout:** Folded bitline $8F^2$ topology (cell area $0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\,\text{nm}$, bitline/wordline pitch $360\,\text{nm}$ to $400\,\text{nm}$) partitioned into array blocks with $256$ to $512$ cells per bitline.
  - **Storage Node:** Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) crown/cylinder structure with ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric ($3\,\text{nm}$ to $4\,\text{nm}$ EOT, effective $\kappa > 15$).

#### Step 2: FSM Controller State Encoding & Pointer Logic
- Configure the address sequencer registers:
  - Direction flag: $\text{DIR} \in \{\text{UP}, \text{DOWN}, \text{ANY}\}$.
  - Step counter: $k \in [0, N-1]$ mapped to Wordline (Row) and Bitline (Column) decode buses.
- **State M0 ($\updownarrow, w0$):** Traverse all addresses ($0 \to N-1$ or arbitrary order); drive bitlines to write background pattern `0` into the storage node capacitor.
- **State M1 ($\Uparrow, r0, w1$):** Traverse strictly ascending ($0 \to N-1$). Read and compare stored state against expected `0` (latch failure flag if mismatch); immediately perform write-back of `1`.
- **State M2 ($\Uparrow, r1, w0$):** Traverse strictly ascending ($0 \to N-1$). Read and verify stored state `1`; write-back `0`.
- **State M3 ($\Downarrow, r0, w1$):** Traverse strictly descending ($N-1 \to 0$). Read and verify stored state `0`; write-back `1`.
- **State M4 ($\Downarrow, r1, w0$):** Traverse strictly descending ($N-1 \to 0$). Read and verify stored state `1`; write-back `0`.
- **State M5 ($\updownarrow, r0$):** Traverse all addresses; perform final read verification against expected `0`.

#### Step 3: Sense Amplifier Timing & Read Signal Margin Guarding
- Gate the FSM read-strobe with sense amplifier activation delay to accommodate bitline charge sharing:
  - Ensure bitline precharge is held at $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$ prior to wordline activation.
  - Verify access transistor gate dielectric ($\sim 3.5\,\text{nm}$ physical $\text{SiO}_2$ dry oxidation at $850^\circ\text{C}$–$900^\circ\text{C}$) drive current safely charges bitlines with capacitance $C_b = 150\,\text{fF}$ to $250\,\text{fF}$.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                                                        
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░░                               │
C_b / C_s Ratio (Max)┤░░                               │
      C_b (Max Range)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
        C_s (Nominal)┤█████                            │
                     │█████                            │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0.0    62.5    125.0   187.5 250.0 
```

1. **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$):**
   - **Target Metric:** $\ge 25\,\text{fF}$ to $30\,\text{fF}$ per cell (Nominal: $28\,\text{fF}$).
2. **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance ($C_b$):**
   - **Target Metric:** $150\,\text{fF}$ to $250\,\text{fF}$ per bitline block ($256$ to $512$ cells per bitline).
3. **Bitline-to-Storage Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$):**
   - **Target Metric:** Maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (must strictly not exceed $10:1$ to maintain read signal margin).
4. **Access Transistor Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$) & Retention Window:**
   - **Target Metric:** Sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, maintaining retention time $> 64\,\text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context.yaml):**
  - Specifies transistor dimensions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) crown/MIM topology with ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$/$\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ ($\kappa > 15$), nominal cell capacitance budget $\ge 28\,\text{fF}$, and leakage target $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **[Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context.yaml):**
  - Details 1T1C $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ architecture, capacitor requirements of $25\,\text{fF}$ to $30\,\text{fF}$ per cell, retention time $> 64\,\text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, $\text{EOT} = 3\,\text{nm}$ to $4\,\text{nm}$, wordline/bitline pitch of $360\,\text{nm}$ to $400\,\text{nm}$, and $\sim 3.5\,\text{nm}$ gate oxide grown at $850^\circ\text{C}$–$900^\circ\text{C}$.
- **[1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets](file:///d:/coding/dram/docs/context.yaml):**
  - Defines folded bitline $8F^2$ footprint area ($0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\,\text{nm}$), bitline parasitic budget $C_b = 150\,\text{fF}$ to $250\,\text{fF}$ across $256$ to $512$ cells/bitline, and strict $C_b / C_s$ ratio bounds of $5:1$ to $9:1$ ($< 10:1$ upper bound).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup

- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Epoxy die-attached, cured, and thermosonically wirebonded to leadframe/substrate pads prior to molding.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## RTL Implementation of Address/Data Pattern Generator & Command Pipeline

### 1. Architectural Overview & Context
This leaf SOP governs the RTL implementation of the **March C- Algorithmic Sequence Generator**, containing the address traversal engine (up/down counter with linear, row-fast, or column-fast ordering), data background generator, and pipeline alignment stage driving the DRAM core.

```text
┌─────────────────────┐
│    March C- FSM     │
│     Controller      │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           ├──────────────────────────╮
           ▼                          ▼
┌─────────────────────┐    ┌─────────────────────┐
│   Address Pattern   │    │   Data Background   │
│      Generator      │    │      Generator      │
└─────────┬───────────┘    └──────────┬──────────┘
          │                           │
          │ ╭─────────────────────────╯
          ▼ ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│  Command Pipeline   │
│      Register       │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│  DRAM Timing & PHY  │
│      Interface      │
└─────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Implementation Procedure

#### Step 1: March C- State Machine Traversal Definition
- Implement synchronous state sequencing covering the standard March C- pattern:
  $$\{\Uparrow (w0); \Uparrow (r0, w1); \Uparrow (r1, w0); \Downarrow (r0, w1); \Downarrow (r1, w0); \Uparrow (r0)\}$$
- Register direction control `addr_dir` ($0 = \Uparrow, 1 = \Downarrow$) and current target pattern vector `exp_data` ($0$ or $1$, inv: `~exp_data`).

#### Step 2: Parameterized Address Pattern Generator
- Implement up/down address generator register with address space matching physical wordline/bitline array geometry.
- Access transistor channel length is $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width is $W = 220\text{ nm}$ per unit cell in folded bitline topology.
- Support burst increment/decrement with wrap-around flags and boundary interrupt status flags for row-column crossing to preserve sense amplifier precharge timing.

#### Step 3: Command & Data Pipeline Alignment
- Synchronize command output (`CMD_ACT`, `CMD_PRE`, `CMD_READ`, `CMD_WRITE`) to ensure valid precharge equalizing bitlines to $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$.
- Register `wdata` and `rdata_expected` into an execution pipeline matched to memory latency cycles to prevent data-bus contention and timing violations.
- Ensure minimum sensing window margin allows signal development:
  $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right) \approx 100\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV}$$
  prior to sense-amplifier strobe activation.

#### Step 4: Logic Synthesis & Timing Closure
- Synthesize RTL against the target standard cell library using the open-source digital toolchain (e.g., OpenROAD).
- Constrain clock periods to satisfy internal register setup/hold times and verify zero timing slack violations across operational voltage and corner temperatures.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

### 4. Verified Context Citations
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Unit cell access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; minimum storage capacitance $C_s = 28\text{ fF/cell}$; sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Bitline equalization to $V_{\text{DD}}/2$; differential signal $\Delta V = (C_s / (C_{\text{BL}} + C_s)) \cdot (V_{\text{cell}} - V_{\text{DD}}/2) \approx 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ with nominal $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$.
- **SkyWater 130nm Open PDK Overview & Architecture**: ASIC synthesis flow integration with OpenROAD tooling, digital standard cell generation, and liberty timing constraint files.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: FPGA DDR PHY state machine must rigorously implement JEDEC initialization sequences (200 us CKE low, precharge all, MRS registers). Skew across high-speed DDR DQ/DQS matched traces must hold <= 10 ps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: PCB transmission line characteristic impedance must hold strictly at 50-ohm single-ended / 100-ohm differential (+/- 5%). Eye diagram opening at receiver must maintain >= 65% horizontal width and >= 200 mV vertical height.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Xilinx/Intel FPGA development carrier boards and high-speed SMA fixtures are standard COTS. Make is strictly restricted to custom daughtercard PCB layout, Verilog DDR PHY controller RTL, and firmware.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 32-60 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Jitter or power rail ripple on FPGA PLL induces intermittent read/write pattern errors during high-speed diagnostic telemetry sweeps).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Clock-to-data skew violating tIS/tIH setup/hold timing margin during DDR write bursts.
1. Power distribution network impedance resonance causing core VDD droop > 100 mV during simultaneous output switching.
1. Asynchronous clock domain crossing metastability in memory controller telemetry FIFO.

Probe DQ0-DQ7 and DQS differential strobe lines directly at DRAM test daughtercard receiver pins. 2. Accumulate 1,000,000 signal transitions into persistence eye diagram. 3. Execute March C- sequence: (w0), up(r0, w1), up(r1, w0), down(r0, w1), down(r1, w0), (r0). 2. Sweep retention pause times from 1 ms to 128 ms between write and read phases. 3. Stream per-address failure bitmap via UART/USB to telemetry logging engine. | `March C- 100% address pass at nominal 64 ms refresh window (Pass); Zero bit error rate (BER < 1e-12) (Pass).` |

- **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD smock and grounded conductive wrist strap (1 MOhm safety resistor), Safety glasses with side shields during soldering and PCB prototyping, Nitrile gloves during circuit board solvent cleaning

- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Point-of-use HEPA/carbon solder fume extractor at soldering workstation (airflow >= 150 m3/h). Standard laboratory climate-controlled HVAC.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solder dross and PCB trimmings in designated recycling bin for precious metal recovery. Solvent cleaning wipes in sealed flammable safety receptacle.

- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully assembled, reflow-soldered, ultrasonic-cleaned, and impedance-tested PCB daughtercard.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Non-critical queue time. If bare PCBs exceed MSL shelf-life (> 168 hours in air), pre-bake at 125°C for 4 hours before reflow soldering to prevent PCB delamination and blistering.

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

### Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
**Title**: March C- Diagnostic Engine Testbench Simulation & Fault Coverage Metrology  
**Document Link**: [sop_march_c_diagnostic_engine_testbench_fault_coverage.md](./docs/sop_march_c_diagnostic_engine_testbench_fault_coverage.md)  
**Generation**: Gen 2 (180nm / µm) | **Action Type**: Buy  

---

#### 1. Simulation & Verification Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Setup 180nm DRAM    │
│     Array Netlist     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Inject Physical    │
│     Fault Models      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Execute March C-    │
│  Sequence Generator   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Sense Amp Strobe &   │
│  Timing Verification  │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Fault Coverage     │
│       Metrology       │
│      Calculation      │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Array Netlist & Parasitic Setup**:
   - Instantiate the $8F^2$ folded bitline cell array ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$, $F = 180\text{ nm}$) with NMOS access transistor dimensions $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, and $t_{ox} = 3.5\text{ nm}$.
   - Set cell storage capacitance to nominal $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$ (acceptable range $25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$) with dielectric $\kappa > 15$, and bitline capacitance to $C_b = 200\text{ fF}$ (within the $150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ block window).
   - Enforce capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ strictly between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (nominal $7.14:1$).
   - Parameterize storage node sub-threshold/junction leakage at $< 1.0\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain retention target $> 64\text{ ms}$.

2. **Fault Injection Matrix Definition**:
   - **Stuck-At Faults (SAF)**: Inject SA0 ($V_{SS}$) and SA1 ($V_{DD}$) across cell nodes and bitlines.
   - **Transition Faults (TF)**: Force rising ($0 \to 1$) and falling ($1 \to 0$) transition blockages.
   - **Address Decoder Faults (AF)**: Emulate non-consecutive wordline multi-selection and decoder decoding slips across the $360\text{ nm}-400\text{ nm}$ pitch array.
   - **Coupling Faults (CFin / CFid)**: Inject coupling capacitance ($C_{couple} > 0.15 \times C_b$) between adjacent bitline pairs.

3. **March C- Diagnostic Sequence Execution ($10N$ Algorithm)**:
   - Phase 1: $\Updownarrow (w0)$ — Global background initialization.
   - Phase 2: $\Uparrow (r0, w1)$ — Ascending read '0', write '1'.
   - Phase 3: $\Uparrow (r1, w0)$ — Ascending read '1', write '0'.
   - Phase 4: $\Downarrow (r0, w1)$ — Descending read '0', write '1'.
   - Phase 5: $\Downarrow (r1, w0)$ — Descending read '1', write '0'.
   - Phase 6: $\Updownarrow (r0)$ — Final read verify all cells equal '0'.

4. **Sense Amplifier Strobe & Signal Margin Validation**:
   - Verify differential strobe signal $\Delta V_{BL} \ge 120\text{ mV}$ prior to latch activation across all read strobes.
   - Confirm timing deskew between March C- pattern generator strobes and sense amplifier latch enable.

5. **Fault Coverage Metrology & Mapping**:
   - Compare simulation response against the reference memory map to extract detection percentage:
     $$\text{Fault Coverage} = \frac{\text{Detected Fault Count}}{\text{Total Injected Fault Count}} \times 100\%$$
   - Export physical failure bitmapping coordinates (Row, Column, Bitline pair) for defect localization.

---

#### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric | Target Specification | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **SAF & TF Fault Coverage** | $100.0$ | $\%$ | Automated Simulation Fault Injector Log |
| **Address Decoder Fault Coverage (AF)** | $100.0$ | $\%$ | March C- Vector Verification Log |
| **Coupling Fault Coverage (CFin / CFid)** | $\ge 98.0$ | $\%$ | Adjacent Cell Inter-bitline Injection Test |
| **Bitline-to-Cell Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)** | $5.0 : 1 \text{ to } 9.0 : 1$ | Ratio | Post-layout Extracted Netlist Parameter Check |
| **Read Strobe Signal Margin ($\Delta V_{BL}$)** | $\ge 120.0$ | $\text{mV}$ | Transient Differential Sense Strobe Probe |

---

#### 4. Fault Coverage Metrology Summary

```text

               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ │

TF (Transition)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
   AF (Address)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
               │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│

               │███████████████████████████████████████│
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
                0        25       50        75      100 
```

---

#### 5. Source Citations
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline, $\kappa > 15$, $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$, leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: $8F^2$ folded bitline footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$), $C_s = 25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$), $C_b = 150\text{ to }250\text{ fF}$, $C_b / C_s$ bound between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (must not exceed $10:1$).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: Retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$, bitline/wordline pitch $360\text{ to }400\text{ nm}$, gate $t_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The March C- testbench must bridge the ESP32 GPIO/SPI timing model with the DRAM asynchronous row/column addressing interface. Cycle-accurate simulation is required to verify that the algorithmic state machine does not violate row-to-column delay (tRCD) and precharge time (tRP) under worst-case clock jitter from the ESP32 APB bus clock (80 MHz).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: March C- algorithmic sequence { ⇕ (w0); ⇑ (r0, w1); ⇑ (r1, w0); ⇓ (r0, w1); ⇓ (r1, w0); ⇕ (r0) } requires exhaustive verification against modeled DRAM defect mechanisms: single stuck-at faults (SAF), transition faults (TF), address decoder faults (AF), and inter-cell coupling faults (CFin, CFid). Fault injection testbenches must achieve 100% test coverage for target modeled primitives on the 180nm storage cell array.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Test firmware and simulation harnesses must run on standard open-source RTL simulators (Verilator/Icarus Verilog) and COTS ESP32-S3-WROOM development modules without requiring proprietary Automated Test Equipment (ATE) software licenses, ensuring reproducible deployment across Vietnamese open-source microfabrication partners.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Testbench coverage analysis and fault injection report generation must be containerized in the project CI pipeline, completing full March C- simulation runs in under 15 minutes per git commit to avoid gating firmware release schedules.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Address decoder aliasing fault (AF) masking caused by non-monotonic address traversal or state machine skip states in the down-addressing phase ⇓ (r0, w1)
1. Timing race condition between ESP32 write strobe pulse width (tWP) and DRAM sense amplifier latch timing during back-to-back read-modify-write transitions
1. Incomplete stuck-open fault detection due to parasitic capacitive charge retention on long bitline simulation models simulating falsely as valid logic 1

Log all detected error flags, fault address capture registers, and compute fault detection ratio. | `All 6 March C- operational phases complete in strict sequence order; 100% (128/128) injected target faults detected and logged with zero false negatives; total simulation time <= 120 seconds.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-2-1-3-02` | **ESP32 Hardware-in-the-Loop March C- Bus Timing and Latency Metrology** | Keysight DSOX1204G (or Siglent SDS1104X-E) 100MHz Digital Storage Oscilloscope, Saleae Logic Pro 16 Logic Analyzer, ESP32-S3 Breakout Board | 1. Power ESP32 target at 3.3V DC regulated supply. 2. Execute firmware self-diagnostic March C- run in loop mode (10 iterations). 3. Capture 500,000 digital samples at 100 MSa/s. 4. Measure pulse width of write enable tWP, row address setup time tASR, and read-to-write turnaround latency. 5. Verify timing adherence against 180nm DRAM Gen 2 operational limits. | `Measured write strobe pulse width tWP >= 25.0 ns; row address hold time tRAH >= 10.0 ns; zero bus contention glitches (>0.8V during tri-state handover); 0 failed write/read cycles across 10 iterations.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Class 0 ESD-safe dissipative wrist strap and grounded work mat, Cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, 4 mil thickness)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air. Skin contact: Wash contact area thoroughly with soap and water. Eye contact: Flush eyes with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; drink water and seek immediate medical consultation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronic laboratory mechanical ventilation providing >= 6 air changes per hour (ACH); local chemical exhaust snorkel active when handling solvent wipe containers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA lint-free wipes must be deposited into closed, spring-loaded, fire-rated flammables disposal bins. Solvent effluent disposed of through certified hazardous chemical liquid waste stream.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: ESP32 diagnostic test PCB assembly and packaged/probed test chip contact pads clean, free of organic flux residues, degreased with IPA wipe, and desiccated.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspected contact probe lands and test socket pins free of micro-welds, oxidation, or mechanical deformation; PCB stored in ESD protective shielding bags.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Surface oxidation on exposed copper/gold test pads leading to increased contact resistance (>5 Ohms), contact bounce during high-speed sampling, and false failure reports during diagnostic metrology.

> Full algorithmic verification and timing metrology of the March C- diagnostic engine implemented on ESP32 firmware, demonstrating complete functional fault coverage across all classical DRAM defect models in co-simulation and meeting timing margins on physical logic analyzer metrology.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## ESP32 Low-Level Memory Interface & Real-Time Pattern Execution Driver

- **Document ID:** `SOP-DRAM-FW-004`
- **Node Title:** ESP32 Low-Level Memory Interface & Real-Time Pattern Execution Driver
- **Hierarchy:** `180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip` > `ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller` > `Automated Parametric Retention & March C- Diagnostic Test Firmware` > `March C- Diagnostic Engine & Fault Mapping Algorithm Implementation` > `ESP32 Low-Level Memory Interface & Real-Time Pattern Execution Driver`
- **Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type:** Buy (COTS ESP32 Platform / Commercial Controller Interface)
- **Author:** Domain Expert AI (DRAM Foundation VN Multi-Agent Council)

---

### Execution & Architecture Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   ESP32 Driver Init    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   GPIO Bus & Direct    │
│       Reg Config       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Real-Time Wordline /  │
│     Bitline Timing     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    March C- Pattern    │
│     Step Execution     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Bitline Sensing &    │
```
