| `ASSERT-02` | **Subthreshold access transistor leakage current (Ioff)** | `<= 1.0 fA/cell` | Max ceiling at 85°C junction temperature | Keysight B1500A sub-fA High-Resolution SMU |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Folded bitline differential sense voltage margin (Delta VBL)** | `>= 180 mV` | Min threshold >= 150 mV across all PVT corners | Strobe sense amplifier latch comparator with calibrated offset voltage |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Statistical Tail-Bit Decay Extraction & Thermal Retention Limit Analysis

**Document Code:** `SOP-MET-DRAM180-042`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm, 1T1C Stacked Capacitor / Folded Bitline)  
**Classification:** Metrology & Characterization Leaf SOP  
**Related Knowledge Doc:** [statistical_tail_bit_decay_analysis.md](./docs/knowledge/statistical_tail_bit_decay_analysis.md)

---

### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│    Step 1: Array     │
│    Initialization    │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Step 2: Thermal    │
│    Soaking & Bias    │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│   Step 3: Variable   │
│    Retention Hold    │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│    Step 4: March     │
│  Sensing & Tail-Bit  │
│       Capture        │
│                      │
└───────────┬──────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌──────────────────────┐
│                      │
│  Step 5: Arrhenius   │
│      Activation      │
│      Extraction      │
│                      │
└──────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Array Initialization & Pre-Conditioning:**
   - Mount the 180nm DRAM test vehicle on the closed-loop thermal chuck interface driven by the ESP32 closed-loop controller.
   - Execute an initial all-`0` write sweep followed by an all-`1` write sweep at nominal wordline and bitline operating bias using the automated March C- diagnostic firmware.
   - Confirm cell layout mapping: 8F² folded bitline topology (nominal cell area $0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$, access NMOS length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$, wordline/bitline pitch $360\,\text{nm}$ to $400\,\text{nm}$).

2. **Thermal Stabilization & Controlled Soaking:**
   - Ramp the thermal stage chuck to the baseline operating limit of **85°C** (soak duration: 120 s to reach isothermal equilibrium across the die).
   - Ensure supply lines ($V_{\text{DD}}$, bitline precharge $V_{\text{BLP}} = V_{\text{DD}}/2$) are regulated within $\pm 1\%$.

3. **Variable-Delay Retention Stress (Charge-Decay Profiling):**
   - Apply pattern write: fill 256/512-cell bitline array blocks with solid data-`1` (charging storage capacitors $C_s \ge 25\,\text{fF}$ nominal).
   - Inhibit automatic background refresh cycles.
   - Step hold pause duration ($t_{\text{pause}}$) through a logarithmic schedule: $10\,\text{ms}, 20\,\text{ms}, 40\,\text{ms}, 64\,\text{ms}, 128\,\text{ms}, 256\,\text{ms}, 512\,\text{ms}$, and $1000\,\text{ms}$.

4. **Burst Read March C- & Tail-Bit Capture:**
   - Execute read verify $\Uparrow (r1)$ at the conclusion of each hold interval.
   - Capture bitline sensing pass/fail states where parasitic capacitance $C_b$ (nominal $150\,\text{fF} \text{ to } 250\,\text{fF}$) causes read margin collapse whenever storage node charge decays below sensing threshold.
   - Stream bit error coordinates $(X, Y)$ and fail counts via the UART/SPI telemetry logger to classify weak tail-bits falling below cumulative distribution population thresholds.

5. **Multi-Temperature Arrhenius Extraction:**
   - Repeat steps 1–4 across temperature setpoints: $25^\circ\text{C}, 55^\circ\text{C}, 85^\circ\text{C}$, and $105^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Plot bit fail fraction vs. retention pause time on Weibull probability paper; isolate normal distribution bulk bits from defective/leakage tail-bits.
   - Extract junction and sub-threshold leakage activation energy $E_a$ to verify dominant leakage mechanisms (trap-assisted tunneling vs. SRH generation).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                      Cell Characterization Targets     
                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐
                 │░                                    │
Leak Target @ 85C┤░                                    │
                 │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
 Cb Parasitic Max┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
   Ret Time @ 85C┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                           │
                 │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                           │
   Cs Storage Cap┤█████                                │
                 │█████                                │
                 └┬────────┬────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0.0     62.5     125.0    187.5  250.0 
```

| Metric Parameter | Specification Target | Physical Unit | Measurement Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Retention Time ($t_{\text{ret}}$)** | $\ge 64$ | $\text{ms}$ | At $85^\circ\text{C}$ across bulk array cells |
| **Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $25 \text{ to } 30$ (nominal $28$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Stacked Crown/Cylinder capacitor with high-$\kappa$ / ONO dielectric |
| **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance ($C_b$)** | $150 \text{ to } 250$ | $\text{fF}$ | Per 256/512 cells per bitline ($C_b / C_s$ ratio between $5:1$ and $9:1$, strictly $< 10:1$) |
| **Max Cell Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Total sub-threshold and junction leakage at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source 1: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Context:* Access transistor channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$; minimum $28\,\text{fF}$ per cell capacitance budget; sub-threshold and junction leakage $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source 2: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Context:* 1T1C stacked capacitor architecture (8F² or 6F²); storage capacitance $25 \text{ to } 30\,\text{fF/cell}$; data retention time $> 64\,\text{ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; bitline/wordline pitch $360 \text{ to } 400\,\text{nm}$; gate dielectric $\sim 3.5\,\text{nm}$ $\text{SiO}_2$.
- **Source 3: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**
  - *Context:* Folded bitline 8F² cell area ($0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\,\text{nm}$); nominal $C_s \ge 25 \text{ to } 30\,\text{fF}$ (nominally $28\,\text{fF}$); bitline parasitic $C_b = 150 \text{ to } 250\,\text{fF}$ (256/512 cells/BL); capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ between $5:1$ and $9:1$ ($< 10:1$ degradation limit).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-3-3-3-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FIRMWARE-3-3-3-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Silicon dicing slurry centrifuged and segregated into solid cake for non-hazardous landfill. Cured thermoset epoxy scrap disposed of as regulated solid waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Epoxy Novolac Resin (Mold Compound)** | `29690-82-2` | Semiconductor Packaging Grade | `Solid pellet / transfer mold compound` |
| **Amorphous Silica Filler** | `14808-60-7` | Sub-micron spherical particle | `75-88 wt% in epoxy mold compound` |
| **Silver-Filled Conductive Die Attach Adhesive** | `7440-22-4` | Electronic Grade Silver Flake | `70-80 wt% Ag in epoxy base` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120.0 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48.0 hours`

# Standard Operating Procedure: FPGA High-Speed DRAM Memory Controller Core

Implementation, synthesis, and timing verification of open-source Verilog RTL for the DRAM physical layer (PHY) controller, auto-refresh scheduling, and command sequencer.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Bridging an ESP32 host via an intermediate bus (SPI/QSPI/Parallel) to an FPGA-synthesized JEDEC DDR controller driving a custom 180nm DRAM chip introduces a critical domain-crossing latency and clock synchronization bottleneck. The FPGA PHY must maintain strict I/O timing margins (setup/hold tDS/tDH < 450 ps at 133-200 MHz DDR) while translating JEDEC state sequences without overflowing FIFO buffers during motor-control burst writes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm, cell charge Q_s is limited to ~25-28 fF per cell with bitline delta V between 100 mV and 150 mV. The JEDEC state machine must strictly respect tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay >= 15 ns), tRP (Row Precharge >= 15 ns), and deterministic tREFI refresh dispatching (<= 64 ms over 4096 rows, i.e., 15.6 µs per refresh tick). Any jitter or phase drift in the FPGA DQS gating window will corrupt sensing or latching operations during read cycles.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Targeting standard open-source toolchain-compatible FPGAs (e.g., Lattice ECP5 or Gowin GW2A) for low-cost validation ensures vendor neutrality; however, PCB trace impedance (50 Ohm single-ended, 100 Ohm differential for CK/CK# and DQS/DQS#) requires tightly controlled stackups and discrete matched series termination resistor arrays that must remain readily sourceable across regional distributors.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Schedule risk centers on JEDEC compliance timing closure in synthesis and physical lab validation against silicon prototype test fixtures. Firmware-to-FPGA register integration must be decoupled from PHY calibration routines to enable parallel testbench development using cocotb/Verilator before tape-out hardware arrives.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. DQS read-enable gating window misalignment causing false preamble capture and bit slippage during high-speed burst reads.
1. Refresh starvation caused by priority inversion in the motor-controller command arbitration queue, leading to data loss in unrefreshed 28 fF 1T1C storage nodes.
1. Setup/hold timing violations on command/address lines during temperature excursions due to uncompensated FPGA I/O delay line (IDELAY/ODELAY) drift.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-01` | **JEDEC State Machine Protocol Timing & tREFI Refresh Enforcement Verification** | 16-channel 1 GHz Mixed Signal Oscilloscope (Keysight InfiniiVision DSOX3014T), 34-channel Logic Analyzer (Saleae Logic Pro 16), calibrated high-bandwidth differential active probes. | 1. Reset controller via active-low reset assertion for 200 µs. 2. Trigger initialization sequence: CKE low, NOP command issue, PRECHARGE ALL, EXTENDED MODE REGISTER SET (EMRS), and AUTO REFRESH cycles. 3. Issue 1,000 randomized ACTIVATE, READ, WRITE, and PRECHARGE transactions under continuous background auto-refresh dispatch. 4. Capture command bus traces (CS#, RAS#, CAS#, WE#, CKE) and timestamp intervals between successive REFRESH commands across 100,000 clock cycles. | `Zero protocol violations detected: tRCD >= 15.0 ns, tRP >= 15.0 ns, tRAS >= 40.0 ns. Refresh interval tREFI must measure <= 15.60 µs +/- 0.05 µs across all recorded cycles without command collision or FIFO underflow.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-02` | **DDR PHY DQS-DQ Eye Margin and Burst Read/Write Bit Error Rate Test** | High-Speed Real-Time Oscilloscope (Teledyne LeCroy WaveRunner 8000HD 2 GHz, 10 GS/s), Pseudo-Random Binary Sequence (PRBS-7) generator module inside FPGA, thermal chamber (-10°C to +85°C). | 1. Configure testbench to stream PRBS-7 continuous burst write sequences across full address space at 133 MHz DDR (266 MT/s). 2. Read back data bursts over 10^9 continuous cycles while sweeping DQS receive delay line taps from 0 to 255. 3. Measure horizontal eye opening (jitter) and vertical eye opening (voltage margin) at the FPGA DQ receivers. 4. Repeat measurements at 25°C, -10°C, and +85°C. | `Measured horizontal eye opening >= 65% of bit period (>= 2.44 ns at 266 MT/s); vertical eye opening >= 350 mV; Bit Error Rate (BER) = 0 across 10^9 transmitted bits (zero bit errors recorded).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Powder-free cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (4 mil)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with IPA cleaning solvent, flush eyes immediately with tepid water from an eye wash station for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual to fresh air. For thermal burns from soldering/rework equipment, cool skin immediately with clean cold running water for 10 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics lab benchtop snorkel exhaust or HEPA/carbon fume extraction unit (minimum flow rate 150 m^3/h) active during board rework, connector cleaning, or IPA flux residue removal.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of solvent-soaked wipes and contaminated swabs in dedicated, sealed, flame-resistant hazardous waste safety cans labeled 'Flammable Waste - Isopropanol'; route to licensed semiconductor hazardous waste disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI / Semiconductor Grade) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `1440 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `168 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly reflowed or socketed FPGA test carrier board and gold/ENIG edge connectors cleaned with electronic-grade IPA and dried with dry N2 blow-off.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cleaned, flux-free PCB assembly with ESD protective bagging, stored in nitrogen dry cabinet at < 5% RH to avoid pad oxidation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Surface oxidation and atmospheric moisture adsorption on high-speed single-ended/differential test traces causing contact impedance degradation, signal integrity loss, and sporadic DQS eye closure during high-frequency testing.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete, fully verified Verilog HDL core for the JEDEC DDR memory controller and PHY, validated via RTL simulation testbenches and physical FPGA-to-DRAM hardware loop testing at >= 133 MHz DDR with compliant tREFI refresh dispatch and zero bit errors over 10^9 cycles.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_controller_phy_top.v`
- [ ] `jedec_timing_compliance_report.pdf`
- [ ] `dqs_eye_diagram_margin_data.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum operating clock frequency of the synthesized DDR controller and PHY on target FPGA** | `133.33 MHz` | +/- 2.0 MHz | Static Timing Analysis (STA) report in FPGA toolchain under worst-case PVT corner combined with direct oscilloscope frequency measurement of CK/CK# pins |
| `ASSERT-02` | **JEDEC auto-refresh period interval tREFI compliance across all operating cycles** | `15.60 us` | +0.00 / -0.20 us | Hardware logic analyzer state trace capture recording 100,000 consecutive REFRESH command issue timestamps |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Continuous read/write data transmission bit error count across full memory address space** | `0 errors` | +0 errors | Integrated FPGA hardware PRBS-7 BIST comparison logic executed across 10^9 continuous read/write cycles |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Static timing closure achieved with positive slack (>= 250 ps) across all clock domains, zero JEDEC protocol violations observed in 100,000 cycles on logic analyzer, and zero bit errors recorded across 10^9 PRBS-7 transaction cycles on hardware test fixture.

# Standard Operating Procedure: JEDEC Timing & Refresh Protocol State Machine Architecture Modeling

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The JEDEC timing and refresh FSM architecture directly governs the deterministic bus turn-around times between the FPGA PHY controller and the 180nm DRAM core. A major vulnerability is clock-domain crossing (CDC) jitter between the asynchronous motor-control feedback loop of the ESP32 and the synchronous DDR state machine on the FPGA, which risks violating tRP (Row Precharge Time) and tRCD (RAS-to-CAS Delay) margins during burst read-modify-write refresh interrupts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node, bitline capacitance C_BL is substantial (typically 200–350 fF), necessitating an extended charge restoration cycle where SAN pulls to ground and SAP pulls to V_DD before issuing an auto-refresh (tRFC) or precharge command. If the JEDEC protocol FSM issues a precharge (tRP) prior to full signal amplification and charge restoration, subthreshold leakage through the access NMOS will corrupt cell retention margins across the 64ms refresh budget.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing this architecture on open-source FPGA toolchains (such as Yosys/nextpnr) targeted at cost-effective COTS FPGAs (e.g., Lattice ECP5 or Gowin) requires pinning specific I/O banks with calibrated DQS/DQ delay lines. Any supply dislocation in calibrated delay cells or tight-tolerance external termination resistor arrays will disrupt signal integrity at the 180nm testboard interface.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The integration milestone requires seamless co-simulation of the Verilog FSM with the analog SPICE netlist extracted via OpenROAD/OpenRCX. Unsynchronized timing models between the digital OpenROAD CTS tree and analog bitline sense-amp restore timings will stall the MPW tape-out schedule if signoff margins are not locked down upfront.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature Precharge Truncation: Issuing a PRECHARGE command before tRAS_min elapses, interrupting PMOS SAP pull-up restore and leaving storage node voltage below 0.9*V_DD, causing retention bit flips.
1. Refresh Collision Starvation: Distributed auto-refresh state machine locks the memory controller during continuous closed-loop motor commutation bursts, inducing command FIFO buffer overflow and loss of motor feedback state.
1. tRFC Timing Violation during Temperature Spikes: Elevated junction temperature decreases 180nm retention time, while FSM counter remains fixed at nominal tRFC cycles without dynamic temperature-compensated refresh (TCSR).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-01` | **JEDEC tRAS/tRP Protocol Compliance & Wordline Charge Restoration Verification** | Keysight Infiniium MXR-Series 4 GHz 16 GSa/s Oscilloscope, differential active probes on WL/BL/SAN/SAP, and an FPGA embedded Logic Analyzer (ILA) core running at 200 MHz. | 1. Issue an ACTIVATE command to Row 0x00A0 via FPGA JEDEC state machine. 2. Measure elapsed delay from WL rising edge (50% V_PP) to SAN pull-down activation. 3. Monitor SAP rising to 1.8V and capture the earliest allowed PRECHARGE command emitted by the FSM. 4. Measure tRAS (ACT-to-PRE delay) and tRP (PRE-to-ACT delay) across 10,000 continuous random access cycles. 5. Verify storage capacitor node retention voltage via high-impedance sense-amp probing. | `Measured tRAS must be >= 45.0 ns and tRP >= 18.0 ns; cell restore voltage at precharge initiation must reach >= 98.5% of V_DD (1.773 V); zero CDC synchronization errors reported by the FPGA logic analyzer across 10,000 cycles.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-02` | **Auto-Refresh (CBR) State Machine Timing & Command Arbitration Under Full Bus Saturation** | Tektronix TLA7012 Logic Analyzer connected to Command/Address bus (CS#, RAS#, CAS#, WE#, CKE) with 100 ps timing resolution and custom JEDEC protocol violation trigger. | 1. Saturate the FPGA memory controller with continuous back-to-back Read/Write bursts. 2. Force the internal refresh timer to fire at tREFI intervals. 3. Record state machine arbitration latency from tREFI trigger to REFRESH command issuance on the external bus. 4. Verify that the FSM asserts bus hold and observes tRFC (Refresh Cycle Time) before allowing subsequent ACTIVATE commands. 5. Inspect data integrity of read responses after 100,000 back-to-back refresh events. | `Refresh cycle time tRFC must strictly satisfy 75.0 ns <= tRFC <= 95.0 ns; no incoming motor controller read/write command dropped or FIFO overrun; 100% data retention verified with 0 bit errors (BER < 10^-12).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100 / ISO 5 compatible), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, ESD-safe dissipative lab coat and grounded dual-conductor wrist strap, Vapor respirator equipped with organic vapor/acid gas cartridges (during board solvent cleaning)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with copious clean water or eyewash station solution for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. Skin Contact: Wash thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and water; remove contaminated dissipative clothing. Inhalation: Relocate personnel to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop chemical fume hood or local exhaust ventilation (LEV) arm operating at a face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) minimum during PCB assembly cleaning and flux residue extraction.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate organic solvent washings in dedicated grounded, spark-proof, labeled flammable solvent collection drums; do not mix with aqueous acid/base drains; dispose through certified hazardous chemical recovery services.

critics.systems_engineer: The JEDEC timing and refresh FSM architecture directly governs the deterministic bus turn-around times between the FPGA PHY controller and the 180nm DRAM core. A major vulnerability is clock-domain crossing (CDC) jitter between the asynchronous motor-control feedback loop of the ESP32 and the synchronous DDR state machine on the FPGA, which risks violating tRP (Row Precharge Time) and tRCD (RAS-to-CAS Delay) margins during burst read-modify-write refresh interrupts.
critics.domain_expert: At the 180nm node, bitline capacitance C_BL is substantial (typically 200–350 fF), necessitating an extended charge restoration cycle where SAN pulls to ground and SAP pulls to V_DD before issuing an auto-refresh (tRFC) or precharge command. If the JEDEC protocol FSM issues a precharge (tRP) prior to full signal amplification and charge restoration, subthreshold leakage through the access NMOS will corrupt cell retention margins across the 64ms refresh budget.
critics.supply_chain: Implementing this architecture on open-source FPGA toolchains (such as Yosys/nextpnr) targeted at cost-effective COTS FPGAs (e.g., Lattice ECP5 or Gowin) requires pinning specific I/O banks with calibrated DQS/DQ delay lines. Any supply dislocation in calibrated delay cells or tight-tolerance external termination resistor arrays will disrupt signal integrity at the 180nm testboard interface.
critics.laya_pm: The integration milestone requires seamless co-simulation of the Verilog FSM with the analog SPICE netlist extracted via OpenROAD/OpenRCX. Unsynchronized timing models between the digital OpenROAD CTS tree and analog bitline sense-amp restore timings will stall the MPW tape-out schedule if signoff margins are not locked down upfront.
critical_failure_modes: Premature Precharge Truncation: Issuing a PRECHARGE command before tRAS_min elapses, interrupting PMOS SAP pull-up restore and leaving storage node voltage below 0.9*V_DD, causing retention bit flips.

Refresh Collision Starvation: Distributed auto-refresh state machine locks the memory controller during continuous closed-loop motor commutation bursts, inducing command FIFO buffer overflow and loss of motor feedback state.

tRFC Timing Violation during Temperature Spikes: Elevated junction temperature decreases 180nm retention time, while FSM counter remains fixed at nominal tRFC cycles without dynamic temperature-compensated refresh (TCSR).

# Standard Operating Procedure: JEDEC Timing Parameters Specification & FSM Architecture Definition

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The FSM architecture specification must tightly bind JEDEC timing parameters (tRAS, tRP, tRCD, tRC) directly to the physical gate delays (tau_d <= 80 ps/stage from the 11-stage ring oscillator) and storage cell leakage (sub-threshold/junction leakage < 1 fA/cell at 85 deg C). Attempting to operate the controller state machine at standard SDR/DDR frequencies without accounting for RC bitline propagation delay in an 8F^2/6F^2 stacked capacitor (C_cell = 28 fF) array will cause state-transition races during precharge-to-activate windows.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node open-source DRAM architecture, tREFI must be strictly constrained by the retention decay curve of the 28 fF ONO/high-k MIM stacked capacitor. At 85 deg C, a 1 fA leakage corresponds to dV/dt = I/C = 1e-15 / 28e-15 = 35.7 mV/s, but soft error margin and sense amplifier offset (V_M = 0.90 V +/- 50 mV) demand a maximum distributed refresh interval tREFI of 64 ms (or 7.8 us per row auto-refresh cycle across 8192 rows). The FSM must enforce hardware-locked command locks to prevent tWR (write recovery) violation before issuing PRECHARGE.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing the controller core on COTS FPGA hardware interfacing to fabricated 180nm test dies requires standard LVCMOS 1.8V I/O pin compatibility matching the 1.8V VDD rail. Sourcing high-speed multi-channel pattern generators/logic analyzers (e.g., Keysight 16860 series) with sub-nanosecond skew matching between FPGA I/O banks and test socket fixtures in regional fabrication partner facilities must be de-risked early.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable schedule must de-couple RTL digital logic synthesis of the JEDEC state machine from the final physical parameter extraction of the tungsten-plug/stacked-capacitor test coupons. Any shift in measured cell capacitance below 28 fF will trigger an immediate renegotiation of tRAS_min and tRC cycle budget milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Data corruption due to premature PRECHARGE command issuance violating minimum active-to-precharge time (tRAS_min), causing incomplete cell capacitor restoration through the sense amplifier.
1. Refresh starvation under sustained burst read/write cycles where the arbiter fails to prioritize auto-refresh (REF) commands within the maximum 7.8 us tREFI window, causing capacitor voltage drop below sense amp delta-V threshold (50 mV).
1. Write-recovery (tWR) timing violation causing bit-flip errors during consecutive write-to-precharge sequences due to uncalibrated I/O pad and W-plug series resistance.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-1-01` | **JEDEC State Machine Command Timing & Interlock Verification** | Keysight 16864A 68-Channel Logic Analyzer (4 GHz timing / 400 MHz state), Rohde & Schwarz RTO6 4 GHz 20 GSa/s Oscilloscope, Xilinx Artix-7/Spartan-7 FPGA Evaluation Board | 1. Program FSM configuration registers with target 180nm parameters: tRCD = 20 ns (2 cycles), tRAS = 50 ns (5 cycles), tRP = 20 ns (2 cycles), tWR = 15 ns (2 cycles), tRC = 70 ns (7 cycles).\n2. Stream continuous pseudo-random command sequence attempting deliberate timing violations (e.g., ACTIVATE to READ at 1 cycle, ACTIVATE to PRECHARGE at 3 cycles, WRITE to PRECHARGE at 1 cycle).\n3. Monitor FSM output flags and command bus via Logic Analyzer, capturing state illegal-transition flags and stall assertions.\n4. Measure command propagation skew on oscilloscope across CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n lines across 1,000,000 clock cycles. | `Zero illegal command sequences emitted on physical bus; FSM must insert wait/stall cycles maintaining tRCD >= 20.0 ns, tRAS >= 50.0 ns, tRP >= 20.0 ns, and tWR >= 15.0 ns with timing jitter < 150 ps; assertion error interrupt asserted on all injected illegal command stimuli.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-1-02` | **Retention-Limited Auto-Refresh (tREFI/tRFC) State Machine Timing & Priority Arbiter Verification** | Tektronix TLA7016 Logic Analyzer, Keysight B2902B Precision Source/Measure Unit (SMU), FPGA Thermal Chamber at 85 deg C | 1. Initiate continuous multi-bank burst read/write transaction streams occupying 100% bus utilization.\n2. Trigger auto-refresh timer event and record the exact latency from timer expiration to the issuance of the REF command on the command bus.\n3. Measure auto-refresh duration (tRFC) to ensure FSM holds row decoders in inactive state for exactly >= 75 ns (8 cycles).\n4. Force simulated peak traffic load for 64 continuous ms (8192 refresh cycles) and verify total executed refresh cycles. | `Refresh command latency from timer expiry must not exceed 2.2 us under peak burst traffic (guaranteeing no refresh loss); exactly 8192 REF commands executed per 64.0 ms window (+/- 0.01%); tRFC commanded duration >= 75.0 ns without collision.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD-safe lab coat, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact safety glasses, Static-dissipative nitrile gloves (Class 100 cleanroom compatible), Heel/wrist ground straps with 1 Megaohm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact: Wash thoroughly with soap and water; remove contaminated ESD apparel. For eye contact: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of water from eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open. For inhalation: Move to fresh air. If irritation persists, seek medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard cleanroom / ESD electronics lab laminar flow bench with HEPA filtration (Class 1000/ISO 6) and dedicated low-volume solvent local exhaust ventilation (LEV) duct for IPA wipe-down operations maintaining face velocity >= 100 FPM.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes and swabs must be collected in closed, dedicated metal safety cans labeled 'Hazardous Waste - Flammable Solvent Solids' and disposed of through certified chemical waste management vendors in compliance with RCRA regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-received wire-bonded or socketed FPGA interposer board with gold-plated (ENIG) contact pads free of particulate contamination (> 0.3 um) and flux residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cleaned, nitrogen-blown, desiccated interposer package ready for environmental chamber probe card mounting.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption and atmospheric oxide formation on micro-pitch socket pins causing contact resistance exceeding 100 mOhm, leading to signal reflection, ground bounce, and false timing violations on sub-nanosecond JEDEC setup/hold checks.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Synthesized, formal-equivalence-verified, and lab-instrumented JEDEC Timing Parameters Specification and State Machine Controller Core in synthesizable Verilog RTL, matching the physical 180nm DRAM cell retention (28 fF, < 1 fA leakage) and inverter delay (tau_d <= 80 ps). Fully verified on FPGA testbed with 100% coverage of standard timing interlocks and refresh scheduling.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `jedec_dram_fsm_timing_spec_v2.0.pdf`
- [ ] `fsm_controller_core_timing_bench_report.csv`
- [ ] `logic_analyzer_timing_waveform_trace.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Minimum Active-to-Precharge time enforcement (tRAS_min)** | `50.0 ns` | +/- 0.5 ns | Keysight 16864A Logic Analyzer time-interval measurement over 500,000 ACT-to-PRE command cycles |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Distributed row refresh interval period (tREFI per row across 8192 rows)** | `7.8125 us` | +/- 0.05 us | Continuous hardware counter register logging correlated with external 100 MHz disciplined oscillator clock reference |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Internal FSM command decode and arbitration propagation latency** | `10.0 ns (1 clock cycle at 100 MHz)` | +/- 0.2 ns | Rohde & Schwarz RTO6 4 GHz Oscilloscope measurement from FPGA input register clock edge to command strobe output pad |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> 100% pass across all JEDEC formal assertion suites in RTL simulation, zero timing violations across 10^9 continuous cycles on FPGA hardware testbench at 85 deg C, and signed engineering sign-off from both Digital Architecture and Circuit Design leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Analytical Derivation of Critical DRAM Timing Parameters ($t_{RP}$, $t_{RCD}$, $t_{RAS}$, $t_{RC}$)

**Document ID:** `SOP-CKT-DRAM180-004`  
**Node Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Cell Area:** $0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ ($8F^2$) / $0.194\ \mu\text{m}^2$ ($6F^2$)  
**Context:** DRAM Foundation VN — Open-Source 180nm DRAM Chip & FPGA Memory Controller PHY  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Timing Decomposition

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Wordline Activation:  │
│          tRCD          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Sense Amp Sensing &   │
│       Overdrive        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Cell Charge       │
│   Restoration: tRAS    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Bitline Precharge:   │
│          tRP           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Total Random Cycle:   │
│    tRC = tRAS + tRP    │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

```text
                   180nm DRAM Timing Budget Limits (ns) 
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │████████████████████████████████████│
tRC (Random Cycle)┤████████████████████████████████████│
                  │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓         │
 tRAS (Min Active)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓         │
   tRP (Precharge)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                          │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                          │
tRCD (Act to Read)┤░░░░░░░░░░                          │
                  │░░░░░░░░░░                          │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     14.2     28.5    42.8    57.0 
```

---

### 2. Physical & Electrical Parameter Baseline
All derivations are calibrated directly against the verified 180nm process metrics:
- **Access Transistor Dimensions**: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, $T_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$ (thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ dielectric).
- **Storage Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)**: Nominal $28\text{ fF}$ (valid physical range: $25\text{ fF} \le C_s \le 30\text{ fF}$).
- **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance ($C_b$)**: $150\text{ fF} \le C_b \le 250\text{ fF}$ (for $256$ to $512$ cells per bitline).
- **Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)**: $5:1 \le C_b / C_s \le 9:1$ (upper limit $< 10:1$).
- **Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage**: $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ ($t_{REF} > 64\text{ ms}$).
- **Operating Voltage**: $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$, $V_{BL\_PRE} = V_{DD} / 2 = 0.90\text{ V}$.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Analytical Derivation Procedure

#### Step 1: Calculate Read Signal Differential Margin ($\Delta V_{BL}$)
Prior to sense amplifier firing, determine the common-mode charge-sharing voltage shift across the bitline pair:
$$\Delta V_{BL} = \frac{V_{DD}/2}{1 + \frac{C_b}{C_s}}$$
- For nominal $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$ and mid-range $C_b = 200\text{ fF}$ ($C_b / C_s \approx 7.14$):
$$\Delta V_{BL} = \frac{0.90\text{ V}}{1 + 7.14} \approx 110.5\text{ mV} \quad (\text{Range across process: } 90\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV})$$

#### Step 2: Formulate RAS-to-CAS Delay ($t_{RCD}$)
$t_{RCD}$ comprises Wordline RC propagation delay, cell-to-bitline charge-sharing time, and cross-coupled latch sensing overdrive delay:
$$t_{RCD} = t_{WL\_rise} + t_{share} + t_{SA\_sense}$$
1. **$t_{WL\_rise}$**: Distributed RC line delay over wordline pitch ($360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$), driven via boosted wordline voltage $V_{PP} \approx 2.5\text{ V}$ to overcome access transistor $V_{th}$: $t_{WL\_rise} \approx 3.2\text{ ns}$ to $4.5\text{ ns}$.
2. **$t_{share}$**: Time for access transistor ($W/L = 220\text{ nm} / 180\text{ nm}$, on-resistance $R_{on} \approx 4.5\text{ k}\Omega$) to transfer $> 95\%$ charge:
   $$t_{share} \approx 3 \cdot R_{on} \cdot C_s \approx 3 \cdot (4500\,\Omega) \cdot (28 \times 10^{-15}\,\text{F}) \approx 0.38\text{ ns}$$
3. **$t_{SA\_sense}$**: Time required for sense amplifier to amplify $\Delta V_{BL}$ past $90\%\,V_{DD}$ for column select read enablement: $t_{SA\_sense} \approx 8.5\text{ ns} - 10.0\text{ ns}$.
4. **Target Allocation**: $t_{RCD} = 15.0\text{ ns}$ (JEDEC standard bin at 180nm).

#### Step 3: Formulate Active-to-Precharge Time ($t_{RAS}$)
$t_{RAS}$ enforces complete cell charge restoration ($Q_{restored} \ge 99\%\,Q_{full}$) to protect against destructive read:
$$t_{RAS} = t_{RCD} + t_{restore}$$
1. During sensing, the access transistor remains active under boosted $V_{PP}$. The storage node charges through $R_{on}$ from the full-rail driven bitline:
   $$t_{restore} = 4.6 \cdot \tau_{cell} = 4.6 \cdot (R_{on\_access} + R_{plug}) \cdot C_s \approx 25\text{ ns} - 27\text{ ns}$$
2. Adding safety guardbands for array substrate bounce and bitline IR drop:
   $$t_{RAS} = 15.0\text{ ns} + 27.0\text{ ns} = 42.0\text{ ns}$$

#### Step 4: Formulate Row Precharge Time ($t_{RP}$)
$t_{RP}$ is the time required for equalization transistors ($V_{eq}$) to reset both $\text{BL}$ and $\overline{\text{BL}}$ back to $V_{DD}/2 = 0.90\text{ V}$ within $\pm 1\%$ offset tolerance:
$$t_{RP} = \tau_{eq} \cdot \ln\left(\frac{V_{DD}}{V_{offset\_tol}}\right) = (R_{eq\_eff} \cdot C_b) \cdot \ln\left(\frac{1.8\text{ V}}{0.018\text{ V}}\right) = 4.605 \cdot (R_{eq\_eff} \cdot C_b)$$
- With equalization network effective resistance $R_{eq\_eff} \approx 13.0\text{ k}\Omega$ and $C_b = 250\text{ fF}$:
  $$t_{RP} = 4.605 \cdot (13\times 10^3\,\Omega) \cdot (250 \times 10^{-15}\,\text{F}) \approx 14.97\text{ ns} \longrightarrow \mathbf{15.0\text{ ns}}$$

#### Step 5: Formulate Row Cycle Time ($t_{RC}$)
Determine total random cycle time ensuring zero residual bitline bias before consecutive row activation:
$$t_{RC} = t_{RAS} + t_{RP} = 42.0\text{ ns} + 15.0\text{ ns} = \mathbf{57.0\text{ ns}}$$

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter Code | Description | Nominal Target | Strict Acceptance Threshold | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **`AC-TIM-01`** | **Sense Amp Read Signal Margin ($\Delta V_{BL}$)** | `110.5` | $\ge 90.0$ | $\text{mV}$ | Transient SPICE at column strobe trigger |
| **`AC-TIM-02`** | **Row Precharge Time ($t_{RP}$)** | `15.0` | $\le 15.0$ (Residual offset $< 5.0$) | $\text{ns}$ ($\text{mV}$) | Time to $|\text{BL} - \overline{\text{BL}}| \le 5\text{ mV}$ post-precharge |
| **`AC-TIM-03`** | **Minimum Active Time ($t_{RAS}$)** | `42.0` | $40.0 \le t_{RAS} \le 45.0$ | $\text{ns}$ | Node restoration level $V_{node} \ge 1.78\text{ V}$ |
| **`AC-TIM-04`** | **Random Row Cycle Time ($t_{RC}$)** | `57.0` | $\le 60.0$ | $\text{ns}$ | Full write-readback cycle test at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 5. Context Citations & Traceability
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Unit cell geometry $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB); $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$; Sub-threshold & junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**: 1T1C stacked capacitor architecture ($8F^2$/$6F^2$); minimum $C_s = 25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$; gate oxide thickness $T_{ox} \approx 3.5\text{ nm}$; wordline & bitline pitch $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$; retention interval $> 64\text{ ms}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: Folded bitline $8F^2$ cell footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$); $C_b = 150\text{ to } 250\text{ fF}$ ($256 - 512$ cells/BL); capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s \in [5:1, 9:1]$ ($< 10:1$ upper boundary).

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge extracted from this formulation has been indexed in [analytical_dram_timing_derivation.md](./docs/knowledge/analytical_dram_timing_derivation.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Derivation of JEDEC timing parameters must strictly close the loop between RC parasitics (W-plug, access transistor Ron, folded bitline capacitance Cbl ≈ 200 fF, wordline RC delay) and FPGA controller state machine latency. Assuming ideal step inputs without modeling slew-rate degradation across the wordline decoder chain risks underestimating tRCD by 15-25% at 180nm process corners (SS, 1.62V, 85°C).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm with Cs = 28 fF (Ta2O5/ONO stacked crown capacitor) and Cbl = 200 fF, the sensing signal margin delta-V = (Vdd/2) * (Cs / (Cs + Cbl)) yields approximately 110 mV across the cross-coupled latch sense amplifier. Therefore, tRCD must include both wordline assert time (twl_rise ≈ 3.2 ns) and sense amplifier latch development time (tsense ≈ 8.5 ns) to avoid premature column access during destructive sensing. Furthermore, tRP must account for bitline precharge equalization through the nMOS/pMOS precharge bridge down to Vdd/2 +/- 10 mV.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Targeting 180nm open-source PDKs (such as SkyWater 130/180nm or regional foundry equivalents) requires sizing stacked capacitor EOT and access transistor W/L ratios against commercially available multi-project wafer (MPW) run rules; overconstraining tRAS to tight sub-35 ns windows will depress wafer sorting yield due to poly-gate CD variations across 200mm fabrication lines.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Analytical derivation must culminate in exact Verilog macro definitions and JEDEC cycle count constraints parameterizing the FPGA memory controller core. Theoretical RC proofs must be cross-checked against SPICE corner runs within the current sprint to avoid downstream resynthesis of the FPGA PHY timing engine.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Incomplete Bitline Precharge (tRP starvation) causing remnant differential offset on sense amplifier nodes, resulting in systematic bit flips on consecutive alternate row activations.
1. Premature Column Read/Write strobe (tRCD truncation) prior to sense amplifier latch state lock-in, causing destructive overwriting of cell storage capacitance (Cs = 28 fF) during sensing.
1. Access transistor subthreshold leakage drain during prolonged row activation (exceeding tRAS_max = 70 µs) leading to bit corruption in unselected half-selected cells along disturbed wordlines.

Monitor BL equalization node and output data valid flag over 1,000,000 continuous cycling loops. | `Zero parity/ECC errors across 10^6 consecutive cycles; command-to-command timing on logic analyzer must measure tRP >= 19.5 ns, tRAS >= 39.5 ns, and tRC >= 59.5 ns without protocol violations.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 2 Cleanroom ESD-safe anti-static lab coat, Class 100 nitrile examination gloves with static dissipative properties, ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact-resistant safety glasses, Conductive ESD heel straps with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of isopropanol inhalation, immediately move personnel to fresh ambient air; if skin contact occurs, flush thoroughly with deionized water for 15 minutes. For cryogenic/compressed nitrogen exposure, provide oxygen therapy if asphyxiation symptoms manifest and seek prompt medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Laboratory and benchtop testing must operate under active localized exhaust hoods with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) and cleanroom HEPA circulation (ISO Class 6) maintaining >= 30 air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent wipes and liquid IPA must be segregated in dedicated closed-top flammable solvent waste drums; zero drainage into municipal sewer lines. Dispose through certified hazardous waste handler according to RCRA Subtitle C.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (Electronics Cleaning Solvent)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI / Semiconductor Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Wafer/Board Purge Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 (Ultra High Purity) | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-deposition Si substrate with tungsten contact plug chemically-mechanically planarized (CMP RMS roughness < 0.3 nm), native oxide stripped via dilute HF clean.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Deposited Ta2O5/ONO stacked capacitor dielectric hermetically sealed under TiN/poly top electrode cap, preventing atmospheric moisture absorption and dielectric degradation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time before capacitor top-plate deposition causes surface carbon contamination and moisture chemisorption, increasing dielectric leakage beyond 1 fA/cell and reducing cell retention time below 64 ms.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete mathematical derivation and SPICE transient validation package establishing baseline JEDEC parameters for the 180nm open-source DRAM architecture (Cs = 28 fF, Cbl = 200 fF, VDD = 1.8V): tRP = 20 ns, tRCD = 20 ns, tRAS = 40 ns, and tRC = 60 ns, packaged for FPGA controller state machine synthesis.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_180nm_timing_derivation_report.pdf`
- [ ] `corner_simulation_transient_data.csv`
- [ ] `jedec_timing_fsm_parameters.vh`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Row Precharge Time (tRP) bitline equalization recovery window** | `20.0 ns` | +/- 2.0 ns | HSPICE transient analysis of node V_BL/V_BLB convergence to (VDD/2) within 10 mV offset. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Row to Column Delay (tRCD) minimum sensing and latch lock latency** | `20.0 ns` | +/- 1.5 ns | Transient differential voltage probe measuring >= 100 mV input before SA latch trigger across all corners. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Row Active Time (tRAS) full-cell restoration time constant** | `40.0 ns` | +/- 3.0 ns | Simulated charge replenishment measurement confirming storage capacitor restores >= 98% of full VDD rail. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Formal sign-off requires 100% test pass on Monte Carlo SPICE timing runs across SS/FF/TT corners at 85°C, complete verification of Verilog header timing macros within FPGA synthesis testbench, and unanimous approval from Council Systems and Domain Leads.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Finite State Machine (FSM) Controller RTL Implementation & Command Decoding

**Target Technology**: 180nm CMOS (Gen 2 µm) DRAM Open-Source Core  
**Node Specification**: $W/L = 220\,\text{nm} / 180\,\text{nm}$, Folded Bitline Architecture  
**Context Reference**: [docs/knowledge/fsm_controller_rtl_decoding.md](./docs/knowledge/fsm_controller_rtl_decoding.md)

---

### 1. Architectural FSM Sequence Overview

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │                      tRP Delay
│       STATE_IDLE       │◄────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│  Precharged BL=V_DD/2  │tRFC Delay
│                        │◄───────────┤                                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘            ╰────────────────────────────────────────┼─╮
             │                                                                 │ │
             ├──────────────────────────────────────────────────╮              │ │
  ACT Command│                                                  │REF Command   │ │
             ▼                                                  ▼              │ │
┌────────────────────────┐                         ┌────────────────────────┐  │ │
│  STATE_ACT WL Assert   │                         │       STATE_REF        │  │ │
│        to V_PP         │                         │      Auto-Refresh      ├──┼─╯
└────────────┬───────────┘                         └────────────────────────┘  │
             │tRCD Delay SAN SAP Latch                                         │
             ▼                                                                 │
┌────────────────────────┐                                                     │
│   STATE_ACTIVE Cell    │                                                     │
│        Restored        │◄───────────╮                                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘            │                                        │
             │                        │Burst Complete                          │
READ or WRITE│                        │                                        │
             ▼                        │                         │PRE Command   │
┌────────────────────────┐            │            ┌────────────────────────┐  │
│   STATE_BURST Column   ├────────────╯            │   STATE_PRE EQ Pulse   ├──╯
│         Access         │                         │                        │
└────────────────────────┘                         └────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Implementation Procedure

#### Step 1: RTL JEDEC Command Decoder Synthesis
1. Instantiate synchronous input sampling for active-low control bus lines: `CS_n`, `RAS_n`, `CAS_n`, `WE_n`.
2. Implement combinatorial command decoding logic:
   - **NOP**: `{CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n} = 4'b0111` (or `CS_n = 1'b1`).
   - **ACTIVE (ACT)**: `{CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n} = 4'b0011`. Latch target Bank Address (`BA[1:0]`) and Row Address (`A[11:0]`).
   - **READ**: `{CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n} = 4'b0101`. Latch Column Address (`A[9:0]`) with auto-precharge bit `A10`.
   - **WRITE**: `{CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n} = 4'b0100`. Latch Column Address and route write data to DQS/DQ buffers.
   - **PRECHARGE (PRE)**: `{CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n} = 4'b0010`. Select individual bank via `A10 = 0` or all banks via `A10 = 1`.
   - **AUTO-REFRESH (REF)**: `{CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n} = 4'b0001`. Triggers internal row refresh counter.

#### Step 2: Analog Wordline & Precharge Control Strobe Sequencing
1. **Precharge & Equalization ($EQ$)**:
   - In `STATE_IDLE`, assert active-high equalization signal $EQ$ to drive equalization NMOS gates, shorting complementary bitlines $BL$ and $/BL$ to precision $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$.
2. **Wordline Activation ($WL$)**:
   - Upon decoding **ACT**, de-assert $EQ$ to high-Z before firing wordline driver.
   - Assert wordline level shifter pulse driving gate voltage from $0\,\text{V}$ to boosted overdrive $V_{PP} = 2.6\,\text{V} - 2.8\,\text{V}$ (eliminating NMOS $V_{th}$ threshold loss during cell charge sharing).

#### Step 3: Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing Orchestration
1. **Signal Development Window**:
   - Maintain $WL$ on while $C_s \ge 28\,\text{fF}$ shares charge $Q_s = C_s \times (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$ with $C_{BL} \approx 250\,\text{fF}$, creating differential voltage $\Delta V = 100\,\text{mV} - 150\,\text{mV}$.
2. **Staggered Latch Activation**:
   - Assert N-sense amp pulldown switch $SAN$, pulling common node from $V_{DD}/2$ rapidly to $\text{GND}$ to pull the lower bitline toward $0\,\text{V}$.
   - Stagger P-sense amp pullup switch $SAP$ by exactly $1.0\,\text{ns} - 2.0\,\text{ns}$ after $SAN$, pulling common PMOS source node to $V_{DD}$ to complete charge restoration.

#### Step 4: Row Cycle ($t_{RC}$) & Auto-Refresh Timing Management
1. Constrain FSM timer counters to satisfy minimum row-to-column access delay ($t_{RCD}$), active-to-precharge delay ($t_{RAS}$), and precharge recovery time ($t_{RP}$).
2. Ensure periodic refresh intervals enforce leakage budget limits ($< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

1. **Source: Cross-Coupled Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing & Charge Restoration**:
   - $V_{BLP}$ equalization reference voltage set to $V_{DD}/2$.
   - Wordline $V_{PP}$ boosted overdrive range: $2.6\,\text{V} - 2.8\,\text{V}$ (overcoming NMOS $V_DD + V_{th}$).
   - Sense amplifier strobe delay: $SAN$ pull-down followed by $SAP$ pull-up with $1 - 2\,\text{ns}$ delay.
2. **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
   - Charge transfer formula: $Q_s = C_s \times (V_{cell} - V_{BL})$ and $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s} \times (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$.
   - Bitline capacitance $C_{BL} \approx 250\,\text{fF}$ producing $\Delta V \approx 100\,\text{mV} - 150\,\text{mV}$.
3. **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Channel dimensions: $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
   - Storage node capacitance budget: Minimum $28\,\text{fF}$ per cell (stacked capacitor over bitline).
   - Leakage threshold constraint: $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

*Documented into workspace knowledge base: [docs/knowledge/fsm_controller_rtl_decoding.md](./docs/knowledge/fsm_controller_rtl_decoding.md)*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The FSM controller must reliably bridge the asynchronous command domain from the ESP32 host via SPI/QPI with the synchronous DDR PHY clock domain running at 133-200 MHz. The design must ensure that command decoding (ACT, PRE, READ, WRITE, REF) enforces hardware interlocking on tRCD, tRP, tRAS, and tRFC without relying solely on software-level compliance, preventing bitline contention or illegal precharge transitions while sense amplifiers are active.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In folded-bitline DRAM architectures, executing an illegal READ or premature PRECHARGE prior to full charge equalization and signal development (delta V ~ 100-150 mV across 25 fF cell / 250 fF bitline) leads to catastrophic cell charge destruction and destructive readouts. The Verilog RTL state machine must integrate deterministic Gray-coded counter timers for tRCD (e.g., min 15-20 ns) and tRP (min 15-20 ns) parameter verification to guarantee robust sensing operation and margin restoration across PVT corners.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Targeting an open-source 180nm/130nm ASIC node requires synthesis compatibility with standard open-source cell libraries (e.g., SkyWater SCL) and FPGA evaluation fabrics (e.g., Lattice ECP5 / Xilinx Spartan-7). Standard cell availability, gate count constraints (<3500 equivalent gates for core FSM/decoder), and pin-count multiplexing for testbenches must be strictly managed to avoid packaging pinout escalations and wafer cost penalties.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: RTL implementation milestones require clear gate-level simulation signoff and FPGA-in-the-loop co-validation before tapeout freezing. Delay risks stem primarily from timing closure under worst-case 180nm slow-slow (1.62V, 125°C) corners and complex corner testbench coverage for auto-refresh burst scheduling during active motor-control loops.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature Precharge Activation Violation: FSM deasserts active row state prior to tRAS minimum, interrupting sense amplifier latching and permanently corrupting 1T1C capacitor state.
1. Command Bus Metatstability & Multi-Hit Decoding: Asynchronous command pulse crossing into DDR controller core clock domain causes illegal intermediate FSM state decoding (e.g., simultaneously triggering ACT and REF).
1. Auto-Refresh Starvation during Motor Loop Bursts: Host controller stalls refresh queue beyond tREFI (7.8 us maximum limit), causing bitcell voltage decay below sense amplifier differential sensing threshold.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 1 ESD-safe anti-static lab coat, Calibrated conductive wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, Powder-free cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (EN 374), ANSI Z87.1 approved impact/UV protective safety glasses
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin exposure to IPA: Flush affected skin immediately with copious clean water for 15 minutes. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately. Eye contact: Irrigate eye at eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention if irritation persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain benchtop localized laminar flow extraction hood with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) during board cleaning and solvent degreasing.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solvent and saturated lint-free wipes in dedicated grounded, airtight flammable solvent disposal cans; transfer to hazardous chemical waste repository for certified high-temperature incineration.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly synthesized FPGA prototype PCB surface with dry solder pads / unpopulated test headers, stored in desiccant dry cabinet (<10% RH).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Instrumented test bench headers soldered, cleaned of flux residues via IPA wash, dried under pure N2 blowdown, ready for probe station contact.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption causing solder joint micro-cracking and parasitic leakage under high-frequency signal probing, resulting in signal integrity degradation and false timing violation triggers.

# Standard Operating Procedure: JEDEC Protocol Compliance Verification & Transient Timing Signoff Simulation

**Document ID:** `SOP-DRAM-MET-004`  
**Classification:** Metrology & Signoff Simulation / Gen 2 (180 nm)  
**Target:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) — Circuit Design & Metrology  
**Persisted Reference:** [docs/sop_jedec_compliance_transient_timing.md](./docs/sop_jedec_compliance_transient_timing.md)

---

## 1. Transient Operational & Timing Flow

The transient timing signoff follows the standard multi-phase sense amplifier equalization, wordline boost, and regenerative sensing sequence:

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Equalization Phase:   │
│    EQ High, V_BLP =    │
│         0.90 V         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  WL Boost Transition:  │
│  V_PP = 2.6 to 2.8 V   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Charge Sharing:     │
│  Delta V_BL on C_b /   │
│          C_s           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  N-Sense Activation:   │
│       SAN to GND       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  P-Sense Activation:   │
│   SAP to V_DD, Delay   │
│         1-2 ns         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Full Restoration:    │
│  V_BL = 1.8 V or 0 V   │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

### Step 1: Netlist Generation & Array Parasitics Parameterization
1. Instantiate the folded bitline memory array ($8F^2$ footprint, cell area $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at feature size $F = 180\text{ nm}$).
2. Configure discrete access transistor geometry to target sub-micron dimensions:
   $$\frac{W}{L} = \frac{2.0\ \mu\text{m}}{0.18\ \mu\text{m}}$$
3. Set the cell storage capacitance $C_s$ to its nominal value of $28\text{ fF}$ (guaranteeing $\ge 25\text{ fF}$).
4. Model bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b$ for a $256$ or $512$ cell folded bitline column within the range of $150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$, enforcing a capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ strictly between $5:1$ and $9:1$.

### Step 2: Static Device Bias & Pre-Charge Initialization (Phase 1)
1. Initialize array supply rail $V_{DD} = 1.8\text{ V}$ and set the bitline precharge reference:
   $$V_{BLP} = \frac{V_{DD}}{2} = 0.90\text{ V}$$
2. Assert equalization signal (`EQ` high) to short complementary bitlines ($BL$ and $\overline{BL}$) to $V_{BLP}$.
3. Verify that access transistor static subthreshold parameters align with physical device limits: NMOS $V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$, $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$, and $I_{on} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$ ($I_{on}/I_{off} > 10^7$).

### Step 3: Wordline Boost & Charge Sharing (Phase 2)
1. Deassert equalization (`EQ` to $0\text{ V}$).
2. Pulse the selected Wordline ($WL$) from $0\text{ V}$ up to boosted supply:
   $$V_{PP} = 2.6\text{ V to } 2.8\text{ V}$$
   *(Ensures gate overdrive $V_{DD} + V_{th}$ without access threshold drop).*
3. Execute transient simulation across the charge sharing window and verify the differential voltage development ($\Delta V_{BL}$) across $BL$ and $\overline{BL}$ prior to sense activation.

### Step 4: Strobe N-Sense & P-Sense Activation (Phases 3 & 4)
1. Pull the common sense amplifier node $SAN$ rapidly from $V_{DD}/2$ ($0.90\text{ V}$) to $\text{GND}$ via the NMOS pulldown switch.
2. Introduce a calibrated strobe delay of $1\text{ ns to } 2\text{ ns}$ between $SAN$ firing and $SAP$ firing.
3. Pull the cross-coupled PMOS source node $SAP$ to $V_{DD}$ ($1.8\text{ V}$) via the PMOS pullup switch.
4. Record transient waveforms until $BL$ and $\overline{BL}$ achieve full digital rail separation ($1.8\text{ V}$ and $0\text{ V}$).

---

## 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter ID | Parameter Description | Minimum Target | Nominal Target | Maximum Target | Physical Unit |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-01** | Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$) | $25.0$ | $28.0$ | $30.0$ | $\text{fF}$ |
| **AC-02** | Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$) | $5.0 : 1$ | — | $9.0 : 1$ (fails at $> 10:1$) | Dimensionless |
| **AC-03** | Boosted Wordline Voltage ($V_{PP}$) | $2.6$ | $2.7$ | $2.8$ | $\text{V}$ |
| **AC-04** | Sense Amp $SAN$-to-$SAP$ Activation Delay | $1.0$ | $1.5$ | $2.0$ | $\text{ns}$ |

---

## 5. Verified Source Citations

1. **Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**:
   - Sub-micron geometry: $W / L = 2.0\ \mu\text{m} / 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$.
   - Linear threshold voltage: $V_{thn} = +0.55\text{ V} \pm 50\text{ mV}$ at $V_{DS} = 50\text{ mV}$.
   - Current limits: $I_{on} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ (at $V_{GS} = 1.8\text{ V}$); $I_{off} \le 10\text{ pA}/\mu\text{m}$ (at $V_{GS} = 0\text{ V}$); $I_{on}/I_{off} > 10^7$.
2. **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**:
   - Folded bitline footprint: $8F^2$ ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$).
   - Capacitance targets: $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF to } 30\text{ fF}$ (nominal $28\text{ fF}$); $C_b = 150\text{ fF to } 250\text{ fF}$; $C_b / C_s = 5 : 1 \text{ to } 9 : 1$ ($> 10 : 1$ degrades margin severely).
3. **Cross-Coupled Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing & Charge Restoration**:
   - Precharge reference: $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$.
   - Boosted Wordline: $V_{PP} = 2.6\text{ V to } 2.8\text{ V}$ ($V_{DD} + V_{th}$).
   - Regenerative timing: $SAN$ pulled to $\text{GND}$, followed by $SAP$ pulled to $V_{DD}$ after $1\text{ to } 2\text{ ns}$ delay.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transient timing signoff between the FPGA soft DDR PHY and the 180nm custom DRAM silicon must incorporate board trace parasitics (interconnect RLC) and bond-wire inductance (L_wire ~ 1.5 nH to 3.0 nH). Validating JEDEC compliance purely in an idealized RTL simulator will create severe clock-to-data-strobe (DQS-to-CK) skew and false positive timing closures, blinding downstream bring-up to real-world ground bounce and setup/hold violations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node (Gen 2 target), discrete MOS transistor driving capability (I_on >= 500 uA/um, V_thn = 0.55V) limits internal DRAM sense amplifier latch speeds and array wordline boost dynamics. JEDEC parameters such as tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay) and tRP (Row Precharge time) cannot be treated as fixed synchronous cycles; they must be verified via mixed-signal SPICE co-simulation under worst-case PVT corners (Slow-Slow, 1.62V, 85°C) to prevent catastrophic mid-burst read corruptions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Characterizing sub-micron physical DRAM dies against JEDEC standards requires high-bandwidth digital mixed-signal instrumentation (minimum 2.5 GHz / 10 GSa/s real-time oscilloscope or Keysight DDR protocol analyzer) with active low-capacitance differential probes (<0.4 pF). These probes are single-source, highly fragile, and cost-prohibitive for garage setups; lack of specialized interposers will delay physical validation signoff by 6-8 weeks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Simulation signoff must strictly gate tapeout and mask lithography. Without automated test-bench regression producing deterministic binary pass/fail logs across all 18 JEDEC SDR/DDR-1 timing intervals (tRAS, tRC, tRRD, tRFC, etc.), the project risks committing silicon to physical wafers with undetected finite state machine lockups during auto-refresh bursts.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. FSM deadlock during concurrent Auto-Refresh (tRFC) and Precharge (tRP) arbitration under asynchronous refresh timer expiration.
1. Read data corruption caused by DQS-DQ setup/hold timing margin collapse due to unmodeled pad capacitance (C_pad > 3.5 pF) and package bond-wire inductance.
1. Sense-amplifier latch failure due to premature column access when tRCD is under-margined across high-temperature slow process corners.

Introduce pseudo-random timing jitter on external bus clocks (CK/CK#) up to +/-200 ps and measure FSM state transitions. 5. | `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-1-3-02` | **Transient DQ/DQS Timing Signoff & Eye-Diagram Simulation** | Synopsys PrimeSim / Cadence Spectre SPICE transient simulator configured with IBIS 180nm I/O buffer models and distributed RLC transmission line PCB trace netlists. | 1. Set up transient SPICE simulation running at 133 MHz DDR (266 MT/s) target frequency over 5 us duration. 2. ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD-safe lab coat, ESD grounding wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, Safety glasses (ANSI Z87.1 approved) for physical workbench debugging
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with cleaning solvent (IPA), flush affected areas with clean water for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics lab HVAC with local benchtop extraction fan (minimum 50 CFM) during solvent-based probe and PCB contact cleaning.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent cleaning solvent wipes in designated sealed, fireproof hazardous waste bins for chemical solvent disposal in accordance with local environmental regulations.

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Verilog RTL State Machine Implementation of Command & Refresh Sequencer

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The FSM must handle clock domain crossing (CDC) between the ESP32 SPI/parallel interface (50 MHz) and the FPGA DDR PHY command domain (133-166 MHz) using asynchronous Gray-code FIFOs. Lack of deterministic latency in JEDEC tRFC and tREFI counters will violate the refresh window, leading to data corruption across sense amplifier latch cycles during motor controller closed-loop bursts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DRAM cells at 180nm exhibit Cs ~ 25 fF and CBL ~ 250 fF, producing a sensing delta V of only 100-150 mV. The sequencer must strictly enforce tRP (precharge-to-activate) and tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay) down to integer clock cycles (e.g., minimum 18 ns tRP = 3 cycles at 166 MHz). Any race condition asserting CAS before sense amplifier latch stabilization (SAN/SAP) directly corrupts the 1T1C storage capacitor charge.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Targeting standard open-source toolchains (Yosys/nextpnr for Gowin/Lattice FPGA, or OpenROAD for 180nm ASIC shuttle runs) requires avoiding proprietary IP primitives. RTL must use fully synthesizable, inferrable dual-port BRAMs and standard cell flip-flops to ensure multi-foundry portable fabrication without vendor lock-in.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable must strictly decouple the command queue from the auto-refresh priority arbiter. Schedule milestone signoff requires bit-accurate simulation passing 100,000 continuous randomized read/write/refresh cycles without deadlocking before handoff to OpenROAD physical synthesis.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Refresh starvation deadlock: Command queue bursts blocking auto-refresh issuance beyond maximum allowable tREFI (7.8 us), triggering capacitive cell charge decay below the 100 mV sense amp threshold.
1. tRP timing violation: Issuing ACTIVATE prior to complete bitline equalization to VDD/2, inducing sense amplifier latch failure and destructive read of adjacent bitline pairs.
1. CDC glitching during burst abort: Unsynchronized state transition flags between ESP32 write bursts and FPGA memory sequencer resulting in illegal JEDEC command encoding (e.g., simultaneous RAS_N=0, CAS_N=0, WE_N=0 invalid entry).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-2-01` | **JEDEC Auto-Refresh Interval (tREFI) and Recovery (tRFC) Protocol Validation** | Synopsys VCS / Icarus Verilog digital simulation with JEDEC DDR memory verification model and ModelSim waveform assertion checker measuring cycle-accurate bus timings. | 1. Saturate the command sequencer FIFO with back-to-back continuous burst write commands from the ESP32 interface model for 50 us. 2. Observe the auto-refresh arbitration logic when the tREFI interval timer expires. 3. Verify that ongoing burst transactions terminate or yield according to JEDEC spec and that the AUTO_REFRESH command (RAS_N=0, CAS_N=0, WE_N=1, CS_N=0) is asserted within the allowed margin. 4. Measure the elapsed clock cycles between AUTO_REFRESH assertion and the subsequent ACTIVATE or PRECHARGE command to verify tRFC recovery delay. | `AUTO_REFRESH command must be issued within <= 8 cumulative tREFI intervals (maximum tREFI postponement limit per JEDEC standard); tRFC must strictly equal or exceed 12 clock cycles (72.0 ns); zero read/write command contention on SDRAM control lines (RAS_N, CAS_N, WE_N).` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-2-02` | **tRP and tRCD Timing Constraint Verification Under Random Read/Write Bank Switching** | FPGA Mixed-Signal Logic Analyzer / Cocotb Python-based regression environment with cycle-exact scoreboard monitoring bank state transition markers. | 1. Inject a randomized sequence of 10,000 Read and Write transactions alternating across all 4 logical memory banks. 2. Force back-to-back PRECHARGE (PRE) followed immediately by ACTIVATE (ACT) to the same bank. 3. Force ACTIVATE (ACT) followed immediately by READ or WRITE to the same row/column. 4. Log cycle deltas between PRE-to-ACT and ACT-to-READ/WRITE across all banks. | `Measured PRE-to-ACT cycle delta >= 3 clock cycles across 100% of iterations (zero tRP violations); measured ACT-to-READ/WRITE cycle delta >= 3 clock cycles across 100% of iterations (zero tRCD violations); scoreboard reports 0 data mismatches.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 1 ESD-safe conductive wrist strap (1 Mohm series resistor), ANSI Z87.1 certified clear safety glasses, Class 1000 cleanroom-compatible anti-static nitrile gloves
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA, flush thoroughly with clean water for 15 minutes. In case of vapor inhalation causing dizziness, move personnel immediately to fresh air. In case of eye splash, flush eyes at emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open and seek medical evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics lab benchtop localized fume extraction hood (minimum face velocity 100 FPM) operating during board-level cleaning and soldering rework.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent isopropyl alcohol in dedicated hazardous chemical solvent waste containers clearly labeled 'Flammable Liquid - Spent Solvent'; dispose of via licensed hazardous waste management protocols; zero drain disposal.
