| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Benchtop Cleaning / PCB Defluxing)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-received fabricated PCB/carrier substrate with immersion gold (ENIG) finish, verified free of copper oxidation and ionic flux residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Assembled FPGA/DRAM test bench module vacuum-sealed in moisture-barrier anti-static bags with relative humidity indicator < 10% RH.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into plastic quad-flat packages (PQFP/QFN) leading to popcorn cracking and wire-bond shear failure during prototype reflow soldering.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Synthesizable Verilog RTL implementation of the JEDEC Command and Auto-Refresh Sequencer with deterministic tRP/tRCD/tRFC timing compliance, verified via cycle-accurate testbenches, FPGA timing signoff, and formal assertion checking.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Auto-refresh issuance latency jitter relative to JEDEC tREFI target** | `0.0` | +/- 2 clock cycles | Post-synthesis gate-level simulation with ModelSim/VCS assertion waveform capture |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero setup and hold timing violations across all PVT corners in OpenSTA; 100% branch and statement code coverage in digital regression testbench; zero data integrity corruption across 1,000,000 simulated DRAM transactions under JEDEC compliance checker.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## JEDEC Timing Counter & FSM Architecture RTL Encoding

- **Domain**: DRAM Foundation VN — Circuit Design & Digital Logic Core
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (180nm CMOS)
- **Target File / Documentation**: [`sop_jedec_timing_counter_fsm_rtl.md`](./docs/sop_jedec_timing_counter_fsm_rtl.md)
- **Action Type**: Make

---

### FSM Architecture & Sequencing Diagram
```text
┌────────────────────┐
│                    │◄──────╮
│  PRECHARGE / IDLE  │               tRFC Met
│                    │◄──────┼───────────────────────────────┤
└──────────┬─────────┘       │                               │
           │                 │                               │
           │                 │                               │
           ├─────────────────┼──────────────────╮            │
           │                 │                  │            │
           │                 │                  │REF Command │
ACT Command│                 │                  │            │
           │                 │                  │            │
           ▼                 │                  ▼            │
┌────────────────────┐       │       ┌────────────────────┐  │
│                    │       │       │                    │  │
│     ACTIVATING     │       │       │    AUTO_REFRESH    ├──╯
│                    │       │tRAS Me│ & PRE              │
└──────────┬─────────┘       │       └────────────────────┘
           │                 │
   tRCD Met│                 │
           ▼                 │
┌────────────────────┐       │
│                    │       │
│      ROW_OPEN      │       │
│                    │       │
└──────────┬─────────┘       │
           │                 │
           │RD/WR Command    │
           ▼                 │
┌────────────────────┐       │
│                    │       │
│    BURST_TRANS     ├───────╯
│                    │
└────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **State Machine Encoding & Architecture Definition**:
   - Encode the high-speed controller using One-Hot or Gray state encoding (`STATE_IDLE`, `STATE_ACTIVATE`, `STATE_ROW_OPEN`, `STATE_READ`, `STATE_WRITE`, `STATE_PRECHARGE`, `STATE_REFRESH`) to minimize glitch transitions and timing overhead at the FPGA/ASIC boundary.
   - Constrain the command sequencer pipeline so that no internal state advancement occurs until dedicated physical countdown counters expire.

2. **JEDEC Timing Parameter Register & Counter Calculation**:
   - Initialize fixed-point countdown registers parameterized by system clock frequency ($t_{CK}$):
     - **Row-to-Column Delay Counter ($t_{RCD}$)**: Calculate countdown cycles matching cell charge sharing and differential development. Charge redistribution over bitline capacitance $C_{BL} = 250\,\text{fF}$ with cell capacitance $C_s \ge 28\,\text{fF}$ develops a differential signal $\Delta V = 100\,\text{mV} - 150\,\text{mV}$. Ensure $t_{RCD}$ permits complete sense amplifier firing (N-sense $SAN \rightarrow 0\,\text{V}$ followed by P-sense $SAP \rightarrow V_{DD}$ after $1\,\text{ns} - 2\,\text{ns}$ delay).
     - **Row Active Time Counter ($t_{RAS}$)**: Establish min duration for wordline overdrive $V_{PP} = 2.6\,\text{V} - 2.8\,\text{V}$ across access transistor gate ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$) ensuring full cell charge restoration back to $V_{DD}$.
     - **Row Precharge Time Counter ($t_{RP}$)**: Set counter to guarantee bitline equalization switch assertion, stabilizing complementary lines back to $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$.

3. **Auto-Refresh Sequencer ($t_{REFI}$ / $t_{RFC}$) Timing Implementation**:
   - Structure a free-running tick generator for the refresh interval $t_{REFI}$, calibrated against the worst-case cell retention leakage limit ($< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Implement an auto-refresh execution sub-state asserting all-bank precharge and holding active wordline restore states for the duration of $t_{RFC}$ before returning to `STATE_IDLE`.

4. **Verilog RTL Verification & Glitch/Race Condition Immunity**:
   - Enforce synchronous reset and register all command outputs (`cs_n`, `ras_n`, `cas_n`, `we_n`) directly from flip-flop stages without combinatorial logic gates in the output path.
   - Verify zero setup/hold timing violations on memory bus turnarounds.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                     Verified 180nm Physical Parameters 
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░                                │
Sense Delay (SAN-SAP)┤░                                │
                     │▒                                │
    WL Overdrive V_PP┤▒                                │
     C_bitline (C_BL)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
         C_cell (C_s)┤█████                            │
                     │█████                            │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                     0.0    62.5    125.0   187.5 250.0 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Value / Range | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bitline Charge-Share Delta ($\Delta V$)** | $100$ to $150$ | $\text{mV}$ | Simulated differential bitline read signal ($C_s \ge 28\,\text{fF}, C_{BL} = 250\,\text{fF}$) |
| **Wordline Overdrive Voltage ($V_{PP}$)** | $2.6$ to $2.8$ | $\text{V}$ | Gate bias level verified on access NMOS ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$) |
| **Sense Amp P-to-N Activation Delay ($t_{SAP\_DLY}$)** | $1.0$ to $2.0$ | $\text{ns}$ | Analog delay timing margin between $SAN$ pulldown and $SAP$ pullup |
| **Max Cell Storage Leakage ($I_{leak}$ @ $85^\circ\text{C}$)** | $< 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Static cell junction & sub-threshold retention ceiling |

---

### 3. Literature Citations
- **Source 1**: *Cross-Coupled Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing & Charge Restoration* — Equalization to $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$; boosted wordline $V_{PP} = 2.6\,\text{V} - 2.8\,\text{V}$; $SAN$ pulldown followed by $SAP$ pullup with $1\,\text{ns} - 2\,\text{ns}$ delay.
- **Source 2**: *Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout* — Differential signal equation $\Delta V = \frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s} (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$ with $C_s = 25\,\text{fF} - 28\,\text{fF}$, $C_{BL} = 250\,\text{fF}$, yielding $\Delta V = 100\,\text{mV} - 150\,\text{mV}$.
- **Source 3**: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench* — 180nm cell dimensions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$), minimum storage capacitance $C_s \ge 28\,\text{fF}$, stacked capacitor dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$, and leakage target $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The RTL state machine orchestrates both the JEDEC protocol commands and the underlying 180nm analog core timings (tRP, tRCD, tRAS, tRC, and tREFI). Given the 28 fF cell capacitance and <1 fA sub-threshold leakage budget, any clock-domain jitter or skew between the FPGA controller core and the ESP32 SPI/parallel management bridge risks violating charge-restoration margins. The counters must be hard-coded with parameterized cycle registers that dynamically scale across varying FPGA fabric operating frequencies (e.g., 50 MHz to 133 MHz) rather than fixed counter delays, ensuring deterministic precharge and bitline equilibration guarantees before any successive activate command is issued.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm COB architecture, sensing relies on a multi-phase charge redistribution where V_PP overdrive (2.6V-2.8V) turns on the NMOS access transistor, followed by SAN pull-down and SAP pull-up with 1-2 ns differential gating. The RTL FSM must enforce strict tRAS minimum dwell times to ensure full logic '1' restoration back into the stacked MIM capacitor through the high-resistance W-plug contact. Truncating tRAS via early AUTO-PRECHARGE in the command sequencer will permanently attenuate stored charge margins, accelerating retention failure well ahead of the specified 64 ms / 4096-cycle refresh window at 85°C.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing this open-source controller core on accessible FPGA fabrics (such as Gowin GW1N/GW2A, Lattice ECP5, or Xilinx Spartan-6/7) requires minimizing specialized hard IP dependencies. Utilizing standard synthesizable Verilog-2001 constructs for Gray-code counters and one-hot FSM encoding ensures compatibility with multiple vendor toolchains (Yosys/nextpnr, Gowin EDA, and Vivado), mitigating supply constraints on single-source FPGA hardware for the open-source DRAM development kit.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable must strictly isolate the synthesis-ready RTL FSM and timing counters from testbench harnesses to maintain clear traceability to the Gen 2 tape-out milestone. Delays in standardizing the parameter interfaces for tRCD, tRP, and tRFC will bottleneck firmware development for the closed-loop motor controller host interface, risking verification slip for the integrated 180nm silicon bring-up.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature Precharge Execution (tRAS violation): FSM transitions from ACTIVE to PRECHARGE before full bitline sense-amplifier rail restoration, causing retention degradation and soft-bit corruption in stacked capacitors below 28 fF.
1. Refresh Starvation under Continuous Bus Bursts: Refresh sequencer counter rollover failure or priority arbitration deadlock during prolonged write bursts, exceeding the 15.625 µs average refresh interval (tREFI) at 85°C.
1. Glitched Command Strobe Generation: Asynchronous decoding of multi-bit counter comparator outputs causing illegal sub-cycle command pulses (e.g., runt CS_N/RAS_N/CAS_N/WE_N assertions) violating DRAM setup/hold times (tIS/tIH).

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified ESD-safe anti-glare safety glasses, ESD wrist strap with 1 Megohm current-limiting safety resistor, Static-dissipative cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100 / ISO 5 compatible)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water. Eye contact: Flush eyes with sterile eyewash solution or isotonic water for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Move individual to well-ventilated fresh air. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; contact medical services immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics lab bench laminar flow hood / localized ESD-safe HEPA ventilation with minimum 50 FPM face velocity for solvent wiping and heat dissipation from FPGA development rigs.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be disposed of in dedicated, airtight, FM-approved flammable waste containers grounded against electrostatic discharge, routed to licensed hazardous waste disposal.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry-pack sealed FPGA development carrier PCB and socketed test interposer, stored in moisture barrier bag (MBB) with desiccant at < 10% relative humidity; gold/immersion-silver contacts free of oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Programmed, bitstream-verified FPGA core running in ambient dry nitrogen chamber or ESD-safe desiccator cabinet ready for physical 180nm analog test-chip interface validation.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric moisture absorption into exposed carrier boards causing solder joint micro-cracking during thermal characterization, and galvanic contact oxidation inducing parasitic impedance/skew on high-speed PHY interface traces exceeding the 500 ps timing budget.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Auto-Refresh Sequencer & Collision Arbiter Implementation

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > FPGA High-Speed DRAM Memory Controller Core (Verilog DDR PHY & JEDEC State Machine) [Digital Logic & FPGA] > JEDEC Timing & Refresh Protocol State Machine Architecture Modeling [Circuit Design] > Verilog RTL State Machine Implementation of Command & Refresh Sequencer [Circuit Design] > Auto-Refresh Sequencer & Collision Arbiter Implementation [Circuit Design]
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Wirebond Shear >= 18 gf, ATE Functional Yield >= 90%, Coplanarity <= 0.08 mm.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Dage 4000 Bond Tester & Advantest Wafer Prober / CMM.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Arbitrating between host memory access requests from the ESP32 closed-loop motor controller and periodic JEDEC auto-refresh commands introduces non-deterministic latency jitter into the motor commutation loop. At a 180nm node operating with a 100MHz DDR PHY clock (10ns period), a stalled ACTIVATE/READ command due to an in-flight tRFC (refresh cycle time >= 60ns to 75ns) can breach the hard real-time 100us torque-control deadline if backpressure queues overflow. The arbiter must implement an urgency-tier priority scheme where pending refreshes can accumulate up to the JEDEC maximum of 8 postponed cycles before forcing a bus stall.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: The 180nm folded bitline architecture yields a modest delta V of 100mV to 150mV across a 25fF storage cell and 250fF bitline parasitic capacitance. At elevated junction temperatures (T_j = 85°C), junction leakage current (I_leak > 1pA) degrades retention time below 64ms across the 4096-row array, requiring strict 15.6us distributed refresh intervals (tREFI). If the collision arbiter prioritizes host transactions too aggressively, row charge drains below the sensing margin (SAN/SAP latch failure), resulting in irreversible soft bit flips. The auto-refresh sequencer counter must be strictly monotonically locked to the master clock divider.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing this RTL core on COTS FPGA targets (such as Lattice iCE40UP5K or Xilinx Spartan-7/Artix-7) for physical hardware-in-the-loop validation of the custom 180nm DRAM test vehicle requires careful pinout budgeting and standard LVCMOS 1.8V/3.3V IO compliance. Sourcing low-jitter SMD TCXO oscillators (+/- 10 ppm) and matched high-speed impedance test fixtures in the local Vietnam supply ecosystem is critical to prevent clock drift from de-synchronizing the auto-refresh interval across temperature swings.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The auto-refresh sequencer and collision arbiter deliverable directly gates physical tape-out simulation sign-off and FPGA co-emulation milestones. Delivery delays in the Verilog state machine or formal proof of mutual exclusion will push the planned multi-project wafer (MPW) shuttle tapeout window. Verification must be closed via automated SystemVerilog testbenches with 100% toggle and branch coverage before proceeding to layout synthesis.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Metastable arbitration state during simultaneous arrival of host ACTIVATE and internal tREFI tick, causing runt command pulses on the DRAM command bus (CS_N, RAS_N, CAS_N, WE_N).
1. Starvation of DRAM refresh cycles during continuous burst read/write traffic from the motor controller, exceeding maximum retention time (tRET > 64ms) and causing silent array data corruption.
1. Race condition in tRFC timer reset logic causing premature wordline re-assertion while bitline equalization and sense amplifier restoration are still active, resulting in collapsed bitline differential voltages.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-2-2-01` | **Hardware Collision Arbitration & Mutual Exclusion Stress Test** | Tektronix MSO64 4-Channel 2.5GHz Mixed Signal Oscilloscope, Keysight 16860A Portable Logic Analyzer, Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA Development Board (XC7A35T-1FTG256C), Rigol DG4162 Arbitrary Waveform Generator. | 1. Connect logic analyzer probes to DRAM command lines (CS_N, RAS_N, CAS_N, WE_N, CKE) and host handshake signals (HOST_REQ, HOST_ACK, REFRESH_PENDING, BUSY). 2. Configure the waveform generator to inject 10,000,000 randomized pseudo-asynchronous host read/write request pulses with edge arrival times uniformly sweeping across -5.0ns to +5.0ns relative to the internal 15.6us tREFI refresh trigger edge. 3. Capture all command transitions over a continuous 1-hour run using logic analyzer hardware protocol violation triggers. 4. Measure the minimum temporal separation between the completion of any AUTO-REFRESH cycle (tRFC) and the subsequent host ACTIVATE command edge across all captured traces. | `Zero occurrences of simultaneous assertion of Refresh and Host Activate commands (protocol collision count = 0). Minimum separation between Refresh command and subsequent row activation must be >= 70.0ns (tRFC). No metastable glitches or runt pulses (pulse width < 4.8ns) detected on any DRAM control line across 10,000,000 randomized injection events.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-2-2-02` | **JEDEC Distributed Refresh Cadence & Postponement Boundary Verification** | Keysight 53230A 350MHz Universal Frequency Counter/Timer, Keysight 16860A Portable Logic Analyzer, High-Precision Digital Multimeter (Keysight 34465A). | 1. Program the host traffic generator to saturate memory bandwidth with continuous back-to-back sequential burst writes for a continuous 128ms period. 2. Configure the timer/counter to log the arrival timestamp of every AUTO_REFRESH command asserted on the command bus. 3. Measure the maximum number of consecutively postponed refresh cycles buffered by the arbiter before an emergency forced refresh preempts the host bus. 4. Compute the cumulative refresh count over a sliding 64.0ms window and calculate the average refresh interval. | `The arbiter must strictly limit postponed refreshes to <= 8 cycles before forcing preemption. The total number of refresh commands executed within any sliding 64.0ms window must be exactly 4096 cycles (+/- 0 cycles). Mean tREFI across the entire window must evaluate to 15.625us +/- 0.05us.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Electrostatic discharge (ESD) wrist strap with 1 Megohm series resistor, Class 100 cleanroom compatible anti-static nitrile gloves (4 mil)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of tempered water at the eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. Skin contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and water. Inhalation of soldering flux vapors or IPA: Remove victim to fresh air immediately; provide supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Thermal burns from soldering iron: Immerse burn in cold running water for a minimum of 10 minutes; do not apply ointments; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop electronic testing and prototype rework must be conducted under localized ESD-safe snorkel exhaust arms with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) or inside a laminar flow hood ducting through HEPA and activated carbon filtration.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA wipes and cleaning swabs must be segregated into closed, airtight, grounded flammables disposal containers labeled for hazardous solvent incineration. Solder dross and wire remnants must be collected in dedicated rigid containers for heavy metal recycling; do not discard into standard sanitary municipal streams.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.8% w/w` |
| **Lead-Free Solder Alloy (Sn96.5/Ag3.0/Cu0.5 - SAC305)** | `7440-31-5` | Electronics Assembly Grade | `96.5% Sn, 3.0% Ag, 0.5% Cu` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly fabricated PCB / FPGA test carrier coupon with Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold (ENIG) surface finish, free of organic ionic residue, packaged in sealed moisture barrier bags (MBB) with desiccant.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Cleaned, post-solder flux-free assembly surface with ionic contamination < 0.75 ug/cm2 NaCl equivalent, verified via ROSE testing, with zero copper oxidation on high-speed traces.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric moisture absorption and airborne sulfur/chloride contamination lead to intermetallic compound degradation (black pad embrittlement), contact oxidation on high-frequency PMOD/SMA connectors, causing signal integrity degradation, high-frequency reflections, and false collision triggers during FPGA-to-DRAM 100MHz PHY characterization.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Synthesized, verified, and physically validated RTL implementation of the JEDEC Auto-Refresh Sequencer and Collision Arbiter Core in synthesizable Verilog HDL, targeted to both FPGA prototype hardware and 180nm ASIC standard cell libraries. The design guarantees strictly bounded refresh latency, zero-glitch arbitration under heavy asynchronous bus traffic, and 100% adherence to JEDEC tREFI and tRFC timing constraints.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_refresh_arbiter_core.v`
- [ ] `collision_arbitration_stress_report.csv`
- [ ] `phy_arbiter_timing_signoff.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum collision arbiter grant latency for an incoming host read/write access when no refresh is in progress** | `10.0 ns` | +/- 1.0 ns | Post-synthesis gate-level timing simulation with SDF back-annotation at 100MHz clock and logic analyzer trace capture on FPGA. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Auto-refresh command duration guarantee (tRFC) during which host accesses are strictly isolated and queued** | `70.0 ns` | +0.0 / -0.0 ns | Constrained-random SystemVerilog assertion-based verification (SVA) run over 10^8 clock cycles and real-time digital storage oscilloscope trigger monitoring. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Postponed refresh buffer ceiling before triggering mandatory non-maskable bus takeover** | `8 cycles` | +0 / -0 cycles | Hardware logic analyzer state trace inspection during continuous bus saturation stress test. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher sign-off requires 100% functional and line coverage on RTL testbench suites, zero setup/hold timing violations at 100MHz under worst-case 180nm process corners (SS / 1.62V / 125°C), zero command bus protocol collisions across 10,000,000 asynchronous injection cycles on the physical FPGA test platform, and formal property verification (FPV) mathematical proof of mutual exclusion between refresh and host commands.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-DES-180-044`
**Title:** RTL Testbench Verification & OpenROAD Synthesis Timing Audit  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > Circuit Design > Verilog RTL State Machine Implementation of Command & Refresh Sequencer > RTL Testbench Verification & OpenROAD Synthesis Timing Audit  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Objective & Scope
This SOP defines the formal verification and physical synthesis static timing audit flow for the DRAM Command & Refresh Sequencer RTL module targeted at the 180nm process node using the OpenROAD-flow-scripts (ORFS) autonomous RTL-to-GDSII infrastructure.

---

### 2. Required Tooling & Input Files
- **Logic Simulator:** Icarus Verilog (`iverilog`) / Verilator with GTKWave for functional simulation.
- **Synthesis & Place-and-Route Engine:** OpenROAD toolflow (`OpenROAD-flow-scripts / ORFS`).
- **Timing Signoff Engine:** OpenSTA (integrated within OpenROAD).
- **Parasitic Extraction:** OpenRCX.
- **Design Inputs:**
  - Synthesizable RTL: `dram_cmd_refresh_sequencer.v`
  - Verification Testbench: `tb_dram_cmd_refresh_sequencer.v`
  - Design Constraints: `constraints.sdc`
  - Process Technology Files: 180nm Liberty standard cell timing models (`.lib`), LEF (`.lef`), and technology rules.

---

### 3. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```
                     RTL & TESTBENCH VERIFICATION & TIMING AUDIT FLOW
                                      (OpenROAD / ORFS)
 
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | 1. Functional Verification (Icarus Verilog / Verilator)                               |
 |    - Run self-checking testbench tb_dram_cmd_refresh_sequencer.v                      |
 |    - Validate JEDEC Command & Refresh sequencing (tRAS, tRP, tRFC, refresh cycle)     |
 +-------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
                                             |
                                             v
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | 2. Synthesis & Floorplan Initialization                                               |
 |    - Synthesize standard cell netlist with Yosys/OpenROAD                             |
 |    - Initialize floorplan, die/core boundaries, core utilization                      |
 |    - Insert tap cells, well ties, and generate Power Distribution Network (PDN)       |
 +-------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
                                             |
                                             v
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | 3. Global & Detailed Placement with Early Timing Analysis                             |
 |    - Execute global standard cell placement & macro placement                         |
 |    - Placement repair & optimization: resolve max slew, max capacitance, max fanout   |
 |    - Detailed placement legalizing cells to standard cell row grid                     |
 |    - Perform incremental static timing analysis (STA)                                 |
 +-------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
                                             |
                                             v
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | 4. Clock Tree Synthesis (CTS) & Setup/Hold Optimization                               |
 |    - Insert balance buffers and resize high-fanout nets along clock distribution tree |
 |    - Run setup & hold timing optimization and repair hold slack violations            |
 +-------------------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
                                             |
                                             v
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
 | 5. Global/Detailed Routing & Parasitic Extraction (OpenRCX)                           |
 |    - Global routing guide generation & antenna violation repair                       |
 |    - Detailed routing to legalize routes and enforce DRC-correct wiring               |
 |    - SPEF extraction via OpenRCX engine & signoff static timing audit via OpenSTA     |
 +---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: RTL Simulation & JEDEC State Sequence Validation
1. Compile RTL and self-checking testbench:
   ```bash
   iverilog -g2012 -o sim_seq tb_dram_cmd_refresh_sequencer.v dram_cmd_refresh_sequencer.v
   vvp sim_seq
   ```
2. Verify all standard JEDEC command transitions (Precharge-to-Activate `tRP`, Active-to-Precharge `tRAS`, Auto-Refresh `tRFC`).
3. Assert that the refresh sequencer initiates periodic distributed refresh commands within the target timing budget without starvation.

#### Step 2: Synthesis & Floorplan Setup in OpenROAD
1. Configure `config.mk` for the 180nm standard cell target library and set `SDC_FILE = constraints.sdc`.
2. Run logic synthesis via ORFS to translate RTL state machine logic into targeted standard cells.
3. Perform floorplan initialization:
   - Define chip core utilization and core-to-IO boundary spacing.
   - Insert well-tie and substrate tap cells.
   - Synthesize the Power Distribution Network (PDN) straps and rails.

#### Step 3: Global Placement, Optimization & Detailed Legalization
1. Run global placement for all sequencer standard cell instances.
2. Run automatic placement optimization in OpenROAD to repair max capacitance, max slew, and high-fanout nets.
3. Legalize standard cell placement onto cell row grids during detailed placement.
4. Execute incremental STA to monitor early worst negative slack (WNS).

#### Step 4: Clock Tree Synthesis (CTS) & Hold Timing Repair
1. Execute CTS in OpenROAD: buffer insertion and driver sizing to minimize clock skew across state registers and refresh counters.
2. Run setup and hold timing repair commands:
   ```tcl
   repair_clock_inverters
   repair_timing -setup
   repair_timing -hold
   ```

#### Step 5: Global/Detailed Routing, OpenRCX Parasitic Extraction & Timing Signoff
1. Generate global routing guides and check for routing congestion.
2. Apply antenna rule repair buffers where long metal runs are identified.
3. Complete detailed routing with zero DRC violations.
4. Extract parasitic RC networks using `OpenRCX`.
5. Run final OpenSTA timing audit across Min/Max process corners to generate timing signoff reports (`worst_slack`, `total_negative_slack`).

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Identifier | Parameter Description | Signoff Target | Physical Unit | Evaluation Tool / Engine |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-TIM-01** | Worst Negative Slack (WNS) - Setup Timing | $\ge 0.00$ | $\text{ns}$ | OpenSTA post-OpenRCX signoff |
| **AC-TIM-02** | Worst Negative Slack (WNS) - Hold Timing | $\ge 0.00$ | $\text{ns}$ | OpenSTA post-OpenRCX signoff |
| **AC-DRC-03** | Max Slew / Max Capacitance Violation Count | $0$ | violations | OpenROAD placement & routing check |
| **AC-PHY-04** | Detailed Routing DRC Cleanliness | $0$ | DRC errors | OpenROAD / KLayout signoff check |

---

### 5. Verified Context Citations
- **OpenROAD Physical Design & Synthesis Toolflow:** Main stages verified from documentation: Floorplanning (initialization, tap/well tie, PDN), Global Placement (repair max slew/capacitance/fanout), Detailed Placement (legalization, incremental timing), Clock Tree Synthesis (buffer insertion, setup/hold optimization), Global/Detailed Routing (antenna repair, DRC-correct routing), and Chip Finishing (OpenRCX parasitic extraction, final timing verification).
- **180nm DRAM Topology Specification:** Access transistor channel length ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), minimum storage capacitance budget ($28\text{ fF/cell}$), and cell leakage ceiling ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The RTL sequencer testbench lacks cross-domain asynchronous assertion checks between the ESP32 SPI/UART command ingress and the 133MHz DDR PHY controller domain. - **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node (1.8V/3.3V dual gate oxide), standard cell library timing models show significant non-linear delay variations across PVT corners (SS_1.62V_125C to FF_1.98V_-40C). - **Supply Chain Critic**: Standard cell libraries for 180nm open-source PDKs (such as SkyWater or generic foundry equivalents) have restricted cell availability for specialized high-fanout clock buffers and low-power latch cells. # Standard Operating Procedure: Timing Signoff & Cycle-Accurate Verification against JEDEC tRP/tRCD/tRFC Rules

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In our 180nm mixed-signal DRAM architecture, the digital core operates at 1.8V nominal VDD while driving discrete access transistor gates through wordline boosters (VPP ~ 3.1V). Cycle-accurate FPGA PHY state machine verification must guarantee that tRP (Row Precharge time, min 15 ns / 3 clock cycles at 200 MHz) and tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay, min 15 ns) are honored not just at nominal 25°C, but across slow-slow (SS, 1.62V, 85°C) corners where inverter propagation delays degrade from 80 ps/stage to >140 ps/stage. Inadequate cycle tracking or clock domain crossing (CDC) jitter between the ESP32 SPI configuration bridge and FPGA DDR controller risks issuing ACTIVATE commands into floating sense amplifiers during precharge bitline equalization (VBLP = 0.90V ± 50 mV), collapsing charge sharing margins.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: JEDEC JESD79-compliant SDR/DDR timing specifications dictate strict minimum durations for tRP, tRCD, and tRFC (Auto-Refresh Cycle Time, min 70 ns / 14 cycles). In an open-source 180nm planar 1T-1C architecture where trench/stacked cell capacitance is marginally 25-30 fF and junction leakage limits retention to <64 ms at 85°C, violating tRFC by even a single clock period truncates distributed refresh sequences. Sense amplifier sense/restore latching requires full tRCD to prevent destructive readouts where delta-V on bitline pairs is less than the 65 mV latch discrimination threshold. Dynamic ring oscillator tracking (tau_d <= 80 ps) must calibrate FPGA digital delay lines (IDELAY/ODELAY) to avoid command-to-data contention.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing cycle-accurate timing metrology relies on low-jitter COTS FPGA verification platforms (AMD/Xilinx Artix-7 XC7A100T or Gowin GW2A) coupled with high-bandwidth 4-channel mixed-signal oscilloscopes (min 1 GHz analog bandwidth, 5 GSa/s, e.g., Keysight InfiniiVision or Rohde & Schwarz RTM3004). Active differential probe tips (0.7 pF capacitive loading) and SMA high-speed breakout interposers face lead times of 8 to 14 weeks. Substituted generic passive probes introduce 12-15 pF parasitic shunt loading, which artificially suppresses rise/fall times (tr/tf > 2.2 ns) and falsifies hardware tRP/tRCD compliance signoffs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology signoff on tRP/tRCD/tRFC rules serves as Milestone Reality Gate G2-PHY prior to tape-out mask fabrication. Schedule risk centers on divergence between RTL cycle simulation (Verilator / Cocotb testbenches) and physical FPGA gate-level netlists with post-synthesis parasitic delays. Researchers must deliver locked Verilog timing assertion coverage logs, cycle-accurate CSV logic analyzer traces, and a signed signoff checklist within a strict 3-day sprint; failure to pass all cycle constraints blocks GDSII merge into the open-source MPW run.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature ACTIVATE command issued prior to tRP completion (tRP_actual < 15.0 ns), inducing catastrophic charge redistribution across bitlines before equalization to V_M (0.90V ± 50 mV), leading to multi-bit read inversion.
1. tRFC refresh window truncation (<70 ns) due to asynchronous clock drift between ESP32 motor controller command stream and FPGA state machine, causing unrefreshed storage cell charge leakage past subthreshold limit (I_off > 10 pA/um) and unrecoverable silent data corruption.
1. Sense amplifier strobe race during tRCD violating the 65 mV differential threshold, triggering latch flip before cell capacitance full restore.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-3-01` | **Cycle-Accurate Measurement of Row Precharge Time (tRP) and RAS-to-CAS Delay (tRCD) under Full Clock Jitter** | Keysight InfiniiVision MSOX3104T (1 GHz, 5 GSa/s, 4 Channel Digital/Analog), N2795A 1 GHz Single-Ended Active Probes (capacitance < 1 pF), Rohde & Schwarz SMA Breakout Fixture, Saleae Logic Pro 16 USB Logic Analyzer (synchronous 500 MSa/s digital capture). | 1. Initialize FPGA JEDEC state machine via ESP32 SPI configuration registers with burst length BL=4, CAS Latency CL=2, tRP=3 cycles (15.0 ns), tRCD=3 cycles (15.0 ns). 2. Execute a continuous loop of 100,000 PRECHARGE -> ACTIVATE -> READ sequences across bank 0, row 0x01AA, column 0x02. 3. Trigger MSOX3104T on the falling edge of command strobe /CS concurrent with PRECHARGE (/RAS=0, /CAS=1, /WE=0). 4. Measure the propagation delay delta-T1 between PRECHARGE registered clock edge and subsequent ACTIVATE (/RAS=0, /CAS=1, /WE=1) registered clock edge. 5. Measure delta-T2 between ACTIVATE registered clock edge and subsequent READ (/RAS=1, /CAS=0, /WE=1) registered clock edge. 6. Record waveform histogram statistics (mean, min, max, std dev) over 100,000 continuous trigger acquisitions. | `PASS if for all 100,000 acquisitions: delta-T1 (tRP) >= 15.000 ns (exactly >= 3 clock cycles with 0 cycle underflow) and delta-T2 (tRCD) >= 15.000 ns (exactly >= 3 clock cycles with 0 cycle underflow), with clock skew jitter <= 120 ps pk-pk and zero false state machine transitions. FAIL if any delta-T < 14.900 ns.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-3-02` | **Auto-Refresh Timing Verification (tRFC) and Continuous Array Retention Strobe Verification** | Keysight MSOX3104T with high-density Mictor-38 logic analyzer breakout adapter, Tektronix Keithley 2450 SourceMeter (monitoring 1.8V core rail current with 10 pA resolution), Espec Thermal Chamber set to 85.0°C. | 1. Program controller state machine to execute 8,192 consecutive AUTO-REFRESH (REF) commands at intervals of tREFI = 7.8 us. 2. Connect active oscilloscope probes to command bus lines (/CS, /RAS, /CAS, /WE, CKE) and Keithley 2450 to VDD rail. 3. Trigger scope on AUTO-REFRESH assertion (/RAS=0, /CAS=0, /WE=1, /CS=0). 4. Measure time interval delta-T3 from REF command active edge to the earliest allowable next command (ACTIVATE or REF) edge to verify tRFC execution. 5. Simultaneously monitor core transient current profile on Keithley 2450 to detect bitline precharge-restore dynamic surge during refresh (expected 12-18 mA peak). 6. Following 8,192 refresh cycles, execute burst READ of all 8,192 rows and perform CRC-32 integrity comparison against preloaded test pattern. | `PASS if delta-T3 (tRFC) >= 70.000 ns (min 14 clock cycles at 200 MHz) across all 8,192 events, peak dynamic current <= 25.0 mA, and array bit error rate BER = 0 (100% CRC-32 match over all rows). FAIL if delta-T3 < 70.000 ns or if any bit errors occur.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/impact-resistant safety glasses, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat conforming to ANSI/ESD S20.20, Class 100 cleanroom compatible powder-free nitrile gloves (thickness 4 mil), Continuous-monitoring grounded ESD wrist strap (1 Mohm series resistor)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye Contact: Immediately flush eyes with gently flowing isotonic eyewash solution for minimum 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek ophthalmic medical evaluation. Skin Contact: Wash skin with mild soap and water; remove contaminated clothing. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh air immediately; in case of N2 asphyxiation in enclosed test chambers, administer supplemental oxygen via trained personnel and initiate CPR if breathing has ceased.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized laminar fume extraction or Class 100 laminar flow hood (face velocity 0.45 to 0.55 m/s) during solvent contact pad cleaning; test bench area equipped with ambient oxygen depletion sensors (alarm setpoint at 19.5% O2) to guard against nitrogen blow-off purging asphyxiation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free swab wipes and cleaning residues must be collected in closed, heavy-gauge poly-lined, grounding-bonded flammable waste receptacles; segregated from oxidizing acids and disposed of through licensed hazardous organic solvent waste reclamation contractors in compliance with local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade (VLSI / ULSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Gaseous Nitrogen (N2)** | `7727-37-9` | Electronic Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `240 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-fabricated bond pads / SMA probe landing points bare Cu/ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold), native oxide thickness < 1.2 nm, particulate contamination < 1 particle/cm2 at >= 0.3 um.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically probed and verified contact pads inspected under 50x optical microscope; scrub mark depth < 150 nm (retaining > 80% gold pad layer thickness), zero solder bridging, zero organic contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air Q-time (>240 minutes) causes atmospheric copper/nickel oxidation and airborne organic hydrocarbon adsorption on test pads, driving probe contact resistance from <0.5 ohm to >15 ohms; this induces signal distortion, false ground bounce, and apparent tRP/tRCD timing violations during high-frequency metrology.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full cycle-accurate verification and timing signoff of the 180nm DRAM FPGA memory controller state machine against JEDEC JESD79 tRP, tRCD, and tRFC protocol rules under nominal and thermal corner conditions, establishing deterministic zero-cycle-violation signoff across 100,000 operational cycles and 8,192 consecutive auto-refresh intervals.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `JEDEC_Timing_Signoff_Report_tRP_tRCD_tRFC.pdf`
- [ ] `Cycle_Accurate_Timing_Metrology_Raw_Data.csv`
- [ ] `FPGA_PHY_Oscilloscope_Waveform_Traces.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Row Precharge Time (tRP) minimum duration constraint verification** | `15.000 ns (3 clock cycles at 200 MHz)` | +5.000 ns / -0.000 ns | High-bandwidth 1 GHz oscilloscope automated delta-time measurement over 100,000 PRECHARGE-to-ACTIVATE transitions |
| `ASSERT-02` | **RAS-to-CAS Delay (tRCD) minimum duration constraint verification** | `15.000 ns (3 clock cycles at 200 MHz)` | +5.000 ns / -0.000 ns | High-bandwidth 1 GHz oscilloscope automated delta-time measurement over 100,000 ACTIVATE-to-READ/WRITE transitions |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Auto-Refresh Cycle Time (tRFC) duration constraint verification** | `70.000 ns (14 clock cycles at 200 MHz)` | +10.000 ns / -0.000 ns | Synchronous logic analyzer and digital oscilloscope capture across 8,192 distributed refresh cycles at 85°C |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 100,000 test sequences demonstrate strictly zero instances where tRP < 15.000 ns or tRCD < 15.000 ns, tRFC conforms to >= 70.000 ns across 8,192 refresh cycles at 85°C with zero data corruption (CRC-32 verified), and formal signoff document JEDEC_Timing_Signoff_Report_tRP_tRCD_tRFC.pdf is counter-signed by Systems Engineering and Metrology leads.

testcases.instrumentation: Keysight InfiniiVision MSOX3104T (1 GHz, 5 GSa/s, 4 Channel Digital/Analog), N2795A 1 GHz Single-Ended Active Probes (capacitance < 1 pF), Rohde & Schwarz SMA Breakout Fixture, Saleae Logic Pro 16 USB Logic Analyzer (synchronous 500 MSa/s digital capture).
testcases.pre_conditions: FPGA testbed running at 200 MHz core system clock (period T_clk = 5.000 ns ± 15 ps jitter); supply rail regulated at VDD = 1.800 V ± 10 mV; ambient chamber temperature maintained at 25.0°C ± 1.0°C; bitline precharge voltage level verified at VBLP = 0.900 V ± 20 mV.
testcases.procedure:
1. Initialize FPGA JEDEC state machine via ESP32 SPI configuration registers with burst length BL=4, CAS Latency CL=2, tRP=3 cycles (15.0 ns), tRCD=3 cycles (15.0 ns).
2. Execute a continuous loop of 100,000 PRECHARGE -> ACTIVATE -> READ sequences across bank 0, row 0x01AA, column 0x02.
3. Trigger MSOX3104T on the falling edge of command strobe /CS concurrent with PRECHARGE (/RAS=0, /CAS=1, /WE=0).
4. Measure the propagation delay delta-T1 between PRECHARGE registered clock edge and subsequent ACTIVATE (/RAS=0, /CAS=1, /WE=1) registered clock edge.
5. Measure delta-T2 between ACTIVATE registered clock edge and subsequent READ (/RAS=1, /CAS=0, /WE=1) registered clock edge.
6. Record waveform histogram statistics (mean, min, max, std dev) over 100,000 continuous trigger acquisitions.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if for all 100,000 acquisitions: delta-T1 (tRP) >= 15.000 ns (exactly >= 3 clock cycles with 0 cycle underflow) and delta-T2 (tRCD) >= 15.000 ns (exactly >= 3 clock cycles with 0 cycle underflow), with clock skew jitter <= 120 ps pk-pk and zero false state machine transitions. FAIL if any delta-T < 14.900 ns.

testcases.title: Auto-Refresh Timing Verification (tRFC) and Continuous Array Retention Strobe Verification
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight MSOX3104T with high-density Mictor-38 logic analyzer breakout adapter, Tektronix Keithley 2450 SourceMeter (monitoring 1.8V core rail current with 10 pA resolution), Espec Thermal Chamber set to 85.0°C.
testcases.pre_conditions: Thermal chamber stabilized at 85.0°C ± 0.5°C; FPGA testboard running JEDEC controller core with auto-refresh counter programmed for distributed refresh interval tREFI = 7.8 us; test memory array preloaded with pseudorandom checkerboard pattern (0x55AA55AA).
testcases.procedure:
1. Program controller state machine to execute 8,192 consecutive AUTO-REFRESH (REF) commands at intervals of tREFI = 7.8 us.
2. Connect active oscilloscope probes to command bus lines (/CS, /RAS, /CAS, /WE, CKE) and Keithley 2450 to VDD rail.
3. Trigger scope on AUTO-REFRESH assertion (/RAS=0, /CAS=0, /WE=1, /CS=0).
4. Measure time interval delta-T3 from REF command active edge to the earliest allowable next command (ACTIVATE or REF) edge to verify tRFC execution.
5. Simultaneously monitor core transient current profile on Keithley 2450 to detect bitline precharge-restore dynamic surge during refresh (expected 12-18 mA peak).
6. Following 8,192 refresh cycles, execute burst READ of all 8,192 rows and perform CRC-32 integrity comparison against preloaded test pattern.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: PASS if delta-T3 (tRFC) >= 70.000 ns (min 14 clock cycles at 200 MHz) across all 8,192 events, peak dynamic current <= 25.0 mA, and array bit error rate BER = 0 (100% CRC-32 match over all rows). FAIL if delta-T3 < 70.000 ns or if any bit errors occur.

Static-dissipative ESD lab coat conforming to ANSI/ESD S20.20

Skin Contact: Wash skin with mild soap and water; remove contaminated clothing. # SOP: JEDEC Timing Assertions & SVA Checker Testbench Setup
**Level:** Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Action Type:** Make  
**Domain:** Architecture & Integration / Digital Logic & Metrology / Circuit Design

---

### Verification Flow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  JEDEC Command Stream  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  SVA Protocol Monitor  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ├─────────────────────────────╮
             │                             │
             ├─────────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                             ▼                             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │    │                        │    │                        │
│     tRP Precharge      │    │     tRCD Activate      │    │  tRFC Refresh Checker  │
│        Checker         │    │        Checker         │    │                        │
└──────────┬─────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
           │                               │                             │
           │   ╭───────────────────────────┼─────────────────────────────╯
           │   │                           │
           ▼ ▼ ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Pass / Fail Log     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Parameter Calibration & Physical Boundary Binding**
   - Bind digital timing constants to the underlying 180 nm physical device models: access transistor dimensions $W/L = 220\,\text{nm} / 180\,\text{nm}$, cell storage capacitance $C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\,\text{fF}$, and supply rail $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$.
   - Ensure the wordline overdrive voltage $V_{PP}$ is set between $2.6\,\text{V}$ and $2.8\,\text{V}$ (providing $V_{DD} + V_{th}$ overdrive with $V_{thn} = +0.55\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$) to eliminate threshold drop during charge sharing.
   - Set sense amplifier activation delays: $1\,\text{ns}$ to $2\,\text{ns}$ separation between NMOS pull-down ($SAN$ low) and PMOS pull-up ($SAP$ high) restoration phases.

2. **SVA Protocol Checker Module Definition**
   - Implement an SVA assertion module monitoring the command bus: `CS_N`, `RAS_N`, `CAS_N`, `WE_N`, `CKE`, `BA`, and `ADDR`.
   - Sample all signals strictly on `posedge CLK`.

3. **$t_{RP}$ (Row Precharge Time) SVA Construction**
   - Assert that after a `PRECHARGE` command (`CS_N=0, RAS_N=0, CAS_N=1, WE_N=0`) targeting a bank, no subsequent `ACTIVATE` command (`CS_N=0, RAS_N=0, CAS_N=1, WE_N=1`) can occur on that bank before the cycle equivalent of $t_{RP}$ has elapsed:
     ```systemverilog
     property p_tRP_check(bank);
       @(posedge clk) disable iff (!reset_n)
       (cmd_precharge && (target_bank == bank)) |-> 
         not (##[1 : CYCLES_TRP - 1] (cmd_activate && (target_bank == bank)));
     endproperty
     ```

4. **$t_{RCD}$ (RAS-to-CAS Delay) SVA Construction**
   - Assert that following an `ACTIVATE` command to a bank, no `READ` (`CS_N=0, RAS_N=1, CAS_N=0, WE_N=1`) or `WRITE` (`CS_N=0, RAS_N=1, CAS_N=0, WE_N=0`) command is issued to the same bank prior to $t_{RCD}$ elapsed cycles:
     ```systemverilog
     property p_tRCD_check(bank);
       @(posedge clk) disable iff (!reset_n)
       (cmd_activate && (target_bank == bank)) |-> 
         not (##[1 : CYCLES_TRCD - 1] (cmd_read_or_write && (target_bank == bank)));
     endproperty
     ```

5. **$t_{RFC}$ (Auto-Refresh Cycle Time) SVA Construction**
   - Assert that upon an `AUTO_REFRESH` command (`CS_N=0, RAS_N=0, CAS_N=0, WE_N=1`), all banks remain idle and no `ACTIVATE` or subsequent `AUTO_REFRESH` command is executed across any bank for the entire duration of $t_{RFC}$ cycles:
     ```systemverilog
     property p_tRFC_check;
       @(posedge clk) disable iff (!reset_n)
       cmd_refresh |-> not (##[1 : CYCLES_TRFC - 1] (cmd_activate || cmd_refresh));
     endproperty
     ```

6. **Testbench Binding & Signoff Run**
   - Bind `sva_jedec_checker` to the FPGA Memory Controller core and DDR PHY interface.
   - Run formal property verification (FPV) or dynamic randomized constrained simulation across corner cases. All assertion violations must halt simulation with cycle-accurate error telemetry.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                       Physical Signoff Parameters      
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │░                                     │
     V_PP WL (V)┤░                                     │
                │▒▒▒                                   │
Capacitance (fF)┤▒▒▒                                   │
       Vthn (mV)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
     Ion (uA/um)┤███████████████████████████████████   │
                │███████████████████████████████████   │
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                0.0     137.5     275.0    412.5  550.0 
```

1. **Storage Cell Capacitance**: Minimum $28\,\text{fF}$ per cell ($C_{\text{cell}} \ge 28\,\text{fF}$) to guarantee noise margin and refresh retention.
2. **Access Transistor Leakage Current**: Sub-threshold and junction leakage strictly $\le 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
3. **Wordline Boost Voltage**: $V_{PP} = 2.6\,\text{V} \text{ to } 2.8\,\text{V}$ (yielding overdrive $> V_{DD} + V_{thn}$ where $V_{thn} = +0.55\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$).
4. **Sense Amplifier Delay Constraint**: NMOS pull-down ($SAN$) to PMOS pull-up ($SAP$) transition delay between $1\,\text{ns}$ and $2\,\text{ns}$.
5. **Protocol SVA Coverage**: $0$ assertion failures across $10^7$ pseudo-random constrained verification cycles.

---

### Citations of Local Literature Sources
- **[Stage 3 Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification](./docs/context.yaml)**: Target sub-micron transistor geometry ($W/L = 2.0\,\mu\text{m} / 0.18\,\mu\text{m}$), $V_{thn} = +0.55\,\text{V} \pm 50\,\text{mV}$, $I_{on} \ge 500\,\mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$, $I_{off} \le 10\,\text{pA}/\mu\text{m}$ at $V_{DS} = 1.8\,\text{V}$.
- **[Cross-Coupled Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing & Charge Restoration](./docs/context2.yaml)**: Equalization to $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$, wordline boosted $V_{PP} = 2.6\,\text{V} - 2.8\,\text{V}$, and $SAN$-to-$SAP$ phase delay of $1 - 2\,\text{ns}$.
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](./docs/context3.yaml)**: Access gate channel dimensions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}, W = 220\,\text{nm}$), minimum capacitance budget $\ge 28\,\text{fF/cell}$, and cell leakage $\le 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

*Micro-knowledge entry has been persisted to [docs/jedec_sva_checker_setup.md](./docs/jedec_sva_checker_setup.md).*

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Formal SVA checkers must bridge the cycle-accurate boundary between the ESP32 host memory bus interface, the FPGA DDR PHY controller, and the custom 180nm DRAM macro model. Writing assertions exclusively at the external pin level misses internal bank state tracking (e.g. tRCD, tRP, and tRFC collisions during back-to-back auto-refresh cycles under high interrupt loads from the closed-loop motor control loop).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm, device parameters (Vthn = +0.55V +/- 50mV, subthreshold swing ~85 mV/dec, and discrete transistor Ron) dictate larger parasitic delays and longer internal charge-redistribution times during row precharge (tRP) and sense amp activation (tRCD). The SVA testbench must mathematically correlate simulated nanosecond timings to conservative PVT corners (SS corner at 1.62V, 125°C) rather than relying on idealized generic DDR synchronous clock assertions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: All SVA suites and testbench harnesses must execute seamlessly on both open-source formal/simulation engines (Icarus Verilog + SymbiYosys/Yosys-SMTBMC) and standard FPGA commercial EDA tools (AMD Vivado / Gowin EDA) without proprietary system-level verification licensing lock-in.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Signoff milestones must explicitly demonstrate 100% formal property coverage for all JEDEC illegal state transitions prior to committing FPGA logic synthesis to OpenROAD macro tapeout; missing an unasserted auto-refresh collision could lead to silent data corruption during live closed-loop motor commutation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Silent data corruption caused by violated row-activation to precharge timing (tRAS minimum violated) when real-time motor controller priorities force preemption of memory accesses.
1. Deadlock or unhandled bus contention in the DDR PHY controller caused by overlapping auto-refresh (tRFC) commands issued during active bank burst transfers.
1. False-positive assertion passes occurring when clock-domain crossing (CDC) between the ESP32 SPI/QSPI interface and FPGA internal memory controller clock causes metastable pulse masking.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-3-1-01` | **Formal SVA Protocol Verification for Bank-Level tRP, tRCD, and tRAS Rules** | SymbiYosys (BMC engine: Boolector/Z3) running SVA sequence checker harness integrated with Cocotb 1.8+ runner and PyRTL monitor. | 1. Constrain formal solver to generate arbitrary valid and invalid stimulus across all 4 internal DRAM bank addresses. 2. Assert property p_trcd: upon ACTIVATE command to bank B, no READ or WRITE command allowed to bank B before tRCD_cycles >= 3 clock cycles. 3. Assert property p_trp: upon PRECHARGE command to bank B, no subsequent ACTIVATE command to bank B allowed before tRP_cycles >= 3 clock cycles. 4. Run BMC check up to depth k = 50 cycles. | `Zero assertion failures; 100% reachable cover properties verified; 0 unreachable state traps detected across 50 execution cycles.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-3-1-02` | **Auto-Refresh (tRFC) Preemption & Collision Cycle-Accurate Gate-Level Check** | Icarus Verilog v12 / Verilator with GTKWave waveform dump parser and automated SVA violation log analyzer script. | 1. Inject high-priority DRAM access request concurrently with the assertion of the internal auto-refresh tick (tREFI). 2. Monitor command bus signals (CS_n, RAS_n, CAS_n, WE_n). 3. Evaluate SVA property p_trfc_guard: verify that during tRFC duration, the DRAM memory controller asserts WAIT/STALL backpressure to the host bus and issues no command other than NOP/DESELECT for exactly >= 10 clock cycles. 4. Run testbench across 10,000 continuous refresh cycles. | `Strict enforcement of 0 commands issued within tRFC window across 10,000 iterations; exactly zero SVA assert error log entries; average host latency overhead <= 12 cycles per refresh.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-static safety glasses, ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, Static-dissipative cleanroom nitrile gloves
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with cleaning solvent, flush immediately with copious clean water at the emergency eyewash station for >= 15 minutes. In case of inhalation, move personnel to fresh outdoor air. For accidental electrical shock, isolate line power immediately and initiate standard CPR if unresponsive.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics lab benchtop snorkel exhaust (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s) active during solvent cleaning of FPGA breakout boards and test sockets.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA cleaning wipes in designated sealed, airtight, grounded, flammables-rated hazardous chemical waste receptacles; dispose via licensed hazardous solvent disposal protocol.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Bench IPA for FPGA PCB & socket contact cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / VLSI Grade (Semiconductor Grade) | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `1440 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `168 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Assembled cleanroom FPGA dev board and 180nm DRAM test silicon packaged and mounted in clean test socket, free of ionic solder flux residue and dust particulate.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Dry, clean, de-energized test assembly stored under ESD-safe static shielding bags inside dry nitrogen storage desiccator.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Oxidation of exposed gold/copper socket contacts and moisture adsorption causing signal degradation, impedance mismatch, and false timing violations on 133MHz DDR signal lines.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete, formally verified SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA) checker testbench suite for JEDEC DDR memory timing compliance, validating tRP, tRCD, tRAS, and tRFC rules against custom 180nm DRAM behavioral and gate-level netlists.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `jedec_timing_sva_checker.sv`
- [ ] `tb_jedec_timing_formal_report.pdf`
- [ ] `timing_assertion_coverage_metrics.csv`

| `ASSERT-01` | **Formal verification proof completeness for all standard JEDEC timing rules (tRP, tRCD, tRAS, tRFC, tRRD)** | `100%` | 0% tolerance (100% of asserted properties must pass formal proof) | SymbiYosys formal model-checker execution summary report |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Minimum row precharge cycle enforcement (tRP) under worst-case 180nm PVT delay corner** | `18.0 ns (3 clock cycles at 133 MHz)` | +/- 0.0 ns (no sub-cycle command violations allowed) | Cycle-accurate SVA temporal property assertion logs in gate-level simulation |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Auto-refresh cycle stall guard duration (tRFC) adherence without command leakage** | `72.0 ns (10 clock cycles at 133 MHz)` | +/- 0.0 ns undershoot tolerance | Verilator assertion monitor waveform trace and GTKWave timing markers |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All formal properties and SVA checkers compile without warnings, achieve 100% proof depth on SymbiYosys without counterexamples, log zero timing assertions violations over 10,000 continuous randomized testbench cycles, and receive formal signoff review from Digital Verification Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-DRAM180-FPGA-004`
**Title:** Cycle-Accurate Dynamic Timing Verification & Constraint Extraction  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > FPGA High-Speed DRAM Memory Controller Core (Verilog DDR PHY & JEDEC State Machine) [Digital Logic & FPGA] > JEDEC Timing & Refresh Protocol State Machine Architecture Modeling [Circuit Design] > Timing Signoff & Cycle-Accurate Verification against JEDEC tRP/tRCD/tRFC Rules [Metrology] > Cycle-Accurate Dynamic Timing Verification & Constraint Extraction [Digital Logic & FPGA]  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Timing Protocol

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Precharge Command   │
│       PRE / tRP       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Row Activate ACT /   │
│         tRCD          │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Column Read/Write   │
│     RD/WR / tCAS      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Sense Amp Restore &  │
│       Equalize        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Auto-Refresh REF /   │
│         tRFC          │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

#### Step 1: Analog Bitline & Storage Node Boundary Parameter Extraction
1. Extract analog parasitic values from the 180nm 1T1C stacked capacitor (COB crown/MIM) layout:
   - Verify access transistor dimensions: channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Ensure storage node capacitance meets baseline: $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominal $28\text{ fF}$).
   - Extract bitline parasitic capacitance ($C_b$) across array blocks with 256 or 512 cells per bitline: nominal range $150\text{ fF} \le C_b \le 250\text{ fF}$.
   - Check capacitance ratio constraint: verify $C_b / C_s$ remains strictly between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (never exceeding $10:1$).

#### Step 2: Dynamic Signal Development & Sense Margin Timing Profiling
1. Simulate differential signal development on folded complementary bitlines ($BL$ and $/BL$) initialized to $V_{DD}/2$:
   $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right)$$
2. Measure analog transition delay required to achieve $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ differential read signal margin before latch activation ($SAN$/$SAP$).
3. Map analog sense amplifier stabilization and charge restoration delays to target FPGA memory controller clock cycles:
   - Determine minimum cycles for Row-to-Column Delay ($t_{RCD}$).
   - Determine minimum cycles for Row Precharge Time ($t_{RP}$) during bitline equalization to $V_{DD}/2$.

#### Step 3: Refresh Timing Calculation & Leakage Constraint Mapping
1. Enforce thermal leakage ceiling: sub-threshold and junction leakage must not exceed $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
2. Compute auto-refresh protocol timing constraints for the JEDEC state machine:
   - Calculate Refresh Recovery / Cycle Time ($t_{RFC}$) covering full row restore and bitline re-equalization across the array.
   - Configure cycle-accurate timer blocks in the FPGA controller to strictly enforce $t_{RP}$, $t_{RCD}$, and $t_{RFC}$ inter-command spacing.

#### Step 4: RTL Testbench Harness & Cycle-Accurate Assertion Verification
1. Instantiate the Verilog DDR PHY and JEDEC State Machine testbench.
2. Bind SystemVerilog assertions (SVA) checking cycle counts between commands:
   - Assert $PRE$-to-$ACT \ge \lceil t_{RP} / T_{clk} \rceil$.
   - Assert $ACT$-to-$(RD/WR) \ge \lceil t_{RCD} / T_{clk} \rceil$.
   - Assert $REF$-to-$ACT \ge \lceil t_{RFC} / T_{clk} \rceil$.
3. Run corner stress simulations (zero-cycle violations permitted under all traffic patterns).

#### Step 5: SDC/XDC Constraint Generation & Static Timing Signoff
1. Export cycle constraints into Synopsys Design Constraints (`.sdc`) / Vivado (`.xdc`):
   - Declare multi-cycle paths and false paths matching the calibrated state machine minimum delays.
   - Ensure dynamic simulation traces align $100\%$ with extracted physical array timing boundaries.

---

### 3. Capacitance & Metrology Distribution Chart

```text
                   Physical Capacitance Budgets (fF)    
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │████████████████████████████████████████│
  C_b Para Max┤████████████████████████████████████████│
              │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
  C_b Para Min┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                │
C_s Budget Nom┤▒▒▒▒▒                                   │
              │▒▒▒▒▒                                   │
C_s Budget Min┤░░░░░                                   │
              │░░░░░                                   │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
              0.0      62.5      125.0    187.5   250.0 
```

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric ID | Parameter Description | Minimum Target | Nominal Target | Maximum Target | Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-MET-01** | Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$) | $25.0$ | $28.0$ | $30.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Post-layout extraction of crown/MIM stacked capacitor |
| **AC-MET-02** | Bitline-to-Cell Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$) | $5.0 : 1$ | $7.0 : 1$ | $9.0 : 1$ (hard limit $< 10.0 : 1$) | Ratio | Metrology extraction across 256/512 cell array blocks |
| **AC-MET-03** | Developed Bitline Differential Voltage ($\Delta V$) | $100.0$ | $125.0$ | $150.0$ | $\text{mV}$ | Analog transient simulation prior to sense amp latching |
| **AC-MET-04** | Cell Sub-threshold & Junction Leakage Current ($85^\circ\text{C}$) | — | — | $1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | DC I-V parameter extraction at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$ |
| **AC-MET-05** | State Machine Cycle Timing Assertion Violations ($t_{RP}, t_{RCD}, t_{RFC}$) | $0$ | $0$ | $0$ | Count / Errors | RTL cycle-accurate testbench dynamic simulation |

---

### 5. Verified Local Literature Citations
- **[1] 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Transistor dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) crown/MIM dielectric ($\kappa > 15$), nominal capacitance budget ($28\text{ fF}$ per cell), leakage target ($< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$).
- **[2] 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: 1T1C cell architecture ($8F^2$ folded bitline footprint $= 0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$), cell capacitance range ($C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$), bitline parasitic capacitance ($C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ for 256–512 cells/BL), and strict capacitance ratio requirement ($5:1 \le C_b / C_s \le 9:1$, $< 10:1$).
- **[3] Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Differential sensing with CMOS cross-coupled inverters, precharge equalization to $V_{DD}/2$, and read signal development margin ($\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ at $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$, $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The cycle-accurate dynamic timing verification framework must close the physical-to-digital loop across the ESP32 host bridge, FPGA DDR PHY, and the custom 180nm DRAM test silicon. Dynamic simulation testbenches often fail to accurately correlate cycle-based digital assertions against analog parasitics extracted via OpenRCX during OpenROAD physical design iterations. Without back-annotated Standard Delay Format (SDF) timing simulations across PVT corners (Slow-Slow 1.62V 125°C to Fast-Fast 1.98V -40°C), extracted Synopsys Design Constraints (SDC) for tRCD, tRP, and tRFC will be overly optimistic, causing intermittent timing closure failures on the real hardware controller.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: DRAM sense amplifier latching dynamics dictate hard analog boundaries that a pure Verilog state machine cannot intuitively comprehend without explicit cycle-accurate phase tracking. The 180nm cross-coupled regenerative sense amplifier requires strict separation between Wordline turn-on (boosted V_PP at 2.6V-2.8V charge sharing), N-sense latching (SAN pulling to 0V), and delayed P-sense restoration (SAP pulled to VDD after 1-2 ns). Failure to enforce exact tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay) and tRP (Row Precharge / Equalization to V_BLP) cycle constraints in the FPGA memory controller leads to destructive reads from incomplete charge restoration or bitline shorting during precharge equalization.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying verification testbenches on vendor-locked FPGA toolchains creates operational bottlenecks. SDC generation must align strictly with vendor-agnostic toolflows (such as Yosys/nextpnr or open-source OpenROAD SDC format) while remaining synthesizable onto low-cost Lattice ECP5 or Xilinx Artix-7 COTS FPGA validation boards. If the pin-level I/O slew constraints and PCB trace delays to the 180nm unpackaged die/QFN-64 package exceed 1.2 ns skew, the timing constraints extracted will demand non-standard, costly high-speed PCB substrate materials rather than standard FR-4.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: From a project execution standpoint, dynamic timing verification is the gatekeeper for tape-out milestone M2. If the timing constraint extraction pipeline takes more than 4 hours per regression run, synthesis iterations will stall development across the motor controller and DDR PHY teams. The deliverables must include automated machine-readable assertion logs, an SDC constraint file, and a cycle-accurate timing margin summary matrix that directly maps to OpenROAD synthesis inputs without manual post-processing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature Sense Amp Latching: Read command issued prior to sufficient differential bitline voltage development (|V_BL - V_/BL| < 150 mV), resulting in flipped data bits during sense amplifier regeneration.
1. Destructive Precharge Overlap: tRP violation causing equalization switch (EQ) activation while Wordline is still asserted at V_PP, instantly draining capacitor storage cell charge to V_BLP (VDD/2).
1. Dynamic Clock Skew and Metastability: Setup/hold violations on FPGA PHY I/O capture registers caused by clock-to-data jitter under high-temperature corner conditions (125°C) exceeding the SDC allowable margin.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-3-2-01` | **Dynamic Cycle-Accurate Verification of tRCD and tRP Parameter Compliance under Max PVT Jitter** | 16-Channel 500 MHz Mixed-Signal Logic Analyzer / Protocol Analyzer (Agilent/Keysight 16800 Series or Saleae Logic Pro 16), 4 GHz Active Differential Oscilloscope Probes, FPGA Internal Integrated Logic Analyzer (ILA) core at 200 MHz sampling, and OpenROAD OpenSTA Timing Engine. | 1. Initialize the JEDEC state machine through power-up and calibration sequence (200 µs clock stabilization, precharge all, auto-refresh x2, mode register set MRS). 2. Issue continuous Row Activate (ACT) command to Bank 0, Row 0x01AA. 3. Sweep the programmable ACT-to-READ delay counter in the FPGA controller from 2 clock cycles to 8 clock cycles (10 ns per cycle at 100 MHz clock). 4. Capture bitline differential sense amplifier signals and FPGA PHY RX valid flag on logic analyzer to detect the minimum valid tRCD. 5. Issue Precharge (PRE) command and sweep PRE-to-ACT (tRP) interval from 1 to 6 clock cycles while continuously measuring bitline equalization signal (EQ) voltage level via active differential probes. 6. Export cycle violation assertion counter logs from the digital verification bench. | `Zero functional bit errors detected when tRCD >= 4 cycles (40.0 ns) and tRP >= 4 cycles (40.0 ns) across 100,000 continuous random access cycles; Setup and hold slack reported by OpenSTA on the DRAM interface bus must be >= +0.35 ns; Logic analyzer confirms EQ pulse strictly transitions only after WL drops to 0.0V with minimum 2.5 ns non-overlap guard band.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-1-3-2-02` | **Automated SDC Constraint Extraction and Round-Trip OpenROAD Static Timing Signoff** | OpenROAD-flow-scripts (ORFS) OpenSTA engine, Python-based SDC generator harness, SystemVerilog SVA (SystemVerilog Assertions) testbench runner with Synopsys VCS / Icarus Verilog. | 1. Run dynamic assertion testbench exercising boundary conditions for JEDEC tRFC (Auto-Refresh Cycle Time, target 70 ns), tRAS (Row Active Time, target 45 ns), and tWR (Write Recovery Time, target 15 ns). 2. Execute Python SDC extraction script against the simulation waveform database (VCD/FSDB) to calculate max allowable input/output delays, clock uncertainty, and multicycle paths. 3.
