# Standard Operating Procedure: $t_{RCD}$ Shmoo Plot Margin Metrology & JEDEC Timing Compliance Verification

**Generation**: Gen 2 (180 nm) | **Action Type**: Make | **Council**: DRAM Foundation VN  
**Target Architecture**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (Folded Bitline $8F^2$, Stacked Capacitor over Bitline)

---

### Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Precharge & VDD/2    │
│      Equalization      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Row Activation & WL   │
│         Boost          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Charge Sharing: BL   │
│   Delta V 100-150mV    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Sense Amp Activation  │
│        SAN/SAP         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Column Read & Shmoo   │
│       Point Log        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) Testbench Initialization**
   - Connect the FPGA DDR Controller Core to the 180nm DRAM device under test (DUT).
   - Configure array precharge circuitry to equalize bitlines ($BL$ and $/BL$) to exactly $V_{DD} / 2$ prior to wordline activation.
   - Establish baseline supply voltages: core array $V_{DD} = 1.80\text{ V}$, wordline boost $V_{PP} = 3.0\text{ V}$, and thermal chamber set to $25^\circ\text{C}$ and $85^\circ\text{C}$.

2. **Test Pattern Loading & Charge Conditioning**
   - Write solid and checkerboard background patterns across all 256/512 cell bitline columns using the access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}, W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Allow bitlines to settle into quiescent precharge state with cell storage capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$) fully charged.

3. **Parametric $t_{RCD}$ Sweep Setup**
   - Configure the FPGA high-speed state machine fine delay lines (IDELAY/ODELAY) to step the Row-to-Column Command Delay ($t_{RCD}$, duration between `ACTIVATE` and `READ`/`WRITE`) in $100\text{ ps}$ increments from $10.0\text{ ns}$ up to $30.0\text{ ns}$.
   - Sweep core supply voltage $V_{DD}$ across the characterization window: $1.62\text{ V}$ ($-10\%$), $1.80\text{ V}$ (Nominal), and $1.98\text{ V}$ ($+10\%$).

4. **Differential Signal Development Characterization**
   - Trigger the `ACT` command to turn on the wordline NMOS access gate.
   - Monitor bitline charge sharing: ensure transfer of cell charge $Q_s = C_s \times (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$ onto bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$.
   - Verify differential signal development $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \times (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$ attains $100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ before the Sense Amplifier Latch (SAN/SAP) strobe activates.

5. **2D Shmoo Matrix Execution & Pass/Fail Capture**
   - At each grid point $(V_{DD},\, t_{RCD},\, T)$, issue burst-read commands and compare received bitstreams against written reference patterns.
   - Flag bit errors caused by premature column selection (insufficient sense amp latching time).
   - Map pass/fail boundaries into the Shmoo plot array matrix and extract maximum operational timing margins.

```text
                  tRCD Timing Margin vs Core VDD (ns)   
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
               │███████████████████████████████████████│
   1.98V (+10%)┤███████████████████████████████████████│
1.80V (Nominal)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒     │
               │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒     │
   1.62V (-10%)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░            │
               │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░            │
               └┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬┘
               0.0       5.1     10.2      15.3    20.4 
```

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$)**:  
   $\mathbf{C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}\text{ to }30\text{ fF}}$ (nominal target $\mathbf{28\text{ fF}}$ per cell).
2. **Bitline Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)**:  
   $\mathbf{5:1 \le C_b / C_s \le 9:1}$ (strictly $\mathbf{< 10:1}$, with $C_b = 150\text{ fF}\text{ to }250\text{ fF}$ across 256/512 cells per bitline).
3. **Differential Sensing Margin ($\Delta V$)**:  
   $\mathbf{\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}\text{ to }150\text{ mV}}$ developed at the sense amplifier input prior to latch activation.
4. **Storage Retention Sub-threshold/Junction Leakage**:  
   $\mathbf{I_{leak} < 1\text{ fA/cell}}$ at $\mathbf{85^\circ\text{C}}$ operating ambient.

---

### Verified Context Citations

- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: Defined $8F^2$ folded bitline footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$), $C_s$ budget ($25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$, nominal $28\text{ fF}$), bitline parasitic $C_b$ ($150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ for 256/512 cells), and critical ratio constraint $5:1 \le C_b / C_s \le 9:1$.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**: Access transistor channel dimensions ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), stacked capacitor over bitline (COB), $28\text{ fF}$ minimum capacitance budget, and retention leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Differential signal development equation $\Delta V = (C_s / (C_{BL} + C_s)) \times (V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2)$, precharge equalization to $V_{DD}/2$, and target signal delta window of $100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$.

---

> [!NOTE]
> Micro-knowledge for this metrology procedure has been persisted to [trcd_shmoo_margin_metrology.md](./docs/knowledge/trcd_shmoo_margin_metrology.md).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The HIL FPGA state machine must account for clock jitter, probe parasitics, and inter-die trace skew between the FPGA PHY and the 180nm DRAM test die. Attempting to measure sub-nanosecond tRCD margins without calibrating out the round-trip board trace delay (T_prop) and digital I/O buffer propagation delays will inject systematic offsets into the Shmoo boundary.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay) is physically governed by wordline boost voltage ramp rate, bitline capacitive loading (Cb/Cs ratio), and sense amplifier latch overdrive speed. Shmoo plots swept across VDD (1.6V to 2.0V) and temperature (-40°C to 125°C) must isolate bitline differential voltage development (delta-V_BL >= 120mV) prior to activating SAN/SAP triggers; otherwise, artificial sensing failures will corrupt the true JEDEC compliance envelope.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom high-bandwidth active differential probe tips (e.g., Keysight InfiniiMax >= 4GHz) and controlled-impedance ceramic interposers for 180nm packaged/bare die test vehicles have long procurement lead times (12-16 weeks). Test fixtures must incorporate COTS SMA interconnects and impedance-matched 50-ohm microstrips to prevent testbench bottlenecks.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Execution schedule requires automated batch sweeping via Python SCPI scripts controlling the FPGA HIL rig and thermal stream chuck within a 48-hour testing window. Manual probe station adjustments risk throughput delays and physical pad scrub degradation on prototype wafers.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature Sense Amplifier Activation: Triggering CAS read command before delta-V_BL reaches full rail-to-rail differential sensing margin, resulting in read disturb and pseudo-random bitflips on the Shmoo cliff edge.
1. Transmission Line Reflection Induced Metastability: Impedance mismatch across the probe card-to-FPGA interconnect causing ringback into input receivers, misinterpreting high-speed strobe transitions during tight tRCD timings.
1. Thermal Runaway / Chuck Drift: Insufficient thermal chuck coupling during 85°C/125°C sweeps altering subthreshold leakage currents (I_off) in access transistors, shifting the tRCD boundary dynamically during acquisition.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-3-3-3-01` | **Automated 2D Voltage-Timing tRCD Shmoo Characterization** | Xilinx Artix-7/Kintex-7 FPGA development board running custom Verilog JEDEC DDR PHY, Keysight B2902B Precision Source-Measure Unit (SMU), Temptronic ThermoStream TPO4300, Keysight Infiniium 4GHz Oscilloscope. | 1. Initialize FPGA state machine and issue JEDEC standard power-on initialization sequence and MRS register configuration. 2. Configure SMU to sweep DRAM core voltage VDD from 1.50V to 2.10V in 25mV increments. 3. For each voltage step, sweep the tRCD programmable delay counter from 10.0ns to 30.0ns in 200ps Vernier delay steps. 4. Execute a write-read-compare burst test across a 1MB memory address bank using pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS-7). 5. Record Pass/Fail status for each (VDD, tRCD) grid point and map the functional boundary cliff. | `Pass if tRCD functional boundary achieves <= 18.0ns at nominal VDD = 1.80V at 25°C, with zero bit errors observed across all addresses over 10^7 read operations, and monotonic scaling observed across the 1.6V-2.0V operating range.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-FPGA-3-3-3-02` | **Four-Corner Temperature & JEDEC Timing Compliance Verification** | FPGA-based High-Speed Memory Testbench with integrated AXI memory tester, Temptronic Thermal Stream enclosure, Tektronix 4-Channel Active Differential Probe (P7700 series). | 1. Soak the DUT chamber sequentially at -40°C, 25°C, 85°C, and 105°C for 15 minutes each. 2. Set VDD to minimum corner (1.62V) and maximum corner (1.98V). 3. At each corner, command back-to-back ACTIVATE-to-READ commands configured at fixed JEDEC compliant tRCD = 20.0ns. 4. Continuously log bit error rate (BER) over 50,000 bursts of March C- algorithm iterations. 5. Measure differential voltage on DQS strobe and DQ data lines using oscilloscope active probes to verify setup (tDS) and hold (tDH) timing margins. | `Zero memory bit failures (BER = 0) across all 4 temperature/voltage corners at JEDEC tRCD = 20.0ns; minimum differential eye opening > 350mV with setup/hold margin > 1.2ns relative to active clock edge.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1000/ISO 6 Cleanroom gown and hood, ESD-safe dissipative nitrile gloves (surface resistivity 10^6 - 10^9 ohms/sq), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact safety glasses, Thermal insulated cryogenic/hot-handling gloves for ThermoStream nozzle maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin or eye contact with IPA, flush immediately with copious amounts of deionized water for at least 15 minutes at the eyewash station. In the event of localized thermal burn or frostbite from ThermoStream nozzle, gently warm affected area with tepid water (do not rub) and seek cleanroom occupational health personnel immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Maintain local exhaust extraction ventilation above test chuck during solvent wipe operations with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s); operate within positive-pressure HEPA-filtered cleanroom environment with continuous N2 purge exhaust venting to prevent asphyxiation hazards.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect IPA solvent wipes and rinse residues in designated airtight, flame-resistant flammable solvent waste cans; dispose of via hazardous chemical waste protocol per semiconductor fab regulatory standards.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Semiconductor Grade)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `>= 99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pristine unoxidized bond pads/leads with wirebond/C4 bump metallization free of organic residue and particulate contamination (MIL-STD-883 Method 2010 inspection passed).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and validated die/package with micro-probe scrub marks within 15% pad area limit, clean of electrostatic carbon residue or thermal condensation moisture.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric copper/aluminum pad oxidation and airborne hydrocarbon contamination causing contact resistance (Rc) drift > 2.5 ohms per pin, leading to false-failure boundary shifts and signal attenuation during high-speed tRCD Shmoo sweeps.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Comprehensive tRCD timing margin and JEDEC compliance characterization matrix for the 180nm DRAM test vehicle, validating row-activation to bitline differential sensing latency across multi-corner voltage and temperature envelopes via FPGA HIL automation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

critics.domain_expert: tRCD (RAS-to-CAS delay) is physically governed by wordline boost voltage ramp rate, bitline capacitive loading (Cb/Cs ratio), and sense amplifier latch overdrive speed. critics.supply_chain: Custom high-bandwidth active differential probe tips (e.g., Keysight InfiniiMax >= 4GHz) and controlled-impedance ceramic interposers for 180nm packaged/bare die test vehicles have long procurement lead times (12-16 weeks). # Standard Operating Procedure: Signal Integrity & Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB

High-speed PCB layout, controlled impedance microstrip routing, propagation delay skew matching, and power delivery network (PDN) impedance optimization.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Interfacing 3.3V LVCMOS ESP32 GPIOs with a 1.8V/3.3V DRAM PHY daughtercard demands strict skew matching across command/address and bidirectional DQ bus lines. Propagation delay through active level shifters (e.g., TXB0108/SN74AXC8T245) must not exceed 2.5 ns with <150 ps channel-to-channel skew, otherwise round-trip read timing margins collapse against the bitline sensing window of the 180nm core.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: A 50-Ohm single-ended microstrip topology on standard FR4 substrate requires tight dielectric constant control (Er = 4.2-4.5) and controlled etch undercut. Reference plane discontinuities across power domain splits (3.3V to 1.8V) will induce return path inductances, resulting in severe ground bounce, overshoot exceeding 200 mV, and parasitic capacitive loading that exceeds the 150-250 fF bitline equivalent budgeting requirements.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying specialized high-speed auto-direction sensing level shifters risks single-source procurement choke points; dual-supply direction-controlled bus transceivers with standardized TSSOP/QFN footprints must be dual-sourced (TI, Nexperia) alongside controlled-dielectric JLC04161H-7628 / standard ISOLA 370HR stackups.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Fabrication lead times for 4-layer 1.0mm controlled-impedance boards with TDR coupon testing must be locked to 5 business days to avoid starving the physical DRAM test fixture assembly schedule; board spin iterations must be budgeted to a maximum of 2 spins.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Microstrip impedance deviation exceeding +/-10% (Z0 > 55 Ohm or < 45 Ohm), inducing transmission line reflections, ringing, and false clock edge triggers.
1. Ground return path disruption across the 3.3V/1.8V level shifter boundary, causing excessive common-mode ground bounce and corrupting the 28 fF cell refresh cycling.
1. Propagation delay mismatch between level-shifter channels causing address setup/hold timing violations during multi-bit DRAM write sequences.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-01` | **Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Characteristic Impedance Verification** | Keysight N1000A DCA-X Wideband Oscilloscope with N1055A 50 GHz TDR/TDT Module and 50-Ohm high-bandwidth microprobe fixture | 1. Launch a 35 ps incident step pulse into the designated 50-Ohm single-ended microstrip test coupons on Top and Bottom signal layers. 2. Measure the reflected waveform amplitude and calculate instantaneous characteristic impedance (Z0) along the entire 50 mm trace length. 3. Record minimum, maximum, and mean Z0 across 8 parallel data traces. | `Z0 across all traces must satisfy 50.0 Ohm +/- 4.0 Ohm (46.0 Ohm <= Z0 <= 54.0 Ohm); peak trace-to-trace impedance deviation must be <= 1.5 Ohm.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-02` | **Level Shifter Dynamic Propagation Delay, Skew, and Eye Integrity Test** | Teledyne LeCroy WaveMaster 820Zi-B (20 GHz, 80 GS/s) with D9000-PS differential/single-ended active probes and Rigol DG4202 arbitrary function generator | 1. Inject a 50 MHz square wave (50% duty cycle, 1.2 ns edge rate, 0-3.3V swing) to input channel IN_A0. 2. Concurrently record input and shifted output OUT_B0 on the oscilloscope. 3. Measure propagation delays t_PLH and t_PHL, calculate intra-chip channel-to-channel skew across channels 0 to 7, and extract 10^6 UI eye diagram parameters at 100 Mbps PRBS7. | `Propagation delay t_pd <= 3.2 ns; channel-to-channel output skew <= 180 ps; output overshoot/undershoot <= 150 mV; eye opening width >= 8.5 ns at 100 Mbps with jitter RMS <= 35 ps.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, ESD-safe powder-free nitrile gloves (minimum 4 mil thickness), Anti-static dissipative lab coat, Thermal protective soldering gloves for hot-air rework
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water for 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush with isotonic saline eyewash for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh ambient air immediately. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; administer water if conscious and contact poison control.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop HEPA/activated-carbon fume extraction operating at a minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s located within 15 cm of soldering/cleaning zone; ambient lab air exchange >= 8 room air changes per hour.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA solvents and flux residues must be collected in labeled, grounded HDPE flammable solvent drums; spent solder dross and contaminated cleaning wipes must be segregated into sealed hazardous chemical solid waste bins for certified industrial disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Rosin Core Flux Residue (Abietic Acid derivatives)** | `514-10-3` | Technical / Electronic Assembly Grade | `15.0%` |
| **Lead-Free Solder Alloy (SAC305 - Tin/Silver/Copper)** | `7440-31-5` | Electronics Grade Solder | `96.5% Sn, 3.0% Ag, 0.5% Cu` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Bare ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold) PCB surface finish free of copper oxidation, organic residues, or moisture adsorption; contact angle < 25 degrees.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully reflowed, cleaned, flux-residue-free (ionic contamination < 1.0 ug/cm2 NaCl equivalent), and baked at 60 deg C prior to conformal coat or test socketing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption in PCB laminate dielectric inducing delamination/popcorning during reflow soldering; gold/nickel intermetallic oxidation causing non-wetting or micro-voiding on fine-pitch QFN level shifter thermal ground pads.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Fabrication, assembly, and empirical electrical signoff of the 4-layer 50-Ohm controlled-impedance signal integrity and level shifter daughtercard PCB, demonstrating compliant TDR trace impedance, matched delay/skew performance, and clean signal transmission between 3.3V MCU domains and 1.8V DRAM evaluation fixtures.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `pcb_tdr_impedance_profile_report.csv`
- [ ] `level_shifter_dynamic_eye_diagram_analysis.pdf`
- [ ] `daughtercard_aoi_xray_solder_inspection.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Characteristic single-ended microstrip trace impedance across all high-speed signals** | `50.0 Ohm` | +/- 4.0 Ohm | High-bandwidth TDR coupon measurement (Keysight N1055A) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Intra-bus channel-to-channel propagation delay skew across 8-bit level-shifted data bus** | `120 ps` | +/- 40 ps (max <= 160 ps) | Multi-channel high-speed real-time oscilloscope acquisition (80 GS/s) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Maximum signal overshoot/undershoot at DRAM-side interface at 50 MHz operation** | `80 mV` | +/- 30 mV (max <= 120 mV above VDD / below GND) | Active high-impedance low-capacitance FET probing under active bus loading |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researchers sign off when 100% of manufactured coupons achieve 50 +/- 4 Ohm impedance, intra-bus delay skew remains below 160 ps across all channels, solder joint voiding under level-shifter QFN pads is verified below 15% via X-ray imaging, and continuous 100 Mbps PRBS7 signal transmission shows zero bit errors over 10^9 cycles.

# Standard Operating Procedure: 50-Ohm Controlled Impedance Stackup Design & Level Shifter Schematic Synthesis

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: FPGA DDR PHY state machine must rigorously implement JEDEC initialization sequences (200 us CKE low, precharge all, MRS registers). Skew across high-speed DDR DQ/DQS matched traces must hold <= 10 ps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: PCB transmission line characteristic impedance must hold strictly at 50-ohm single-ended / 100-ohm differential (+/- 5%). Eye diagram opening at receiver must maintain >= 65% horizontal width and >= 200 mV vertical height.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Xilinx/Intel FPGA development carrier boards and high-speed SMA fixtures are standard COTS. Make is strictly restricted to custom daughtercard PCB layout, Verilog DDR PHY controller RTL, and firmware.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 32-60 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Jitter or power rail ripple on FPGA PLL induces intermittent read/write pattern errors during high-speed diagnostic telemetry sweeps).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Clock-to-data skew violating tIS/tIH setup/hold timing margin during DDR write bursts.
1. Power distribution network impedance resonance causing core VDD droop > 100 mV during simultaneous output switching.
1. Asynchronous clock domain crossing metastability in memory controller telemetry FIFO.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-01` | **DDR High-Speed Signal Integrity & Eye Diagram Oscilloscope Capture** | Keysight Infiniium 4 GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope with Differential High-Z Active Probes | 1. Probe DQ0-DQ7 and DQS differential strobe lines directly at DRAM test daughtercard receiver pins. 2. Accumulate 1,000,000 signal transitions into persistence eye diagram. 3. Extract horizontal eye width, vertical eye opening height, and RMS clock jitter. | `Eye width >= 65% UI (Pass); Vertical eye height >= 200 mV (Pass); Clock jitter RMS <= 12 ps (Pass).` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-02` | **March C- Algorithmic Memory Fault & Retention Telemetry Verification** | FPGA Hardware-in-the-Loop Diagnostic Firmware & Automated Python Telemetry Suite | 1. Execute March C- sequence: (w0), up(r0, w1), up(r1, w0), down(r0, w1), down(r1, w0), (r0). 2. Sweep retention pause times from 1 ms to 128 ms between write and read phases. 3. Stream per-address failure bitmap via UART/USB to telemetry logging engine. | `March C- 100% address pass at nominal 64 ms refresh window (Pass); Zero bit error rate (BER < 1e-12) (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD smock and grounded conductive wrist strap (1 MOhm safety resistor), Safety glasses with side shields during soldering and PCB prototyping, Nitrile gloves during circuit board solvent cleaning

# Standard Operating Procedure: 4-Layer PCB Stackup Definition & 50-Ohm Microstrip Field Solver Modeling

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The 4-layer stackup (Signal-GND-PWR-Signal) must guarantee an unbroken, low-inductance return path directly beneath L1 high-speed lines to L2 GND plane; reference plane stitching vias and decoupling capacitor placement near level-shifter transceivers are mandatory to prevent ground bounce and common-mode radiation during 180nm DRAM test pattern burst generation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: 2D/3D electromagnetic boundary element field solver modeling must accurately account for trapezoidal copper trace etch factor (typically 1:1.5 to 1:2 taper), soldermask conformal coating thickness (er_mask ~3.8, 15-25 um over trace vs 10-15 um on dielectric), and prepreg resin-rich glass weave non-homogeneity (FR-4/Isola high-Tg core, er_core ~4.3-4.5) to avoid a 3-5 Ohm characteristic impedance offset from the nominal 50.0 Ohm target.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standard low-cost quick-turn prototype fab houses utilize standard 7628 / 2116 / 1080 prepreg constructions with nominal core thicknesses (0.2 mm, 0.36 mm, 0.71 mm, 1.0 mm); custom dielectric press-outs cause long fabrication lead times and yield loss, so microstrip trace widths must be calculated strictly against off-the-shelf standard prepreg glass styles and 1 oz (35 um) copper foils.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Field solver modeling outputs, cross-sectional stackup drawings, and coupon Gerber files must be locked before tape-out to avoid tooling hold-ups; automated stackup validation scripts must be committed to the CI pipeline to prevent silent impedance drift in KiCad/Altium layout revisions.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Return path discontinuity across split power/ground planes causing severe ringing, overshoot exceeding level-shifter V_IH/V_IL thresholds, and false clock edge triggering on DRAM control strobes.
1. Dielectric thickness variation during lamination press-out exceeding +/-10%, shifting Z0 beyond 55 Ohms and introducing reflections that degrade setup/hold margins on high-speed DRAM bitline sense-amplifier readout tests.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-01` | **Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) 50-Ohm Characteristic Impedance Verification** | Keysight E5080B VNA or Tektronix 8300 TDR Mainframe with 20 GHz 80E04 TDR Sampling Head and 50-Ohm GSG differential/single-ended microprobes (250 um pitch). | 1. Land calibrated GSG probe onto the standardized L1 microstrip test coupon coupon pads. 2. Acquire reflected step response waveform over a 50 mm uniform line length. 3. Gate out probe launch discontinuities and pad capacitive loading effects (first 5 mm). 4. Measure mean, minimum, and maximum instantaneous impedance across the flat 40 mm trace section. | `Single-ended characteristic impedance Z0 must measure 50.0 Ohm +/- 2.5 Ohm (47.5 Ohm <= Z0 <= 52.5 Ohm) across the uniform transmission line coupon segment.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-02` | **VNA Scattering Parameter (S11 Return Loss & S21 Insertion Loss) Characterization** | Rohde & Schwarz ZNB20 Vector Network Analyzer (100 kHz - 20 GHz) equipped with calibrated semi-rigid SMA test cables and 3.5mm female test fixtures. | 1. Connect Ports 1 and 2 to the SMA launch connectors of the 100 mm microstrip coupon. 2. Sweep S-parameters from 10 MHz to 3.0 GHz with 1001 points and 1 kHz IF bandwidth. 3. Log S11 return loss profile and S21 insertion loss profile. 4. Extract dielectric attenuation and copper surface roughness loss components. | `S11 return loss must remain <= -18.0 dB from 10 MHz up to 2.5 GHz; S21 insertion loss magnitude must be >= -1.2 dB over the entire 100 mm line at 1.5 GHz.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: EN 374 Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (thickness >= 0.12 mm), ANSI Z87.1 approved chemical splash safety glasses with side shields, Electrostatic discharge (ESD) safe lab coat with grounded wrist strap, Fume extraction snorkel / localized particulate mask during destructive cross-section grinding
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA or uncured resin, wash immediately with copious running water and mild soap for >= 15 minutes. For eye splash, rinse thoroughly at the eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek medical attention. If inhaled, move personnel immediately to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Perform solvent board degreasing and coupon cleaning inside a chemical fume hood maintaining face velocity between 0.4 m/s and 0.6 m/s (80-120 FPM); use benchtop HEPA/activated carbon snorkel extractors during coupon sawing and polishing.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA in clearly labeled, grounded, flammable-waste hazardous solvent containers. Collect cured metallographic epoxy blocks and abrasive silicon carbide grinding slurry in solid hazardous waste drums for licensed industrial incineration; never discharge into sanitary sewer.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Epoxy Mounting Resin (for cross-section microsectioning)** | `25068-38-6` | Metallographic Grade | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-cleaned, micro-etched, degreased Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold (ENIG) or Lead-Free HASL copper surface coupon free of oxidation, fingerprints, or flux residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Moisture-purged, desiccated board coupon stored in sealed anti-static nitrogen dry cabinet (< 5% RH) ready for precision TDR/VNA measurement or component assembly.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric moisture absorption into FR-4 core dielectric increases relative permittivity er by up to 0.4, causing a downward impedance shift of ~2-3 Ohms, and copper pad surface tarnish elevates contact resistance on precision GSG test probes.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Synthesized 4-layer PCB stackup definition table, boundary-element 2D/3D microstrip field solver impedance calculation dataset, and TDR coupon layout files guaranteeing 50.0 Ohm +/- 5% single-ended characteristic impedance for the 180nm DRAM daughtercard interface.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_pcb_stackup_field_solver_report.pdf`
- [ ] `microstrip_50ohm_impedance_sweep_w_vs_h.csv`
- [ ] `gerber_tdr_impedance_coupon_layers.zip`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Calculated 2D Boundary Element Field Solver characteristic microstrip impedance Z0 for nominal trace width W=0.254 mm (10 mil) over H=0.150 mm (6 mil) prepreg with er=4.3 and soldermask** | `50.0 Ohm` | +/- 1.5 Ohm | Electromagnetic 2D field solver simulation (Ansys Q2D / Polar SI9000 equivalent numerical boundary solver) |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Differential microstrip impedance Z_diff for level-shifter high-speed clock pair at nominal trace width and spacing** | `100.0 Ohm` | +/- 5.0 Ohm | Static and full-wave BEM field solver matrix extraction over 100 MHz to 3 GHz |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Physical TDR measurement mean characteristic impedance across fabricated production coupon** | `50.0 Ohm` | +/- 2.5 Ohm | Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) step reflection gating using Keysight E5080B or Tektronix 8300 TDR probe fixture |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Engineering sign-off requires unanimous concurrence across systems, SI/PI, and layout engineering that field solver modeling matches stackup supplier tolerances within +/-5%, all quantitative assertions (ASSERT-01 to ASSERT-03) evaluate to PASS, and impedance coupons are integrated into the master production Gerber panel.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## FR4/Copper Dielectric Core & Prepreg Material Sourcing & Vendor Stackup Characterization

- **Document ID:** `SOP-PCB-IMP-002`
- **Revision:** `v1.0`
- **Context Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller > Signal Integrity & Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB (50-Ohm Controlled Impedance Microstrips) > 50-Ohm Controlled Impedance Stackup Design & Level Shifter Schematic Synthesis > 4-Layer PCB Stackup Definition & 50-Ohm Microstrip Field Solver Modeling > FR4/Copper Dielectric Core & Prepreg Material Sourcing & Vendor Stackup Characterization
- **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Visual Process Flow

```text
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                       │
│   FR4/Copper Dielectric Sourcing &    │
│      Vendor Stackup Procurement       │
│                                       │
└───────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                       │
│    Coupon Cut & Cold Mounting Epoxy   │
│     Micro-Section Sample Polish       │
│                                       │
└───────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                       │
│      Optical / SEM Metrology &        │
│     Time-Domain TDR Z0 Profiling      │
│                                       │
└───────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│                                       │
│    Field Solver Calibration & 50-Ohm  │
│        Acceptance Verification        │
│                                       │
└───────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Characterization Procedure

#### Step 1: Vendor Prepreg & Core Material Procurement Specification
- Procure standard high-$T_g$ ($T_g \ge 150^\circ\text{C}$) FR4 dielectric core and prepreg glass-weave material (e.g., 2116 or 7628 prepreg styles, nominally $\varepsilon_r \approx 4.2 \text{ to } 4.5$ at 1 GHz).
- Specify finished outer copper foil nominal thickness as $1.0\text{ oz}$ ($35\,\mu\text{m}$) and inner reference ground planes as $1.0\text{ oz}$ ($35\,\mu\text{m}$).
- Request vendor-certified pressed thickness sheets for outer dielectric height $H_1 = 100\,\mu\text{m} \pm 10\,\mu\text{m}$ between Layer 1 (RF/Signal Microstrip) and Layer 2 (Continuous GND Plane).

#### Step 2: Cross-Sectional Micro-Sectioning & Specimen Preparation
- Extract test coupons containing the 50-Ohm transmission line test vehicles from the PCB panel rails.
- Mount coupon in cold-curing acrylic/epoxy metallographic resin; cure and grind flat using successive silicon carbide (SiC) abrasive papers (grit 320 to 1200).
- Final polish using $1\,\mu\text{m}$ and $0.05\,\mu\text{m}$ alumina suspension to achieve a scratch-free copper/FR4 interface cross-section under metallographic inspection.

#### Step 3: Physical Geometry Metrology (Optical & Cross-Section SEM)
- Measure finished microstrip trace width ($W$), trace thickness ($T$), and dielectric isolation distance ($H$) to adjacent ground planes.
- Verify finished copper trace thickness is within target bounds of $35\,\mu\text{m} \pm 5\,\mu\text{m}$.
- Quantify trace trapezoidal etch factor: bottom width $W_{\text{bot}}$ versus top width $W_{\text{top}}$ to calibrate field solver dielectric boundary conditions.

#### Step 4: Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Impedance Characterization
- Connect calibrated high-bandwidth TDR sampling head ($t_r \le 35\,\text{ps}$) to the 50-Ohm microstrip test coupon via precision coplanar RF microprobes.
- Record characteristic impedance $Z_0$ profile along the flat microstrip plateau across the active daughtercard routing segment.
- Confirm dielectric consistency and signal layer planar uniformity across the entire panel coupon span.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
                  Stackup Parameter Verification Targets
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                │
    Z0 Imp. (50-Ohm)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                │

                    │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
```

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations

1. **Microstrip 50-Ohm Controlled Impedance System**:
   - Trace geometries referenced directly from parent node requirements: *50-Ohm Controlled Impedance Microstrips (Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB) & 4-Layer Field Solver Modeling*.
2. **Package & Assembly Interface Boundaries**:
   - Die pad metallization and packaging thermal/mechanical baseline derived from:
     - `--- Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging ---`: Pad clearance guidelines ($100\,\mu\text{m} \times 100\,\mu\text{m}$ pads), gold/aluminum bond wire clearances ($25\,\mu\text{m}$ wire), and package lead integrity standards (Mil-Std-883 Method 2011).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Sourcing standard commercial FR4 (Tg ~130-140°C) introduces significant dielectric constant (Dk) variation (4.2 to 4.8 across batches and humidity swings), which directly degrades the 50-Ohm single-ended microstrip impedance tolerance on the level shifter daughtercard. At high-speed switching frequencies required to drive 180nm DRAM test signals, this impedance mismatch induces reflections, degrades edge rates (<1.5 ns rise times), and compromises data transmission integrity across the ESP32-to-DRAM interface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Prepreg resin content and weave style (e.g., 7628 vs. 2116 or 1080) dictate both the pressed dielectric thickness and local weave-induced skew. Utilizing coarse weave styles introduces localized Dk variations that alter microstrip propagation velocity. Specifying mid-loss, high-Tg (Tg >= 170°C, e.g., Shengyi S1000-2M or Isola FR408HR) with controlled resin content and explicit prepreg pressed-thickness datasheets is mandatory to achieve reliable 2D field solver modeling within +/-5% of 50 Ohms.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Generic COTS PCB fabs frequently substitute prepreg styles and copper foil suppliers without change notifications (PCN). Sourcing must explicitly lock in standard IPC-4101 slash-sheet compliant laminates (IPC-4101/126) with electrodeposited (ED) low-profile or very low-profile (VLP) copper foil from certified tier-1 laminate vendors to prevent unnotified stackup substitutions across prototype and production runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterization lead times can stall daughtercard spin iterations if coupon cross-sectioning and Dk/Df testing depend on external third-party labs. A vendor stackup characterization agreement must be contractually bound to deliver cross-section micrographs and TDR microstrip coupon test reports within 5 business days of panel pressing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dielectric constant (Dk) deviation (>10%) causing microstrip characteristic impedance to shift outside the 45-55 Ohm window, inducing ringing and bit errors on DRAM command/address buses.
1. Resin starvation or micro-voiding in prepreg bond plies leading to high-voltage leakage or delamination during 260°C lead-free reflow profiling.
1. Copper foil tooth profile excessive roughness (Rz > 7 µm) causing anomalous conductor attenuation and localized microstrip impedance reduction at GHz harmonics.

| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-1-02` | **Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) 50-Ohm Characteristic Impedance Verification** | Tektronix CSA8300 / 80E04 TDR Sampling Module with 20 ps incident rise time and 50-Ohm micro-coaxial ground-signal differential/single-ended probe pitch 500 µm | 1. Record minimum, mean, and maximum characteristic impedance across the central 80% plateau of the trace. | `Mean single-ended characteristic impedance Z0 must lie strictly within 50.0 +/- 2.5 Ohms (47.5 to 52.5 Ohms), with localized impedance variations not exceeding +/-1.5 Ohms along the plateau.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles and face shield, Nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, dual-layer during resin handling), Lab coat with ESD protection, N95 or particulate respirator during mechanical dry cutting/polishing of cured laminate coupons
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation of glass fiber or resin dust: Move exposed individual to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if irritation persists. Eye contact with polishing slurry or particulates: Flush eyes with copious isotonic saline or running water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water; do not use organic solvents. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly; do not induce vomiting.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate rotary coupon saws, grinding platens, and metallurgical polishing wheels within dedicated downdraft dust extraction enclosures or local HEPA exhaust hoods maintaining a minimum face velocity of 100 LFPM (0.5 m/s).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect micro-sectioning slurries, diamond suspension runoff, and spent polishing pads in designated particulate sedimentation tanks; filter suspended glass/resin particulate matter down to 5 µm before discharging aqueous phase to industrial wastewater handling. Solid fiberglass/epoxy shavings disposed of as non-hazardous industrial solid waste in accordance with EPA/local regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| **Continuous Filament Glass Fibers (E-Glass)** | `65997-17-3` | Industrial Grade | `30-50% w/w` |
| **Alumina Polishing Suspension (Aluminum Oxide)** | `1344-28-1` | Reagent Grade | `0.05 µm aqueous suspension (5% w/v)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Prepreg sheets vacuum-sealed in moisture barrier bags with desiccants and humidity indicator cards at <=5°C storage; copper clad core surfaces micro-etched, degreased, and chemically passivated (free of organic residues and fingerprint oxides).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Pressed, cured 4-layer laminate panel with microstrip top copper surface treated with immersion tin or OSP (organic solderability preservative), devoid of oxidation (water break-free test passed).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption into unlaminated prepreg leads to steam blister explosion, catastrophic delamination, and excessive dielectric loss (Df spike) during subsequent high-temperature lamination or reflow soldering.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical, chemical, and electrical characterization signoff of the vendor-supplied 4-layer FR4/copper stackup for the 50-Ohm controlled impedance daughtercard. Validates exact prepreg pressed thicknesses, core Dk/Df stability, and transmission line impedance conformance under 200 ps edge-rate TDR stimulus.

| `ASSERT-03` | **Substrate bulk dielectric constant (Dk) at 2.45 GHz (25°C, 50% RH)** | `4.30` | +/- 0.15 | Keysight E5063A VNA paired with Split-Post Dielectric Resonator (SPDR) test fixture |

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-PCB-EM-002`
**Title:** 2D/3D Field Solver Numerical Extraction of $50\ \Omega$ Microstrip & Differential Pair Geometries  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > Signal Integrity & Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB ($50\ \Omega$ Controlled Impedance Microstrips) [PCB & Hardware] > $50\ \Omega$ Controlled Impedance Stackup Design & Level Shifter Schematic Synthesis [Circuit Design] > 4-Layer PCB Stackup Definition & $50\ \Omega$ Microstrip Field Solver Modeling [Circuit Design] > 2D/3D Field Solver Numerical Extraction of $50\ \Omega$ Microstrip & Differential Pair Geometries [Circuit Design]  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 ($\mu\text{m}$) | **Action Type:** Buy (Commercial / Standard Fabrication Workflow)

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Stackup Dielectric &  │
│    Foil Definition     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Boundary &       │
│    Cross-Section 2D    │
│        Meshing         │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Quasi-Static 2D EM   │
│       Extraction       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  3D Via & Transition   │
│    Full-Wave Model     │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│       Acceptance       │
│      Validation &      │
│   Touchstone Export    │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Stackup & Material Parameter Ingestion
1. Define the 4-layer stackup substrate parameters in the 2D field solver:
   - Outer copper weight: $1.0\ \text{oz}$ finished copper thickness $t = 35.0\ \mu\text{m}$ ($1.4\ \text{mil}$).
   - Prepreg layer 1–2 (dielectric core/prepreg): Thickness $h = 100.0\ \mu\text{m}$, dielectric constant $\varepsilon_r = 4.2 \pm 0.1$, loss tangent $\tan\delta = 0.018$ at $1\ \text{GHz}$.
   - Reference plane (Layer 2, GND): Continuous solid copper return plane ($t = 35.0\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Solder mask: Thickness over laminate $c_1 = 20.0\ \mu\text{m}$, thickness over trace $c_2 = 12.0\ \mu\text{m}$, $\varepsilon_{r,\text{mask}} = 3.6$, $\tan\delta_{\text{mask}} = 0.020$.
2. Configure conductor material as annealed electrolytic tough pitch (ETP) copper with bulk conductivity $\sigma = 5.8 \times 10^7\ \text{S/m}$ and surface roughness $R_q = 0.6\ \mu\text{m}$ (modified Hammerstad/Huray model).

#### Step 2: 2D Quasi-Static Single-Ended $50\ \Omega$ Microstrip Extraction
1. Establish the cross-sectional trace geometry:
   - Base trace width $W = 180.0\ \mu\text{m}$ (matching standard 180 nm DRAM node interface scaling rules where sub-micron traces step up to interconnect transmission lines).
   - Trace etch factor (trapezoidal profile): sidewall slope angle $\alpha = 75^\circ$ ($W_{\text{top}} = W_{\text{base}} - t/\tan(75^\circ) \approx 170.6\ \mu\text{m}$).
2. Solve Laplace’s electrostatic equation $\nabla \cdot (\varepsilon(x, y) \nabla V) = 0$ over a fine finite-element mesh (minimum 12 elements per trace thickness, bounding box $> 10 \times W$).
3. Numerically compute per-unit-length capacitance with dielectric ($C$) and free space ($C_0$), inductance ($L = \mu_0 \varepsilon_0 / C_0$), and characteristic impedance:
   $$Z_0 = \sqrt{\frac{L}{C}} = \frac{1}{v_0 \sqrt{C C_0}}$$
4. Sweep width $W$ in $2.5\ \mu\text{m}$ increments to pinpoint $Z_0 = 50.0\ \Omega \pm 1.0\ \Omega$.

#### Step 3: Differential Pair Extraction ($100\ \Omega$ Differential Impedance)
1. Set up coupled microstrip edge-to-edge differential pair model on Layer 1 over Layer 2 return plane.
2. Initialize trace width $W = 150.0\ \mu\text{m}$ and inter-pair edge-to-edge separation gap $S = 180.0\ \mu\text{m}$.
3. Solve mixed-mode 2D Poisson formulation for even-mode impedance ($Z_{0e}$) and odd-mode impedance ($Z_{0o}$).
4. Calculate differential impedance $Z_{\text{diff}} = 2 \times Z_{0o}$ and common-mode impedance $Z_{\text{comm}} = Z_{0e} / 2$.
5. Tune gap $S$ until $Z_{\text{diff}}$ converges to $100.0\ \Omega \pm 2.0\ \Omega$ while verifying differential coupling coefficient $k_c = (Z_{0e} - Z_{0o}) / (Z_{0e} + Z_{0o}) \ge 0.15$.

#### Step 4: 3D Full-Wave Discontinuity & Transition Verification
1. Export 2D optimal cross-sections into 3D FEM full-wave solver (e.g., Ansys HFSS / OpenEMS).
2. Model connector launch footprints, level shifter IC pads (e.g., 1.8 V core interface logic to 3.3 V / 5.0 V ESP32 logic), and via transitions down to internal layers:
   - Ground return via pitch $\le 1.0\ \text{mm}$ adjacent to signal vias.
   - Antipad diameter $D_{\text{anti}} = 0.70\ \text{mm}$ for via drill diameter $d_{\text{drill}} = 0.30\ \text{mm}$.
3. Run adaptive frequency sweep from DC to $3.0\ \text{GHz}$ (covering high-speed DRAM clock harmonics and $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\ \text{V}$ switching edge rates).
4. Extract 2-port / 4-port S-parameters and export Touchstone files (`.s2p`, `.s4p`).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Eye Mask Margin (%)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                   │▒▒▒▒▒                              │
  Phase Match (deg)┤▒▒▒▒▒                              │
  Zdiff Tol (+/- %)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                    │
                   │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                    │
     Zo Tol (+/- %)┤████████                           │
                   │████████                           │
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                   0.0      6.2    12.5     18.8   25.0 
```

1. **Single-Ended Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$):**
   - **Target:** $50.0\ \Omega$
   - **Acceptance Limit:** $50.0\ \Omega \pm 2.5\ \Omega$ ($\pm 5.0\%$) over $100\ \text{MHz}$ to $3.0\ \text{GHz}$.
2. **Differential Characteristic Impedance ($Z_{\text{diff}}$):**
   - **Target:** $100.0\ \Omega$
   - **Acceptance Limit:** $100.0\ \Omega \pm 5.0\ \Omega$ ($\pm 5.0\%$) over $100\ \text{MHz}$ to $3.0\ \text{GHz}$.
3. **Return Loss ($S_{11}$ / $S_{dd11}$):**
   - **Target:** $\le -20.0\ \text{dB}$ across operational band; absolute maximum cutoff $\le -15.0\ \text{dB}$ at $2.5\ \text{GHz}$.
4. **Differential Phase Skew ($\Delta \theta$):**
   - **Target:** $\le 3.0^\circ$ at $1.5\ \text{GHz}$ (equivalent to group delay skew $\Delta \tau \le 5.5\ \text{ps}$).

---

### 4. Verified Literature & Context Citations

- **Source: Stage 3 Reality Gate: Discrete Long-Channel MOSFET & CMOS Inverter Verification**  
  - *Extracted Context:* Dynamic logic signaling and level shifting interfaces link sub-micron gates ($W/L = 2.0\ \mu\text{m} / 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$, operating at $V_{\text{DS}} = 1.8\ \text{V}$ with $I_{\text{on}} \ge 500\ \mu\text{A}/\mu\text{m}$ and $V_{\text{thn}} = +0.55\ \text{V} \pm 50\ \text{mV}$) to PCB-level microstrips. Field solver models must guarantee $50\ \Omega$ match to prevent reflection-induced gate oxide breakdown and false switching under fast $1.8\ \text{V}$ CMOS inverter edges.
- **Source: Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity**  
  - *Extracted Context:* Principles of transmission line parameters and planar resistance models ($R_T = 2 R_c + (R_s/W)d$). Conductor loss calculations for copper microstrip line boundaries utilize sheet resistance $R_s$ and transfer width formulation to account for edge current crowding and skin depth at microwave frequencies.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**  
  - *Extracted Context:* The $180\ \text{nm}$ lithographic generation establishes strict capacitive budgets (minimum $28\ \text{fF/cell}$ noise floor against bitline coupling capacitance). Transmission line parasitics extracted by 2D/3D field solvers must limit capacitive loading and cross-talk below the critical bitline sensing margin.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Numerical extraction of 50-ohm single-ended and 100-ohm differential microstrips must account for copper foil profile roughness (Huray or modified Hammerstad models) and dispersion in FR4/standard polyimide laminates up to the Nyquist frequency of the ESP32 fast GPIO/SPI interface (>= 1.5 GHz harmonic content). Failure to include soldermask dielectric constant (Dk ~ 3.5 to 3.8 at 1 GHz) and loss tangent directly over the outer microstrip will introduce a systematic -3 to -5 ohm characteristic impedance shift relative to idealized bare-copper simulations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: 2D quasi-static vs 3D full-wave FEM solvers exhibit divergence on differential pair edge-coupling due to the non-vertical sidewall trapezoidal etch factor (typically 65 to 75 degree trace sidewall taper on 1 oz / 35 um Cu). The numerical extraction must parameterize trace base width W_base and top width W_top, as well as the resin-rich versus glass-bundle local Dk variations along the weave to prevent phase skew in differential signaling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-tight dielectric core thicknesses (e.g., 0.1 mm +/- 5%) or non-standard prepreg glass styles (e.g., 106/1080) for low-cost domestic PCB prototype fabrication in Southeast Asia runs severe yield risks. The geometry extraction matrix must establish a dual-source envelope across JLCPCB and local quick-turn stackups (standard 7628 vs 2116 prepregs) without requiring custom laminate stocking.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable must strictly decouple CAD modeling milestones from physical coupon fabrication. Sign-off requires parameterized geometry lookup tables embedded directly into KiCad layout constraint rule files (.kicad_dru) before schematic tape-out, ensuring no downstream layout redesign cycle occurs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Impedance mismatch exceeding +/- 10% (Z0 < 45 ohms or > 55 ohms) caused by neglected soldermask deposition over thin dielectric microstrips.
1. Excessive differential phase delay skew (> 15 ps) resulting from unmodeled fiber weave anisotropic dielectric permittivity beneath differential pairs.
1. Transmission line signal reflections and ring-down exceeding 100 mV overshoot on 3.3V DRAM level-shifter outputs due to trapezoidal trace etch undercutting.

Parameterize microstrip trace width W from 0.25 mm to 0.45 mm in 5 um steps. 2. Refine adaptive mesh until energy error norm delta_E < 0.05%. 3. Extract per-unit-length capacitance matrix [C] and inductance matrix [L]. 4. Calculate characteristic impedance Z0 = sqrt(L/C) and effective permittivity E_eff. 5. Cross-verify against 3D full-wave port extraction under TEM boundary conditions. | `Single-ended microstrip geometry converges to Z0 = 50.0 ohms +/- 0.5 ohms numerically; 100-ohm differential pair (odd-mode Z_diff = 2 * Z_odd) converges to 100.0 ohms +/- 1.0 ohms at the nominal target width W and spacing S.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-2-02` | **Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Numerical Pulse Response & Return Loss (S11) Extraction** | 3D Full-Wave Electromagnetic Field Solver (transient FDTD or frequency-domain FEM with SPICE macromodel generator) | 1. Run transient simulation over a 5 ns time window. 2. Monitor reflected voltage waveform V_refl at the feed point. 3. Compute instantaneous impedance profile Z(t) = Z_ref * (1 + V_refl(t)/V_inc) / (1 - V_refl(t)/V_inc). 4. Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) the response to extract return loss S11 from DC to 3.0 GHz. | `Peak instantaneous impedance variation Delta_Z along the uniform transmission line segment does not exceed +/- 1.5 ohms from 50.0 ohms (48.5 ohms <= Z(t) <= 51.5 ohms); S11 parameter remains below -20 dB across the entire DC to 1.5 GHz band.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Standard ANSI Z87.1 approved anti-glare safety glasses for computer workstation simulation environments, Ergonomic wrist supports and ESD-compliant lab coat when operating physical hardware validation consoles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with solvent: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes. In case of inhalation of vapors: Remove victim to fresh air. If skin irritation occurs: Wash thoroughly with mild soap and water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard clean office/computational lab HVAC with >= 6 air changes per hour (ACH); dedicated benchtop fume extractor (min. 100 CFM) active when using cleaning solvents during test coupon preparation.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solvent wipes and cleaning residues in a sealed, labeled, flammable-waste container for disposal per local hazardous waste regulatory frameworks; no direct drain disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Benchtop Cleaning Solvent for Prototype Calibration Substrates)** | `67-63-0` | ACS Reagent Grade | `>= 99.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `1440 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `168 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Simulated CAD surface boundaries mathematically smooth; physical coupon calibration substrates pristine, degreased, and free of oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Geometry parameter matrix frozen into DRC constraint profiles; physical validation coupons vacuum-sealed with desiccant indicators prior to microprobe TDR.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding physical coupon queue times in ambient air causes native copper oxidation and humidity absorption in FR4 dielectrics, elevating apparent loss tangent (tan delta > 0.025) and biasing validation measurements away from numerical solver extraction baselines.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Numerical extraction of 50-ohm single-ended and 100-ohm differential microstrip trace geometries complete across realistic 4-layer stackup parameter variations (copper thickness, etch undercut, soldermask coverage, Dk tolerances), delivering validated KiCad design rules and impedance tables.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_pcb_stackup_field_solver_extraction_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `microstrip_50ohm_diff100ohm_numerical_report.pdf`
- [ ] `tdr_simulated_step_response_polar_s11.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Single-ended microstrip characteristic impedance Z0** | `50.0` | +/- 1.0 Ohm | 2D/3D Electrostatic/TEM boundary element extraction at 1.0 GHz center frequency |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Differential microstrip pair odd-mode impedance Z_diff** | `100.0` | +/- 2.0 Ohm | Coupled field solver capacitance matrix [C] and inductance matrix [L] eigensolution |
| `ASSERT-03` | **High-frequency return loss S11 up to 1.5 GHz fundamental harmonic** | `-25.0` | <= -20.0 dB | 3D full-wave S-parameter port simulation with 50-ohm reference terminations |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit condition is satisfied when the field solver extraction matrix confirms Z0 = 50.0 +/- 1.0 ohm and Z_diff = 100.0 +/- 2.0 ohm across all nominal and corner stackup parameters, the KiCad DRC netclass rules are updated with exact trace widths and clearances, and the formal extraction report is approved by the Systems Engineer.

### Controlled Impedance TDR Coupon Design & Signal Integrity Tolerance Verification

**Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)** has been authored and cataloged into [`docs/knowledge/sop_controlled_impedance_tdr_coupon.md`](./docs/knowledge/sop_controlled_impedance_tdr_coupon.md).

---

#### 1. Process Flow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Coupon Edge Launch   │
│      SMA / Probe       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Lead-in Segment min   │
│          25mm          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Uniform 50-Ohm Trace  │
│     100mm to 150mm     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ├─────────────────────────────╮
             ▼                             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐    ┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │    │                        │
│  Far-End Termination   │    │  TDR Fast Step Pulse   │
│         / Open         │    │       Injection        │
│                        │    │                        │
└────────────────────────┘    └────────────┬───────────┘
                                           │
             ╭─────────────────────────────╯
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Z0 Profile       │
│   Extraction 50 Ohm    │
│       +/- 10pct        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

#### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Panel Break-Away Coupon Physical Placement**:
   - Embed standard test coupons along the perimeter tooling rails of the 4-layer production panel.
   - Maintain identical stackup cross-section (Layer 1 Top Signal over continuous Layer 2 Solid Ground Plane).
   - Maintain a minimum separation of $\ge 2.5\,\text{mm}$ from V-score scoring paths or mouse-bite perforations to eliminate breakout-induced micro-fractures.

2. **Geometric Layout & Launch Configuration**:
   - Fabricate a uniform microstrip trace with physical length $L = 100.0\,\text{mm} \text{ to } 150.0\,\text{mm}$ (nominal $120.0\,\text{mm}$).
   - Include a launch lead-in length of $\ge 25.0\,\text{mm}$ from the coaxial edge connector (or micro-probe launch pads) to ensure connector reactance decays prior to the evaluation zone.
   - Place ground stitching vias alongside probe pads at a pitch $\le 1.0\,\text{mm}$ directly into the Layer 2 ground reference.

3. **TDR Calibration & Setup**:
   - Power on the TDR sampling oscilloscope and stabilize for 30 minutes.
   - Set step pulser edge risetime $T_r \le 35\,\text{ps}$.
   - Perform Open-Short-Load (OSL) calibration to shift the measurement reference plane to the coupon input connector.

4. **Time-Domain Reflectometry Acquisition & Time-Gating**:
   - Inject step stimulus ($200\,\text{mV} \text{ to } 400\,\text{mV}$).
   - Apply time-gating to ignore the initial $25.0\,\text{mm}$ launch discontinuity ($\approx 350\,\text{ps}$).
   - Evaluate the steady-state microstrip impedance profile across the central $50\%\text{--}80\%$ window ($30.0\,\text{mm} \text{ to } 100.0\,\text{mm}$):
     $$Z_0(t) = 50.0 \cdot \frac{1 + \rho(t)}{1 - \rho(t)}$$

---

#### 3. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

```text
                       TDR & DRAM Cell Key Metrics      
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │█                                     │
     VPP Min (V)┤█                                     │
                │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 BL Cap Max (fF)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Z0 Max Tol (Ohm)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                             │
                │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                             │
Z0 Min Tol (Ohm)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                              │
                │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒                              │
    Z0 Nom (Ohm)┤████████                              │
                │████████                              │
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                0.0     62.5      125.0    187.5  250.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Nominal Target | Tolerance / Acceptance Limit | Physical Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$)** | $50.0$ | $45.0 \text{ to } 55.0\ (\pm 10\%)$ | $\Omega$ | TDR Time-Gated Window ($30\text{--}100\,\text{mm}$) |
| **Propagation Delay ($T_{pd}$)** | $6.8$ | $6.5 \text{ to } 7.2$ | $\text{ps/mm}$ | Physical marker delta delay |
| **Bitline Parasitic Capacitance ($C_b$)** | $150.0 \text{ to } 250.0$ | $\le 250.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Integrated DRAM Macro characterization |
| **Wordline Boost Voltage ($V_{PP}$)** | $2.5 \text{ to } 2.8$ | $\ge 2.5$ | $\text{V}$ | Charge pump test monitor pin |

---

#### 4. Context Literature Citations

- **`180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench`**:
  - Validated access transistor dimensions ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$), stacked capacitor target $C_s \ge 28\,\text{fF}$, and leakage budget $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **`1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets`**:
  - Validated folded bitline ($8F^2 = 0.259\,\mu\text{m}^2$), $C_s \ge 25\,\text{fF} \text{ to } 30\,\text{fF}$ (nominal $28\,\text{fF}$), bitline parasitic $C_b = 150\,\text{fF} \text{ to } 250\,\text{fF}$, and capacitance ratio $C_b/C_s$ between $5:1$ and $9:1$.
- **`High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture`**:
  - Validated pass gate threshold loss compensation requiring boosted overdrive voltage $V_{PP} = V_{DD} + V_{th} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 2.8\,\text{V}$ using 4-stage Dickson oscillator topology ($C_{\text{pump}} = 20\,\text{pF} \text{ to } 50\,\text{pF}$, $20\,\text{MHz} \text{ to } 50\,\text{MHz}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The 50-Ohm TDR test coupon must accurately replicate the exact stackup dielectric core thickness (FR4/prepreg), soldermask deposition profile, and trace geometries utilized on the main ESP32-to-DRAM level shifter daughtercard. Any variation in ground reference return paths or via transitions in the breakout footprint will distort TDR reflectometry and yield false impedance mismatches.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-speed TDR metrology requires sub-35 ps incident rise-time step pulses to resolve localized impedance discontinuities on short daughtercard microstrip segments (< 50 mm). The coupon design must implement calibrated Ground-Signal-Ground (GSG) or SMA launch structures with de-embedding calibration standards (Open-Short-Load) to isolate launch parasitics from bulk trace characteristic impedance (Z0).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standard low-cost PCB prototyping fabricators exhibit up to ±10% to ±15% trace width tolerance and dielectric constant (Dk) fluctuations across substrate batches (FR-4 Dk varying from 4.2 to 4.6). Coupon routing must mandate explicit coupon inclusion on the manufacturing production panel edge, using controlled dielectric prepreg lots certified to IPC-4101/21.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Design and physical characterization of the TDR coupon must be frozen prior to fabricating the primary multi-layer level shifter layout. Yield gating requires coupon verification to pass IPC-TM-650 Method 2.5.5.7 specifications before clearing assembled boards for cryogenic or 180nm DRAM wafer probing interconnect integration.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Launch discontinuity masking: Excessive capacitive parasitics at SMA/GSG probe landing pads obscuring characteristic impedance reflections along the first 10-15 mm of the coupon trace.
1. Dielectric thickness and etching undercut variation: Lateral copper over-etching reducing trace top width (trapezoidal profile), causing characteristic impedance to drift above the 50 Ohm ± 5% tolerance window.
1. Soldermask dielectric loading shift: Non-uniform soldermask thickness over microstrips depressing characteristic impedance by 2 to 4 Ohms relative to field solver models without soldermask permittivity inclusion.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-3-01` | **Differential & Single-Ended Microstrip Characteristic Impedance (Z0) Verification via Sampling TDR** | Keysight DCA-X 86100D Wide-Bandwidth Oscilloscope with 54754A Differential TDR/TDT Module (or Tektronix CSA8300 with 80E04 TDR sampling head), 50-Ohm precision coaxial semi-rigid SMA test cables, calibrated torque wrench (8 in-lb). | 1. Connect channel 1 TDR step generator output to the coupon SMA launch pad using torque-calibrated SMA connector. 2. Configure incident step voltage to 200 mV with 35 ps (10%-90%) system rise time. 3. Establish TDR horizontal acquisition window to span 0 to 5 ns across the coupon trace (minimum physical trace length 100 mm). 4. Apply time-domain gating to exclude launch SMA transition (first 1.2 ns) and coupon open-circuit end reflection (last 0.8 ns). 5. Measure mean, minimum, and maximum characteristic impedance across the central 50 mm flat plateau region of the reflected waveform. | `Single-ended microstrip characteristic impedance must evaluate within 50.0 Ohm ± 2.5 Ohm (47.5 Ohm <= Z0 <= 52.5 Ohm) across the gated plateau window. Reflections along trace must exhibit peak-to-peak impedance delta <= 2.0 Ohm.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-3-02` | **Cross-Sectional Microstrip Physical Geometry & Dielectric Spacing SEM/Optical Metrology** | Precision diamond wire saw, cold epoxy mounting vacuum pot, automated rotary polisher (down to 0.05 um colloidal silica), calibrated optical metallurgical microscope (Olympus BX53M) and Zeiss Sigma Field Emission SEM. | 1. Align cross-section block on motorized stage under 500x-1000x calibrated optical/SEM imaging. 2. Measure base copper thickness (H_cu), trace bottom width (W_bot), and trace top width (W_top) to compute trapezoidal etch factor. 3. Measure dielectric core/prepreg thickness (H_diel) between trace bottom surface and underlying Layer 2 reference ground copper plane. 4. Measure soldermask thickness at trace crown (T_sm) and adjacent trace sidewalls. 5. Input measured physical dimensions into 2D electrostatic boundary element method (BEM) field solver and compare computed Z0 against empirical TDR findings. | `Dielectric thickness (H_diel) within nominal ± 10% of stackup spec. Trace width top/bottom delta must not exceed 12 um (etch factor >= 2.5). Field-solver recalculated impedance must match TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-3-01 measured TDR value within ± 1.5 Ohm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved impact & chemical splash safety goggles, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness), Standard ESD-safe static-dissipative lab coat, Thermal protective gloves for heated mounting press / bakeout oven operations
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately remove contaminated clothing; wash affected skin thoroughly with copious water and non-abrasive soap for >= 15 minutes. Eye contact: Flush opened eyes under eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids apart; seek prompt ophthalmological medical attention. Inhalation: Relocate individual immediately to fresh air; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Execute coupon degreasing and epoxy potting preparation under certified chemical fume hood with face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.5 m/s). Laboratory ambient air changes must exceed 10 room turnovers per hour.

critics.systems_engineer: The 50-Ohm TDR test coupon must accurately replicate the exact stackup dielectric core thickness (FR4/prepreg), soldermask deposition profile, and trace geometries utilized on the main ESP32-to-DRAM level shifter daughtercard. Any variation in ground reference return paths or via transitions in the breakout footprint will distort TDR reflectometry and yield false impedance mismatches.
critics.domain_expert: High-speed TDR metrology requires sub-35 ps incident rise-time step pulses to resolve localized impedance discontinuities on short daughtercard microstrip segments (< 50 mm). The coupon design must implement calibrated Ground-Signal-Ground (GSG) or SMA launch structures with de-embedding calibration standards (Open-Short-Load) to isolate launch parasitics from bulk trace characteristic impedance (Z0).
critics.supply_chain: Standard low-cost PCB prototyping fabricators exhibit up to ±10% to ±15% trace width tolerance and dielectric constant (Dk) fluctuations across substrate batches (FR-4 Dk varying from 4.2 to 4.6). Coupon routing must mandate explicit coupon inclusion on the manufacturing production panel edge, using controlled dielectric prepreg lots certified to IPC-4101/21.
critics.laya_pm: Design and physical characterization of the TDR coupon must be frozen prior to fabricating the primary multi-layer level shifter layout. Yield gating requires coupon verification to pass IPC-TM-650 Method 2.5.5.7 specifications before clearing assembled boards for cryogenic or 180nm DRAM wafer probing interconnect integration.
critical_failure_modes: Launch discontinuity masking: Excessive capacitive parasitics at SMA/GSG probe landing pads obscuring characteristic impedance reflections along the first 10-15 mm of the coupon trace.

Dielectric thickness and etching undercut variation: Lateral copper over-etching reducing trace top width (trapezoidal profile), causing characteristic impedance to drift above the 50 Ohm ± 5% tolerance window.

Soldermask dielectric loading shift: Non-uniform soldermask thickness over microstrips depressing characteristic impedance by 2 to 4 Ohms relative to field solver models without soldermask permittivity inclusion.

testcases.title: Differential & Single-Ended Microstrip Characteristic Impedance (Z0) Verification via Sampling TDR
testcases.instrumentation: Keysight DCA-X 86100D Wide-Bandwidth Oscilloscope with 54754A Differential TDR/TDT Module (or Tektronix CSA8300 with 80E04 TDR sampling head), 50-Ohm precision coaxial semi-rigid SMA test cables, calibrated torque wrench (8 in-lb).
testcases.pre_conditions: Coupon stabilized in metrology environment at 23 °C ± 2 °C and 45% ± 5% RH for at least 60 minutes. TDR system warmed up for 2 hours and calibrated using 50-Ohm precision termination standard (IPC-TM-650 Method 2.5.5.7).
testcases.procedure:
1. Connect channel 1 TDR step generator output to the coupon SMA launch pad using torque-calibrated SMA connector.
2. Configure incident step voltage to 200 mV with 35 ps (10%-90%) system rise time.
3. Establish TDR horizontal acquisition window to span 0 to 5 ns across the coupon trace (minimum physical trace length 100 mm).
4. Apply time-domain gating to exclude launch SMA transition (first 1.2 ns) and coupon open-circuit end reflection (last 0.8 ns).
5. Measure mean, minimum, and maximum characteristic impedance across the central 50 mm flat plateau region of the reflected waveform.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Single-ended microstrip characteristic impedance must evaluate within 50.0 Ohm ± 2.5 Ohm (47.5 Ohm <= Z0 <= 52.5 Ohm) across the gated plateau window. Reflections along trace must exhibit peak-to-peak impedance delta <= 2.0 Ohm.

testcases.title: Cross-Sectional Microstrip Physical Geometry & Dielectric Spacing SEM/Optical Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: Precision diamond wire saw, cold epoxy mounting vacuum pot, automated rotary polisher (down to 0.05 um colloidal silica), calibrated optical metallurgical microscope (Olympus BX53M) and Zeiss Sigma Field Emission SEM.
testcases.pre_conditions: Test coupon extracted from the production panel perimeter adjacent to the level-shifter daughtercard active array. Epoxy-mounted cross-section cured and polished to scratch-free mirror finish perpendicular to trace longitudinal axis.
testcases.procedure:
1. Align cross-section block on motorized stage under 500x-1000x calibrated optical/SEM imaging.
2. Measure base copper thickness (H_cu), trace bottom width (W_bot), and trace top width (W_top) to compute trapezoidal etch factor.
3. Measure dielectric core/prepreg thickness (H_diel) between trace bottom surface and underlying Layer 2 reference ground copper plane.
4. Measure soldermask thickness at trace crown (T_sm) and adjacent trace sidewalls.
5. Input measured physical dimensions into 2D electrostatic boundary element method (BEM) field solver and compare computed Z0 against empirical TDR findings.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Dielectric thickness (H_diel) within nominal ± 10% of stackup spec. Trace width top/bottom delta must not exceed 12 um (etch factor >= 2.5). Field-solver recalculated impedance must match TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-1-1-3-01 measured TDR value within ± 1.5 Ohm.
