# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Bandwidth Active Differential Probe & Oscilloscope Fixture Calibration

- **Task Hierarchy**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > Signal Integrity & Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB (50-Ohm Controlled Impedance Microstrips) [PCB & Hardware] > Microstrip TDR Impedance Metrology & Signal Integrity Eye-Diagram Validation [Metrology] > High-Speed Eye-Diagram Signal Integrity & Jitter Margin Verification [Metrology] > **High-Bandwidth Active Differential Probe & Oscilloscope Fixture Calibration** [Metrology]
- **Document**: [sop_differential_probe_fixture_calibration.md](./docs/sop_differential_probe_fixture_calibration.md)
- **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm Node

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Start: Equipment    │
│        Warm-Up         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Probe Deskew &     │
│  Nulling Calibration   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Fixture De-embedding  │
│   & S-Parameter Load   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Differential Signal   │
│  Acquisition & Metric  │
│       Validation       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Acceptance       │
│     Verification &     │
│        Sign-off        │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Thermal Stabilization & Environment Conditioning**:
   - Power on the digital storage oscilloscope and active differential probe amplifier system.
   - Soak for 30 minutes in a controlled cleanroom/lab environment ($23^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$, $45\% \pm 5\%$ RH).
   - Terminate oscilloscope channels into $50\ \Omega$ DC coupling.

2. **Probe DC Offset Nulling & Common-Mode Rejection**:
   - Clamp the active probe differential tips (`+` and `-`) to the zero-volt reference ground plane on the calibration substrate.
   - Trigger the internal auto-zero routine on the oscilloscope to cancel amplifier $V_{os}$ offset drift.
   - Verify differential nulling across common-mode levels up to the bitline precharge rail $V_{DD}/2$.

3. **High-Speed Channel Deskew & Step-Response Peaking**:
   - Connect differential tips to the fast-edge calibration pulse generator ($t_r \le 20\text{ ps}$).
   - Adjust digital delay registers on the oscilloscope to align positive and negative paths until channel deskew timing error $|\Delta t| \le 10\text{ ps}$.
   - Tune probe high-frequency damping trimmers/DSP filters to suppress overshoot and ringing.

4. **Fixture S-Parameter Extraction & De-embedding**:
   - Measure 2-port S-parameters ($S_{11}, S_{21}, S_{22}$) on the daughtercard 50-Ohm microstrip calibration trace standards (2x Thru, Open, Short).
   - Import the Touchstone `.s2p` fixture model into the oscilloscope de-embedding engine to push the measurement plane directly to the DRAM folded bitline pads (`BL` and `/BL`).

5. **DRAM Differential Signal Development Verification**:
   - Validate dynamic pulse sensitivity using test charge injection reflecting nominal cell storage capacitance $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$) dumped onto bitline capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$.
   - Ensure the calibrated acquisition chain faithfully measures differential readout signal swings of $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ with probe loading negligible relative to $C_b$.

---

### Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                        Acceptance Threshold Metrics    
                     ┌─────────────────────────────────┐
                     │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                  │
      C_b/C_s Rat Max┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                  │
                     │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
Fixt Return Loss (dB)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
    Diff V Error (mV)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                        │
                     │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                        │
 Deskew Residual (ps)┤█████████████████                │
                     │█████████████████                │
                     └┬───────┬───────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                      0       5      10      15      20 
```

| Metric Name | Target Value | Physical Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Residual Channel Deskew** | $\le 10$ | ps | Oscilloscope edge-transition deskew tool ($t_r \le 20\text{ ps}$) |
| **Differential Voltage Measurement Accuracy** | $\le 5$ | mV | DC/AC standard calibrator across $100\text{ mV} - 150\text{ mV}$ range |
| **Fixture Microstrip Return Loss ($S_{11}$)** | $\ge 20$ | dB | TDR / Vector Network Analyzer across signal bandwidth |
| **Bitline Capacitance Ratio Target ($C_b / C_s$)** | $5:1\text{ to }9:1$ (Max $10:1$) | Dimensionless ratio | Extracted from high-frequency fixture & layout metrology |

---

### Verified Literature Citations

1. **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
   - Bitline equalization to $V_{DD}/2$.
   - Differential readout voltage formulation:
     $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{cell} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right)$$
   - Expected differential signal level: $100\text{ mV}$ to $150\text{ mV}$ for $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$, $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$.
2. **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**:
   - Nominal storage node capacitance: $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$).
   - Bitline parasitic capacitance: $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ per 256/512 cell array block.
   - Operating capacitance budget ratio: $C_b / C_s$ kept between $5:1$ and $9:1$ ($>10:1$ causes severe read margin failure).
   - Cell area: Folded bitline $8F^2$ footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$).
3. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Access transistor dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
   - Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) with crown polysilicon or MIM structure and ONO or high-k $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$).
   - Storage target: $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$ with leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Fixture de-embedding (2x-thru / SOLT) must be calibrated up to at least the 5th harmonic of the fastest DRAM level-shifter slew rate (minimum 4 GHz bandwidth). Failure to account for active probe tip parasitic capacitive loading (typical Cin > 0.4 pF) will degrade risetime measurements on the 50-Ohm microstrips and skew high-speed eye margin evaluations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Active differential probe calibration requires verification of common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR > 30 dB across 1 GHz to 3 GHz) and deskew against the oscilloscope reference channel within +/- 5 ps. Direct solder-in tip attachments must maintain lead lengths under 1.5 mm to prevent tip inductance resonance within the measurement passband.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: COTS high-bandwidth differential probes (> 4 GHz active probe head, e.g., Keysight InfiniiMax / Tektronix TDP series) require proprietary matched tip consumables (damping resistors and elastomer contacts) with long lead times (6-12 weeks) and dedicated calibration fixtures (deskew / pulse generators) that must be secured under active metrology service contracts.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Calibration cycles must align strictly with the incoming PCB board bring-up schedule; uncalibrated probe fixtures block both TDR characterization and DRAM command/data eye-diagram sign-off, creating a critical-path gating milestone for Gen 2 PCB release.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Probe tip excessive capacitive loading (> 0.5 pF) suppressing high-frequency harmonics and artificially rounding transition edges on 50-Ohm microstrips.
1. Fixture trace loss and channel skew (> 15 ps) resulting in false eye-mask violations and erroneous jitter margin failure reports.
1. Improper probe ground/shield contact causing severe ringing, inductive peaking, and degraded CMRR during single-ended to differential signal conversion.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-3-3-1-01` | **Active Differential Probe Frequency Response and Bandwidth Attenuation Verification** | Keysight E5071C 4-Port ENA Vector Network Analyzer (100 kHz - 8.5 GHz), N4889A De-embedding Calibration Substrate / Fixture, Torque Wrench (3.5 mm SMA, 8 in-lbs) | 1. Connect active differential probe input pins to the calibrated 50-Ohm coplanar microstrip fixture output ports using 1.0 mm solder tips. 2. Terminate probe output into VNA Port 2 through appropriate matching attenuator. 3. Sweep forward transmission |S21| from 10 MHz to 4.0 GHz with -10 dBm input power. 4. Record the -3 dB cutoff frequency and gain flatness across 100 MHz to 2.5 GHz. | `-3 dB analog bandwidth must be >= 4.0 GHz; passband ripple between 100 MHz and 2.5 GHz must not exceed +/- 0.75 dB.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-3-3-1-02` | **Probe Fixture Channel Deskew and Slew-Rate Rise-Time Calibration** | Tektronix DPO70000SX 8 GHz Digital Phosphor Oscilloscope, Picosecond Pulse Labs 4015C Fast Pulse Generator (< 15 ps edge rate), 50-Ohm Precision Power Splitter, Agilent 11636B | 1. Feed 15 ps fast step pulse into precision power splitter. 2. Connect Channel A directly to oscilloscope reference port using phase-matched 2.92 mm coaxial cable (< 1 ps delta). 3. Connect Channel B to active differential probe seated in calibration fixture. 4. Measure time delta at 50% voltage transition thresholds between Channel A and probe output. 5. Adjust internal channel deskew register until alignment is achieved. 6. Measure 10%-90% rise time of calibrated probe channel. | `Channel skew after hardware/software adjustment must be <= 5.0 ps; measured 10%-90% rise time of step response must be <= 95 ps with overshoot < 8%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 cleanroom nitrile gloves (powder-free, static-dissipative), ANSI Z87.1 certified ESD safety glasses with side shields, ESD wrist strap connected to 1-Megaohm verified earth ground point
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with IPA, flush thoroughly with emergency eyewash for 15 minutes. In case of skin irritation, wash affected area with DI water and mild soap. If vapor inhalation causes dizziness, move individual to fresh air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized ESD fume extraction arm (minimum 50 CFM airflow rate) during solvent wipe and tip micro-soldering.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of IPA-saturated lint-free cleanroom wipes in sealed, dedicated, fire-rated hazardous solvent waste bins for proper incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.8%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (> 18.0 Mohm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Gold/Immersion-Silver (ENIG/ENEPIG) PCB test coupons cleaned with electronic-grade IPA wipe, free of organic flux residue and particulate contaminants.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Calibrated fixture interface clean, probe contact pads de-fluxed, stored in desiccant-sealed dry pack (< 10% RH) with protective terminal caps.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric oxidation and moisture absorption on microstrip fixture contact pads causing high-resistance ohmic contact (> 0.2 Ohm increase), generating contact noise and degrading TDR reflection accuracy.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical calibration and de-embedding verification of the high-bandwidth active differential probe and oscilloscope fixture, validating multi-GHz analog bandwidth, sub-5ps channel deskew, and touchstone S-parameter fixture modeling for DRAM level-shifter eye-diagram metrology.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PROBE_FIXTURE_CAL_REPORT_TC331.pdf`
- [ ] `ACTIVE_PROBE_S21_BANDWIDTH_SWEEP.csv`
- [ ] `DE_EMBEDDED_FIXTURE_S4P.s4p`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Active differential probe -3 dB analog bandwidth** | `4.0` | +0.5/-0.0 GHz | VNA transmission magnitude |S21| frequency sweep up to 5 GHz |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Inter-channel phase deskew residual error** | `0.0` | +/- 5.0 ps | Fast step response edge delay delta analysis on 8 GHz sampling oscilloscope |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Common-mode rejection ratio (CMRR) from 100 MHz to 1.5 GHz** | `35.0` | +15.0/-5.0 dB | Mixed-mode S-parameter Scd21 measurement using 4-port VNA |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Active differential probe and calibration fixture achieve valid S4P de-embedding file generation, -3 dB bandwidth >= 4.0 GHz, channel deskew within +/- 5.0 ps, and zero unresolved calibration anomalies verified by Lead Metrology Researcher.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: PRBS Pattern Transmission & 50-Ohm Microstrip Eye-Diagram Capture
**Hierarchy:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Firmware] > Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB [50-Ω Microstrip] > Eye-Diagram & Jitter Metrology  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type:** Make

---

### 1. Test Architecture & Signal Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  ESP32 / Pattern Gen   │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │ PRBS7 / PRBS15 Stream
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│ Level Shifter / Driver │ (1.8 V VDD Domain)
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │ 50-Ohm Controlled Microstrip
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Daughtercard SMA    │
│       Interface        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │ Matched 50-Ω Coaxial Interconnect
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Real-Time DSO / BERT  │ (50-Ω Internal Termination)
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Eye-Diagram & Jitter  │
│   Metrology Engine     │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Execution Procedure

1. **Hardware & Fixture Interconnect Setup:**
   - Mount the Signal Integrity & Level Shifter Daughtercard onto the test bench.
   - Connect the controlled $50\,\Omega$ microstrip transmission line output via SMA launch to the real-time Digital Storage Oscilloscope (DSO) or BERT using phase-matched $50\,\Omega$ coaxial cables (< 1 ps channel skew).
   - Set the DSO input channel coupling to DC, internal termination to $50\,\Omega \pm 0.5\,\Omega$, and establish baseline DC offset calibration at $V_{DD}/2 = 0.90\,\text{V}$ (for nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$).

2. **Pattern Generator & Clock Configuration:**
   - Configure the pattern source (ESP32 / dedicated pattern generator) to stream pseudo-random binary sequence patterns (PRBS7 / PRBS15).
   - Align the transmission clock frequency to the non-overlapping pump/readout operating range ($20\,\text{MHz}$ to $50\,\text{MHz}$ clock domains).
   - Enable daughtercard level-shifter rail voltages at nominal core $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ (and wordline high-voltage rail $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V}$ to $2.8\,\text{V}$ monitoring where applicable).

3. **Trigger & Continuous Eye-Diagram Acquisition:**
   - Configure the oscilloscope CDR (Clock and Data Recovery) PLL loop bandwidth according to the transmission rate.
   - Set persistent eye-diagram capture mode to accumulate a minimum statistical sample depth of $10^6$ unit intervals (UI) to resolve deterministic and random jitter.
   - Overlay the differential sensing eye mask against bitline sensing development limits ($\Delta V = 100\,\text{mV}$ to $150\,\text{mV}$).

4. **Metrology Extraction & Parameter Recording:**
   - Measure inner Eye Height ($V_{EH}$ at 50% UI cross point).
   - Measure inner Eye Width ($UI_{EW}$ between 20%–80% threshold crossing distributions).
   - Extract Total Jitter ($TJ$ at BER $10^{-12}$) and deterministic rise/fall transition times ($t_r / t_f$).

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
Acceptance Thresholds & Signal Margins (mV)
                        ┌──────────────────────────────┐
                        │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
Bitline Swing VDD/2 (mV)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
     Diff Margin dV (mV)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒                        │
                        │▒▒▒▒▒▒                        │
         Eye Height (mV)┤██████                        │
                        │██████                        │
                        └┬──────┬───────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                         0     225     450    675   900 
```

| Metric Parameter | Target Specification | Physical Units | Tolerance / Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transmission Line Characteristic Impedance ($Z_0$)** | **50.0** | $\Omega$ | $\pm 10\%$ ($45.0\,\Omega - 55.0\,\Omega$ via TDR) |
| **Dynamic Differential Eye Opening Height ($V_{EH}$)** | **$\ge 100.0$ to $150.0$** | $\text{mV}$ | Measured at nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$ across $C_{BL} = 250\,\text{fF}$, $C_s \ge 25\,\text{fF}$ loading |
| **Total Jitter ($TJ$ @ BER $10^{-12}$)** | **$\le 0.20$** | $\text{UI}$ (Unit Interval) | Measured across $20\,\text{MHz} - 50\,\text{MHz}$ clock rates |
| **Nominal Center Precharge / Baseline Voltage** | **0.90** | $\text{V}$ | Target $V_{DD}/2 = 1.8\,\text{V} / 2$ ($\pm 5\%$) |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**
  - Equalization and reference level: Bitlines equalized to $V_{DD} / 2$ ($0.9\,\text{V}$ at $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$).
  - Differential signal development: $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{cell} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right) \approx 100\,\text{mV} \text{ to } 150\,\text{mV}$ for $C_s = 25\,\text{fF}$ and $C_{BL} = 250\,\text{fF}$.
- **Source: High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**
  - System clock frequency range: Two-phase non-overlapping clocks driven at $20\,\text{MHz} \text{ to } 50\,\text{MHz}$.
  - Core supply voltage: Nominal $V_{DD} = 1.8\,\text{V}$; Wordline overdrive: $V_{PP} \ge 2.5\,\text{V} \text{ to } 2.8\,\text{V}$.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Storage node capacitance budget: Minimum $28\,\text{fF}$ per cell (baseline $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Transmitting high-speed pseudo-random binary sequence (PRBS-7/PRBS-15) signals from the ESP32 GPIO/SPI subsystem across a level-shifter daughtercard to 50-Ohm microstrips introduces substantial parasitic inductance at header pins and connector interfaces. If the board-to-board transition lacks continuous ground return stitching vias within 1.0 mm of signal pins, loop inductance will distort rising edges (<1.5 ns), inducing ground bounce that corrupts eye aperture and invalidates DRAM timing margin verification.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-frequency signal integrity verification requires proper de-embedding of coaxial launch cables, SMA end-launch transitions, and active probe tip capacitances (typ. 0.8 pF). If the oscilloscope input is terminated into high impedance (1 MOhm) rather than a calibrated 50-Ohm feedthrough termination, multiple transmission reflections along the microstrip will generate artificial standing waves, false inter-symbol interference (ISI), and completely obscure deterministic jitter components.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Custom low-loss Rogers or high-Tg FR4 (e.g., Isola 370HR) substrates with controlled dielectric thickness (+/- 5%) and precision 18 GHz SMA edge-launch connectors face extended lead times and volatile procurement lot variations in regional assembly fabs. Standard commercial FR4 exhibits uncontrolled loss tangents (tan delta ~0.02) and dielectric constant shifts (Er = 4.2 to 4.8) across production batches, demanding traceable coupon-based coupon impedance verification for every received panel.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Balancing high-bandwidth DSO (Digital Storage Oscilloscope >= 1 GHz) laboratory time against tight project milestones necessitates an automated PRBS pattern generation script and one-click eye-mask compliance measurement pipeline. Testing must not bottleneck daughtercard batch signoff prior to closed-loop motor stage integration and wafer-level DRAM timing characterization.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Impedance mismatch discontinuity (>62 Ohm or <40 Ohm) at connector launches creating severe reflected wave superpositions that induce complete eye-mask violations.
1. Excessive deterministic jitter (DJ > 120 ps) caused by cross-talk from adjacent digital switching lines or level-shifter power rail ripple exceeding 50 mVpp.
1. Transmission line dielectric absorption and skin-effect losses degrading PRBS rise/fall times beyond 2.5 ns, leading to severe vertical eye closure (<60% open eye height).

Configure DSO to trigger on recovered clock or software CDR (Phase-Locked Loop 1st order, loop BW = 1.0 MHz). 4. Accumulate persistence eye-diagram over 1,000,000 unit intervals (UI). 5. Measure horizontal eye width (ps), vertical eye height (mV), and total jitter (TJ at BER 10^-12). | `Eye Width >= 0.70 UI (>= 8.75 ns at 80 Mbps); Eye Height >= 700 mVpp (for 1.2V/3.3V translated swing); Total Jitter (TJ at BER 10^-12) <= 150 ps; Zero mask violations over 10^6 recorded waveforms.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-PCB-3-3-2-02` | **Time-Domain Reflectometry (TDR) Characteristic Impedance Profile** | TDR Sampling Oscilloscope / Vector Network Analyzer with TDR module (rise time <= 35 ps), 50-Ohm precision calibration kit (Open, Short, 50-Ohm Load), SMA torque wrench (5 in-lbs). | 1. Observe the reflected voltage profile and convert reflection coefficient (rho) to characteristic impedance Z0 along trace length. 4. Record baseline Z0 at trace midpoint, peak discontinuity at SMA launch, and termination pad landing. | `Microstrip characteristic impedance Z0 = 50.0 Ohm +/- 4.5 Ohm (45.5 Ohm to 54.5 Ohm) across entire active trace length; Connector launch discontinuity <= +/- 5.0 Ohm deviation.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD-safe conductive lab coat, Grounded dissipative wrist strap (1 MOhm series resistor), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Powder-free nitrile gloves (thickness >= 4 mil)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Remove contaminated clothing, flush skin thoroughly with clean water for at least 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush eyes immediately at eyewash station for >= 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek prompt medical evaluation. Inhalation: Relocate individual immediately to fresh air; provide artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operate chemical solvent cleaning of RF connectors and PCB pads inside an approved local benchtop exhaust hood or laminar flow booth with face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); maintain non-recirculating exhaust to exterior.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA cleaning wipes and solvent rinses in an airtight, grounded, FM-approved flammable solvent waste drum; do not pour into municipal drains; dispose through certified hazardous waste handler according to RCRA solvent disposal regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (> 18.0 MOhm*cm at 25 deg C) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold (ENIG) or Immersion Silver microstrip pads and SMA connector pins solvent-cleaned with IPA, de-fluxed, dried under dry N2 blow, free of particulate contamination and oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: SMA connectors capped with ESD-protective conductive dust caps; microstrip traces cleaned, desiccant-packed, and sealed in static-shielding moisture barrier bags (MBB).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Extended air exposure causes atmospheric sulfurization and copper/silver tarnishing on exposed RF launch pads, causing contact resistance spikes (>0.5 Ohm), attenuation degradation, and unpredictable RF reflection at >1 GHz.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verifiable delivery and acceptance of the 50-Ohm controlled impedance daughtercard microstrip under continuous 80 Mbps PRBS-7 data transmission, demonstrating full eye opening, compliant jitter boundaries, and nominal 50-Ohm TDR profile without signal integrity degradation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PRBS_EyeDiagram_Compliance_Report_TC_MCU_COTS_PCB_3_3_2.pdf`
- [ ] `TDR_Microstrip_Impedance_Profile_Data.csv`
- [ ] `HighRes_Eye_Persistence_Bitmap_1MUI.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |

| `ASSERT-01` | **Characteristic impedance of the daughtercard microstrip measured via 35 ps step TDR** | `50.0 Ohm` | +/- 4.5 Ohm | Calibrated TDR reflection coefficient analysis sampled at 10 ps increments across the 50 mm microstrip trace |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Horizontal eye width aperture under 80 Mbps PRBS-7 transmission over 10^6 unit intervals** | `10.0 ns` | -1.25 ns / +2.0 ns (Minimum 8.75 ns) | DSO eye diagram measurement at 50% threshold level with software clock recovery at BER 10^-12 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total jitter (TJ) at BER 10^-12 across 50-Ohm SMA microstrip output** | `85.0 ps` | +/- 35.0 ps (Maximum 120.0 ps) | Dual-Dirac jitter decomposition algorithm on 2.5 GHz DSO persistence waveform histogram |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 3 quantitative assertions strictly met with zero recorded mask violations across 1,000,000 PRBS unit intervals, confirmed by calibrated TDR impedance plot within 45.5-54.5 Ohms and dual-signed by Systems Engineer and Lead Metrologist.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Deterministic & Random Jitter Decomposition and Bit Error Rate Margin Metrology

- **Module / Level:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller > Signal Integrity & Level Shifter Daughtercard PCB (50-Ohm Controlled Impedance Microstrips) > Metrology
- **Generation:** Gen 2 (µm)
- **Action Type:** Buy (Equipment / Instrumentation Acquisition & Verification Protocol)

---

### Metrology Workflow

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Calibration and 50   │
│     Ohm Fixturing     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  TIE Acquisition and  │
│  Dual Dirac Fitting   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│       DJ and RJ       │
│     Decomposition     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  BER Bathtub and Eye  │
│   Margin Validation   │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Test Fixture Setup & 50-Ohm Line De-embedding**
   - Connect the real-time high-bandwidth digital oscilloscope (DSO) or bit error rate tester (BERT) using calibrated low-loss 50-Ohm matched coaxial cables and precision active micro-probes to the test daughtercard.
   - Perform full channel de-embedding (2-port S-parameters) up to the level-shifter daughtercard microstrip breakout to isolate daughtercard trace effects from test fixture parasitics.

2. **Acquisition of Time Interval Error (TIE) Waveforms**
   - Inject continuous synchronous read/write test patterns matching DRAM command/address and differential folded bitline readout bursts.
   - Capture a minimum record length of $10^6$ unit intervals (UI) to establish reliable statistical histograms of edge threshold crossings ($V_{DD}/2$).

3. **Dual-Dirac Model Decomposition (Deterministic vs. Random Jitter)**
   - Fit the extracted TIE probability density distribution using the standard Dual-Dirac model:
     $$TJ(BER) = DJ(\delta-\delta) + 2 \cdot Q(BER) \cdot RJ_{rms}$$
   - Separate total jitter ($TJ$) into:
     - **Deterministic Jitter ($DJ$)**: Periodic jitter (PJ), Data-Dependent Jitter (DDJ/ISI), and Duty Cycle Distortion (DCD).
     - **Random Jitter ($RJ$)**: Gaussian-distributed thermal and shot noise modeled as $RJ_{rms}$.

4. **Bit Error Rate (BER) Bathtub Curve & Eye Margin Extrapolation**
   - Project the bathtub curve down to target $BER = 10^{-12}$ using Gaussian tail extrapolation.
   - Evaluate horizontal timing margin at $BER = 10^{-12}$ and verify vertical voltage opening against the folded bitline sense amplifier differential readout threshold ($\Delta V$).

---

### DRAM Physical Budgets & Boundary Metric Baseline

```text
                    DRAM Signal and Parasitic Budgets   
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │░░                                    │
     Cb/Cs Ratio┤░░                                    │
                │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
 Bitline Cb (fF)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
 Storage Cs (fF)┤▓▓▓▓▓                                 │
                │▓▓▓▓▓                                 │
Sense SA dV (mV)┤████████████████████                  │
                │████████████████████                  │
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                0.0     62.5      125.0    187.5  250.0 
```

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Target | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Sense Amplifier Readout Differential Window ($\Delta V$)** | $\ge 100 \text{ to } 150$ | $\text{mV}$ | Cross-coupled inverter latch sense amplifier input at wordline assert; $C_s = 25 \text{ fF}$, $C_{BL} = 250 \text{ fF}$ |
| **Storage Node Cell Capacitance ($C_s$)** | $\ge 25 \text{ to } 30$ (Nominal: $28$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Stacked MIM/ONO capacitor over bitline (COB), $L = 180\text{ nm}, W = 220\text{ nm}$ |
| **Folded Bitline Capacitance Budget ($C_b$)** | $150 \text{ to } 250$ | $\text{fF}$ | Block array segment of 256 or 512 cells per folded bitline pair |
| **Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$)** | $5:1 \text{ to } 9:1$ ($< 10:1$) | Dimensionless | Ratio limit to prevent read margin and sense degradation |
| **Sub-threshold & Junction Cell Leakage Current** | $\le 1.0$ | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Measured at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh retention requirements |

---

### Context Citations

- **Source: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**:
  - Storage node capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF}$ to $30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$).
  - Bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ fF}$ to $250\text{ fF}$ across 256/512 cell array blocks.
  - Bitline-to-cell capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ strictly bounded between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (degrades severely if $> 10:1$).
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - $180\text{ nm}$ unit cell access transistor dimensions: $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) with ONO/high-$\kappa$ dielectric delivering $\ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$.
  - Junction and sub-threshold leakage limit $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **Source: Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:
  - Precharge equalization to $V_{DD} / 2$.
  - Developed differential voltage signal $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right)(V_{cell} - V_{DD}/2) \approx 100\text{ mV to } 150\text{ mV}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Jitter decomposition across the level-shifter interface between the 3.3V ESP32 host domain and the 1.8V 180nm DRAM memory bus must decouple power distribution network (PDN) induced periodic jitter (PJ) from transmission line inter-symbol interference (ISI). Without strict de-embedding of the probe fixture S-parameters up to at least the 5th harmonic (1.25 GHz for a 250 MHz bitline strobe), high-frequency deterministic jitter (DJ) will be misattributed to DRAM I/O pad slew mismatch, masking bitline sense-amp strobing margin degradation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At Gen 2 (µm-scale contact/aligner limits transitioning to 180nm silicon), bitline sensing margins are governed by a critical C_b/C_s ratio between 5:1 and 9:1. Unaccounted random jitter (RJ) exceeding 3.5 ps RMS on the latch-enable strobe truncates the differential bitline voltage development window (delta-V_BL < 150 mV), inflating the projected Dual-Dirac Bit Error Rate (BER) beyond the 1e-12 threshold and triggering soft-read failures during folded bitline precharge-equalize cycles.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Real-time oscilloscopes with hardware jitter decomposition packages (e.g., Keysight EZJIT Plus or Tektronix DPOJET with >= 4 GHz bandwidth and 20 GSa/s) and active differential micro-probes (> 4 GHz, < 0.5 pF tip capacitance) represent severe capital constraints and long calibration lead times (6-8 weeks) in regional Vietnam/Southeast Asia labs. Test fixtures must rely on standardized sub-miniature push-on (SMP) or U.FL micro-coaxial launches to avoid reliance on proprietary active probe sockets.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Jitter decomposition characterization and eye-diagram BER extrapolation must conclude within a 3-day sprint prior to taped-out daughtercard production freeze. Testing delays risk bottlenecking subsequent firmware calibration loops on the ESP32 closed-loop DRAM motor controller, jeopardizing the integration milestone for the open-source silicon bring-up.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dual-Dirac tail fitting divergence caused by insufficient sample depth (< 1e6 UI), underestimating total jitter TJ(BER=1e-12) and obscuring catastrophic data-hold violations on the DRAM input latch.
1. Ground bounce and parasitic inductance in single-ended return paths of the level shifter converting supply rail ripple into artificial data-dependent deterministic jitter (DDJ), falsely indicating transmission line microstrip impedance mismatch.
1. Probe-loading-induced capacitive peaking attenuating edge slew rates, artificially bloating data-dependent jitter (DDJ) by > 18 ps and falsely failing eye-mask compliance.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |

critics.systems_engineer: Jitter decomposition across the level-shifter interface between the 3.3V ESP32 host domain and the 1.8V 180nm DRAM memory bus must decouple power distribution network (PDN) induced periodic jitter (PJ) from transmission line inter-symbol interference (ISI). Without strict de-embedding of the probe fixture S-parameters up to at least the 5th harmonic (1.25 GHz for a 250 MHz bitline strobe), high-frequency deterministic jitter (DJ) will be misattributed to DRAM I/O pad slew mismatch, masking bitline sense-amp strobing margin degradation.
critics.domain_expert: At Gen 2 (µm-scale contact/aligner limits transitioning to 180nm silicon), bitline sensing margins are governed by a critical C_b/C_s ratio between 5:1 and 9:1. Unaccounted random jitter (RJ) exceeding 3.5 ps RMS on the latch-enable strobe truncates the differential bitline voltage development window (delta-V_BL < 150 mV), inflating the projected Dual-Dirac Bit Error Rate (BER) beyond the 1e-12 threshold and triggering soft-read failures during folded bitline precharge-equalize cycles.
critics.supply_chain: Real-time oscilloscopes with hardware jitter decomposition packages (e.g., Keysight EZJIT Plus or Tektronix DPOJET with >= 4 GHz bandwidth and 20 GSa/s) and active differential micro-probes (> 4 GHz, < 0.5 pF tip capacitance) represent severe capital constraints and long calibration lead times (6-8 weeks) in regional Vietnam/Southeast Asia labs. Test fixtures must rely on standardized sub-miniature push-on (SMP) or U.FL micro-coaxial launches to avoid reliance on proprietary active probe sockets.
critics.laya_pm: Jitter decomposition characterization and eye-diagram BER extrapolation must conclude within a 3-day sprint prior to taped-out daughtercard production freeze. Testing delays risk bottlenecking subsequent firmware calibration loops on the ESP32 closed-loop DRAM motor controller, jeopardizing the integration milestone for the open-source silicon bring-up.
critical_failure_modes: Dual-Dirac tail fitting divergence caused by insufficient sample depth (< 1e6 UI), underestimating total jitter TJ(BER=1e-12) and obscuring catastrophic data-hold violations on the DRAM input latch.

Ground bounce and parasitic inductance in single-ended return paths of the level shifter converting supply rail ripple into artificial data-dependent deterministic jitter (DDJ), falsely indicating transmission line microstrip impedance mismatch.
Probe-loading-induced capacitive peaking attenuating edge slew rates, artificially bloating data-dependent jitter (DDJ) by > 18 ps and falsely failing eye-mask compliance.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Automated VDD vs Retention Time Shmoo Plot Telemetry Engine

Software and hardware telemetry loop sweeping supply voltage and refresh pause intervals to construct 2D operational margin shmoo plots.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automating the VDD vs retention time characterization via an ESP32 host introduces significant latency, clock jitter, and ground-bounce vulnerability across GPIO-based command bursts. Bitline equilibration (V_EQ = VDD/2) and sense amplifier activation dynamics scale non-linearly below 1.5V in 180nm CMOS; the telemetry loop must synchronize sub-microsecond write/pause/read cycles without ESP32 FreeRTOS context-switch preemption injecting uncontrolled retention delays into the shmoo grid points.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm planar 1T-1C cells with folded bitline architecture, cell charge restoration requires the cross-coupled PMOS pair (SAP) to pull to full rail VDD while CSL remains open. If the programmable power supply (or on-chip LDO) steps VDD down too rapidly during active read-restore cycles, incomplete charge replenishment occurs, misrepresenting sub-threshold leakage as premature storage capacitor discharge rather than marginal sensing headroom.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying specialized high-resolution source measure units (SMUs) like Keithley 2450 or Keysight B2902B directly controlled over SCPI/UART limits bench-test deployment at the Vietnamese academic foundry partner; telemetry software must incorporate fallback drivers for cost-effective DAC/ADC instrumentation boards (e.g., AD5662 16-bit DAC + INA226 monitoring) without stalling Gen 2 timeline deliverables.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The telemetry engine schedule is compressed between bare-die wire-bonding handoff and tapeout review; allocating 3 weeks to firmware edge-case handling risks delaying wafer-level parametric sorting unless automated self-calibration test scripts and mock hardware HALs are delivered within Sprint 1.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Asynchronous ESP32 FreeRTOS tick interrupts distorting pause durations during refresh-disabled hold periods, creating false-positive bit retention failures.
1. Power-rail ringing during dynamic VDD stepping inducing sub-ground undershoot (>300mV) on bitlines, turning on parasitic NPN bipolar structures and collapsing unselected cell capacitor charge.
1. Destructive read-disturb masquerading as cell retention leakage due to improper sense-amplifier strobe timing (SAN/SAP assertion) at depressed VDD operating points (<1.2V).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-01` | **Automated VDD Margin vs Refresh Pause Retention Grid Sweep** | Keysight B2902B Precision Dual-SMU (VDD sweep 1.0V to 2.0V in 25mV steps, 10pA resolution), ESP32-WROOM-32D Development Board (SPI/GPIO interface at 20MHz), Rigol DS7054 Oscilloscope (10x passive probes on BL, /BL, and VDD rails), Logic Analyzer (Saleae Logic Pro 16). | 1. Telemetry engine commands programmable SMU to step VDD to target index (1.80V down to 1.00V in -25mV increments). 2. Write deterministic solid '1's and checkerboard patterns across a 4096-word sector. 3. Hold DRAM in unrefreshed idle state for logarithmically spaced pause duration t_pause (1ms to 10000ms across 40 steps). 4. Assert Row Address Strobe (RAS), activate folded bitline sense amplifiers (SAN pulled to GND, SAP to VDD), strobe Column Select Line (CSL), and burst read stored data back to ESP32 telemetry buffer. 5. Compare read data against written golden image, compute Bit Error Rate (BER), log CSV tuple (VDD, t_pause, fail_count, bit_map), and iterate until VDD=1.00V. | `Telemetry engine completes full 33x40 matrix (1320 points) without protocol hang; identifies retention waterfall boundary with monotonic retention time scaling (log(t_ret) vs VDD linear correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.94); zero bit errors reported at nominal VDD=1.8V for t_pause <= 64ms.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-02` | **Dynamic Supply Transient and Slew-Rate Verification during Read-Restore** | Tektronix MSO64B Mixed Signal Oscilloscope (4 GHz, 25 GS/s) with TDP1500 differential probes on DRAM core VDD pins, programmable fast-slew linear regulator driven by ESP32 DAC. | 1. Trigger continuous page-mode read accesses via ESP32 telemetry script. 2. Execute automated step command from 1.8V to 1.4V while monitoring supply rail dip during sense amplifier charge-restoration peak current. 3. Capture VDD rail droop (Delta V_DD) and overshoot using oscilloscope single-shot acquisition synchronized to CSL assertion. 4. Log telemetry engine ADC voltage readback against calibrated MSO measurement. | `Supply rail dynamic droop Delta V_DD <= 65mV during sense amplifier latching peak across all swept levels (1.2V to 1.8V); no supply ringing exceeding +/-5% of steady-state voltage; telemetry ADC report deviation <= 1.5% compared to scope measurement.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 10,000 / ISO 7 cleanroom anti-static nitrile gloves (ESD dissipative, minimum 4 mil), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Static-dissipative ESD lab coat (grounded via snap to cleanroom grid), Conductive heel grounders on ESD-rated dissipative flooring
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For IPA skin contact: Wash thoroughly with water and mild soap for at least 15 minutes. For IPA inhalation: Move subject to fresh air immediately; administer artificial respiration if breathing is labored. For eye splash: Flush immediately at emergency eyewash station with isotonic saline or copious sterile water for 15 minutes, holding eyelids open. Seek emergency medical attention if irritation or corneal clouding persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized elephant-trunk snorkel local exhaust ventilation (LEV) operating at minimum face capture velocity of 100 FPM (0.5 m/s) over solvent cleaning and ZIF socket defluxing station. Testing station operated inside cleanroom area with minimum 20 air changes per hour (ACH).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of IPA-saturated cleanroom wipes and cotton swabs in airtight, grounded, FM-approved flammable waste containers lined with static-dissipative polyethylene. Contaminated solvent rinses collected in designated HDPE solvent carboys for certified hazardous waste processing; no drain disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (electronic grade for socket and testboard cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Lead-Free Solder Rosin Flux Residue (from probe board rework)** | `65997-05-9` | Technical | `<1.0% surface deposit` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-dicing / post-wirebond open ceramic package with aluminum/gold bond pads inspected; Au/Al wire bonds intact; lead-frame free of particulate contamination and oxidation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Electrically validated, hermetically capped or nitrogen-purged desiccated carrier state with socket contact pins clean and zero flux/halogen contamination.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air exposure causes moisture adsorption and galvanic corrosion on 180nm bond pads and ZIF socket pogo-pins, inducing micro-ohm contact resistance shifts, false VDD IR-drop signatures, and bitline leakage skew during retention sweeps.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Firmware and telemetry pipeline delivering automated, reproducible VDD versus retention time 2D shmoo maps for the 180nm DRAM test vehicle, validating minimum operating VDD rails (down to 1.35V degraded retention, 1.8V nominal) and charge-restoration retention boundaries across 4096-bit arrays without human operator intervention.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_shmoo_telemetry_firmware_v2.bin`
- [ ] `retention_vs_vdd_shmoo_matrix_report.csv`
- [ ] `automated_shmoo_contour_plot.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Maximum retention hold time at nominal VDD (1.80V) before first single-bit error (FBE)** | `128 ms` | +/- 16 ms | Automated staircase pause-time search logged via TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-01 at 25.0°C |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Telemetry engine voltage stepping resolution and reproducibility across VDD sweep** | `25.0 mV` | +/- 1.5 mV | Keysight B2902B 4-wire remote sense SMU voltage readback cross-verified with internal ESP32 telemetry log |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum retention-retaining core supply voltage VDD_min at standard refresh period (t_ref = 64 ms)** | `1.45 V` | +/- 0.05 V | Binary search algorithm identifying 0-fail to 1-fail boundary on 4096-cell array |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful unattended generation of three consecutive, error-free shmoo characterization runs on five packaged 180nm DRAM Gen 2 dies, displaying monotonic retention degradation curves, zero telemetry communication dropouts, and documented sign-off approval from both Domain Expert and Systems Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-EFW-DRAM180-042`
**Title:** ESP32 DAC & Power Stage $V_{\text{DD}}$ Sweep Step Generator Calibration  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > Automated $V_{\text{DD}}$ vs Retention Time Shmoo Plot Telemetry Engine [Firmware & Software] > ESP32 DAC & Power Stage $V_{\text{DD}}$ Sweep Step Generator Calibration [Electronics & Firmware]  
**Technology Generation:** Gen 2 (180 nm / $\mu\text{m}$)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Scope and Objective
Calibrate and characterize the ESP32 internal Digital-to-Analog Converter (DAC) and external linear power stage used as the programmable $V_{\text{DD}}$ step generator for characterization and automated $V_{\text{DD}}$ vs. retention time Shmoo plot generation. The target system delivers a calibrated nominal $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ bias along with precise stepping down to sub-nominal voltages (to evaluate sense margins, $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right)$) and up to boosted rail levels for wordline pump margin characterization ($V_{\text{PP}} \ge 2.5\text{ V}\text{ to }2.8\text{ V}$).

---

### 2. Physical Setup & Calibration Flow

```text
  +------------------+       +-------------------+       +-----------------------+
  |  ESP32 DAC       | ----> | Linear Op-Amp /   | ----> | 180nm DRAM DUT Array  |
  |  (GPIO25 / DAC1) |       | Power Stage (Gain)|       | VDD Rail (C_s, C_BL)  |
  +------------------+       +-------------------+       +-----------------------+
          |                           |                             |
          +-------------------- Calibration Loop -------------------+
                               (Precision 6.5-digit DMM / DSO)
```

#### Step 1: Baseline Hardware Interconnect & Instrumentation
1. Connect ESP32 DAC channel 1 (`GPIO25`) to the input buffer of the external low-noise linear power amplifier stage.
2. Terminate the output of the power stage with an equivalent 180nm DRAM core capacitive load ($C_{\text{load}} \ge 10\text{ nF}$ decoupling network, representing array bypass capacitance) and a calibrated shunt load resistor.
3. Attach a 6.5-digit precision digital multimeter (DMM) and a 500 MHz oscilloscope (AC coupled, $1\text{ M}\Omega$ termination) to the output rail of the power stage.

#### Step 2: DAC Transfer Curve Offset & Gain Characterization
1. Step the 8-bit DAC code $D_{\text{in}}$ across its full span from `0x00` (0) to `0xFF` (255) in increments of 1 code step with a dwell time of $10\text{ ms}$ per step.
2. Record the steady-state output voltage $V_{\text{out}}(D_{\text{in}})$.
3. Perform a linear regression fit over the active linear sub-range ($V_{\text{out}} \in [0.8\text{ V}, 2.0\text{ V}]$ covering nominal $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$) to extract gain error $\alpha$ and offset error $\beta$:
   $$V_{\text{cal}}(D_{\text{in}}) = \alpha \cdot D_{\text{in}} + \beta$$
4. Program the calibration LUT (Look-Up Table) into ESP32 non-volatile storage (NVS) to ensure monotonic 10 mV to 25 mV step increments.

#### Step 3: Nominal $V_{\text{DD}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ and Intermediate Step Setting Verification
1. Command the calibrated generator to step through standard Shmoo evaluation points: $1.2\text{ V}$ (representing the threshold-loss level $V_{\text{DD}} - V_{\text{th}} = 1.8\text{ V} - 0.6\text{ V}$), $1.5\text{ V}$, $1.8\text{ V}$ (nominal $V_{\text{DD}}$), and overdrive targets.
2. Verify output settling time upon a step command transition of $\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ (typical signal margin range: $100\text{ mV}\text{ to }150\text{ mV}$).
3. Measure rail transient droop and ripple during simulated sense amplifier latching events.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Metric | Unit | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nominal Output Voltage Accuracy** | $1.800 \pm 0.005$ | $\text{V}$ | 6.5-digit DMM at DUT sense terminal |
| **Output Step Settling Time ($\Delta V = 100\text{ mV}$ step)** | $\le 5.0$ | $\mu\text{s}$ | Oscilloscope trigger at 90% target window |
| **Rail Ripple & High-Frequency Noise (0.1–20 MHz)** | $\le 3.0$ | $\text{mV}_{\text{p-p}}$ | AC-coupled 500 MHz DSO, bandwidth limited to 20 MHz |
| **Step Monotonicity & Differential Non-Linearity (DNL)** | $\le 0.5$ | $\text{LSB}$ | Monotonic sweep over $1.2\text{ V}\text{ to }2.0\text{ V}$ range |

---

### 4. Verified Literature Context & Source Citations
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**:  
  - Bitline precharge target is $V_{\text{DD}} / 2$.  
  - Signal development: $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{\text{BL}} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{\text{DD}}}{2}\right) \approx 100\text{ mV to }150\text{ mV}$ for $C_s = 25\text{ fF}$ and $C_{\text{BL}} = 250\text{ fF}$. Precise $V_{\text{DD}}$ stepping verifies sense amplifier margins at reduced differential signals.
- **High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**:  
  - Access transistor $V_{\text{th}} \sim 0.5\text{ V to }0.7\text{ V}$ (nominal $\approx 0.6\text{ V}$).  
  - Unboosted write cap loss: $V_{\text{DD}} - V_{\text{th}} = 1.8\text{ V} - 0.6\text{ V} = 1.2\text{ V}$ (33% loss).  
  - Boosted overdrive target: $V_{\text{PP}} = V_{\text{DD}} + V_{\text{th}} + \Delta V_{\text{overdrive}} \ge 2.5\text{ V to }2.8\text{ V}$.
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:  
  - Cell geometry: Channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.  
  - Minimum cell capacitance budget: $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ (leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at 85°C). Calibration ensures supply stability during retention sweeps.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: FPGA DDR PHY state machine must rigorously implement JEDEC initialization sequences (200 us CKE low, precharge all, MRS registers). Skew across high-speed DDR DQ/DQS matched traces must hold <= 10 ps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: PCB transmission line characteristic impedance must hold strictly at 50-ohm single-ended / 100-ohm differential (+/- 5%). Eye diagram opening at receiver must maintain >= 65% horizontal width and >= 200 mV vertical height.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Xilinx/Intel FPGA development carrier boards and high-speed SMA fixtures are standard COTS. Make is strictly restricted to custom daughtercard PCB layout, Verilog DDR PHY controller RTL, and firmware.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 32-60 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Jitter or power rail ripple on FPGA PLL induces intermittent read/write pattern errors during high-speed diagnostic telemetry sweeps).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Clock-to-data skew violating tIS/tIH setup/hold timing margin during DDR write bursts.
1. Power distribution network impedance resonance causing core VDD droop > 100 mV during simultaneous output switching.
1. Asynchronous clock domain crossing metastability in memory controller telemetry FIFO.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-1-01` | **DDR High-Speed Signal Integrity & Eye Diagram Oscilloscope Capture** | Keysight Infiniium 4 GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope with Differential High-Z Active Probes | 1. Probe DQ0-DQ7 and DQS differential strobe lines directly at DRAM test daughtercard receiver pins. 2. Accumulate 1,000,000 signal transitions into persistence eye diagram. 3. Extract horizontal eye width, vertical eye opening height, and RMS clock jitter. | `Eye width >= 65% UI (Pass); Vertical eye height >= 200 mV (Pass); Clock jitter RMS <= 12 ps (Pass).` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-1-02` | **March C- Algorithmic Memory Fault & Retention Telemetry Verification** | FPGA Hardware-in-the-Loop Diagnostic Firmware & Automated Python Telemetry Suite | 1. Execute March C- sequence: (w0), up(r0, w1), up(r1, w0), down(r0, w1), down(r1, w0), (r0). 2. Sweep retention pause times from 1 ms to 128 ms between write and read phases. 3. Stream per-address failure bitmap via UART/USB to telemetry logging engine. | `March C- 100% address pass at nominal 64 ms refresh window (Pass); Zero bit error rate (BER < 1e-12) (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD smock and grounded conductive wrist strap (1 MOhm safety resistor), Safety glasses with side shields during soldering and PCB prototyping, Nitrile gloves during circuit board solvent cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn first aid station: Cold sterile water irrigation, hydrogel burn dressing. For flux vapor irritation, move to well-ventilated fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Point-of-use HEPA/carbon solder fume extractor at soldering workstation (airflow >= 150 m3/h). Standard laboratory climate-controlled HVAC.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent solder dross and PCB trimmings in designated recycling bin for precious metal recovery. Solvent cleaning wipes in sealed flammable safety receptacle.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Lead-Free Solder Alloy SAC305 (Sn-Ag-Cu)** | `7440-31-5` | RoHS Compliant Electronic Grade | `Sn96.5 / Ag3.0 / Cu0.5 wire & paste` |
| **Rosin Core Solder Flux (Colophony)** | `8050-09-7` | Type ROL0 / No-Clean | `Internal wire core flux (< 3 wt%)` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade 99.9% | `Flux residue cleaning solvent` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `N/A` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `N/A`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Fabricated bare test daughtercard PCB with immersion gold (ENIG) surface finish.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully assembled, reflow-soldered, ultrasonic-cleaned, and impedance-tested PCB daughtercard.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Non-critical queue time. If bare PCBs exceed MSL shelf-life (> 168 hours in air), pre-bake at 125°C for 4 hours before reflow soldering to prevent PCB delamination and blistering.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of ESP32 DAC & Power Stage VDD Sweep Step Generator Calibration: High-speed FPGA DDR memory controller, 50-ohm test daughtercard PCB, and automated diagnostic firmware successfully achieve reliable read/write access and telemetry.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `FPGA_DDR_Controller_Synthesizable_RTL.tar.gz`
- [ ] `Controlled_Impedance_Daughtercard_Altium_Gerbers.zip`
- [ ] `Automated_March_C_Shmoo_Telemetry_Suite.py`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **PCB transmission line single-ended characteristic impedance (Z0)** | `50.0 ohms` | +/- 2.5 ohms (+/- 5%) | Time Domain Reflectometry (TDR) coupon measurement |
| `ASSERT-02` | **High-speed DDR data eye opening width at 200 MHz** | `>= 65.0% UI` | Minimum horizontal eye opening >= 60.0% UI | Real-time 4 GHz digital oscilloscope persistence eye diagram |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Algorithmic memory pattern test coverage (March C-)** | `100.0% address pass` | Zero single-bit faults across entire array at nominal VDD (1.80V) | Automated hardware-in-the-loop diagnostic firmware sweep |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

# Standard Operating Procedure: Variable Retention Pause & March Pattern Bit-Flip Audit Firmware

**Category**: Firmware & Software | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The ESP32 closed-loop telemetry engine operates over GPIO/SPI test interfaces with inherent microsecond-level timing jitter caused by FreeRTOS scheduler preemption and interrupt latency. If variable retention pause loops rely on software delay functions rather than hardware 64-bit microsecond timers or external programmable pulse generators, retention timing measurements will introduce systematic timing drift exceeding +/-5%, corrupting the parametric Shmoo retention boundaries at 180nm node targets (where sub-threshold and junction leakages are evaluated below 1 fA/cell).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node folded bitline (8F^2) architecture with a 28 fF stacked MIM/ONO capacitor, write/read margins are strictly dictated by C_b/C_s ratios (5:1 to 9:1). March C- or March SR patterns must account for physical row-to-row and column-to-column topological twisting. Applying generic linear address increments instead of scambled physical address maps will fail to trigger maximum worst-case bitline coupling capacitance (C_b crosstalk) and wordline disturb leakage across adjacent poly wordlines during extended pause intervals.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: The ESP32 microcontroller and associated level shifters (converting 3.3V logic to 180nm core 1.8V/3.3V I/O domains) must be sourced with automotive-grade temperature tolerances (AEC-Q100 Grade 2 or industrial -40°C to 105°C) to withstand prolonged thermal chamber runs during 85°C retention validation without thermal throttle or clock frequency drift.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Firmware audit iterations must not bottleneck physical tester throughput during multi-site wafer probe or packaged DUT validation. The firmware must implement on-chip streaming bit-flip compression (run-length encoded bitmap coordinates) over high-speed UART/USB to maintain telemetry reporting within the 30-minute test envelope per die index without causing memory buffer exhaustion on the ESP32 SRAM.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Software timer jitter on ESP32 causing non-deterministic variable retention pause intervals, resulting in artificial bit-flip tail distribution artifacts.
1. Logical-to-physical address mapping mismatch failing to excite worst-case topological bitline coupling during March pattern retention pause.
1. Level shifter ground-bounce and ringing during high-speed March pattern bursts corrupting write margins prior to the pause cycle.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-01` | **Variable Retention Pause March C- Bit-Flip Tail Distribution Audit** | ESP32 Closed-Loop Test Jig with 64-bit Hardware Timer Telemetry, Keithley 2450 SourceMeter (monitoring 1.8V VDD core at 100 pA resolution), Keysight MSOX6004A Oscilloscope, Espec Thermal Chamber at 85°C (+/-0.5°C) | 1. Initialize ESP32 firmware and establish telemetry sync at 921600 baud. 2. Execute March C- Phase 1: Write background data 0 across all 8F^2 array physical addresses 0x00000 to 0x3FFFF. 3. Assert hardware timer calibrated variable pause interval t_pause stepped from 10 ms to 1000 ms in 10 ms increments without refresh commands. 4. Read verify array (March C- read 0, write 1) and record failing address coordinates, bitline polarities, and bit-flip counts. 5. Repeat across inverse data background (Write 1, pause t_pause, read 1, write 0). 6. Stream run-length encoded bit-flip telemetry logs to host PC. | `Zero bit-flips recorded across all addresses at t_pause <= 64 ms at 85°C and VDD = 1.80V; bit-flip rate must follow an exponential log-normal tail with retention failure inflection >= 128 ms; hardware timer jitter must not exceed +/-5.0 microseconds across all pause steps.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-02` | **March SR Disturb Pattern & VDD Core Shmoo Voltage Sensitivity Audit** | ESP32 Controller, Keysight 34465A DMM (sampling VDD at 50 kSa/s), Programmable Low-Noise LDO Regulator with 1 mV step resolution, Thermal Chamber at 25°C and 85°C | 1. Set VDD core supply to target voltage step (starting at 1.350V). 2. Write checkerboard pattern (alternating physical BL/WL charges to maximize C_b/C_s noise). 3. Apply March SR disturb burst: Read target cell 10,000 times while pulsing adjacent wordlines at 10 MHz to induce subthreshold/gate-induced drain leakage (GIDL). 4. Apply 32 ms retention pause. 5. Read out full array status and map spatial bit-flip density. 6. Increment VDD core voltage by 25 mV and repeat across full operational voltage envelope up to 1.980V. | `Array must maintain 100% data integrity (0 bit-flips) at nominal VDD >= 1.620V under 10k read disturb pulses with 32 ms pause at 85°C; minimum operational VDD core cutoff (first bit-flip observed) must occur below 1.480V at 25°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor, ESD-safe lab coat, ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (mil thickness >= 4 mil) for solvent wipe-down
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Inhalation: Move exposed personnel to fresh air immediately. Eye Contact: Flush eyes with copious amounts of clean running water for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical attention if irritation persists. Skin Contact: Wash skin thoroughly with soap and water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics test bench with local snorkel extraction or benchtop HEPA/carbon fume extraction operating at a minimum face velocity of 50 ft/min during socket solvent cleaning.

1. Initialize ESP32 firmware and establish telemetry sync at 921600 baud.

# Standard Operating Procedure: March C- Pattern Sequence & Variable Pause Register Firmware Architecture

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The integration of an ESP32 closed-loop controller executing March C- pattern sequences directly against an open-source 180nm DRAM test vehicle introduces deterministic timing jitter on the GPIO/SPI/parallel bus interface. ESP32 FreeRTOS context switching and interrupt latency (typically 2-5 µs) risk violating DRAM access cycle boundaries (t_RCD, t_RP, t_RAS) during retention pause evaluation unless hardware timers (e.g., General Purpose Timer Module with high-resolution APB clock) and dedicated DMA or RMT/I2S parallel engines are mandated to hold bus timing within ±5 ns determinism.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: March C- consists of { ↕(w0); ⇑(r0, w1); ⇑(r1, w0); ⇓(r0, w1); ⇓(r1, w0); ↕(r0) } and provides full coverage for address decoder faults (AF), stuck-at faults (SAF), transition faults (TF), and unlinked coupling faults (CFin). To turn this into a retention Shmoo telemetry engine, the variable pause register must be inserted symmetrically between the complementary march elements (e.g., after ⇑(r0, w1) and ⇓(r0, w1)) while disabling auto-refresh lines. With a minimum cell capacitance target of 28 fF and junction/subthreshold leakage below 1 fA/cell at 85°C (retention target >64 ms), microsecond-level timing skew in the pause register will introduce unacceptable variance in the extracted retention distribution curves.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: COTS ESP32-WROOM-32E modules utilize internal flash and onboard crystal oscillators with typical frequency tolerances of ±10 to ±30 ppm over -40°C to +85°C. For precision Shmoo telemetry characterizing retention degradation up to 105°C, thermal drift in the local MCU oscillator directly translates to uncalibrated drift in pause register durations; external TCXO-stabilized clocking or periodic loop calibration against an IEEE-1588 / rubidium standard source must be incorporated into the BOM to ensure cross-batch repeatability.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Coupling the firmware architecture delivery directly to the physical 180nm silicon Shmoo gate introduces critical path dependency risk. The March C- variable pause engine must first be fully signed off in an automated Verilator/QEMU co-simulation harness utilizing synthetic DRAM behavioral models with injected leakage vectors, decoupled from raw wafer fab delivery timelines, ensuring test firmware maturity reaches 100% test coverage prior to tape-out probe testing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Asymmetric Subthreshold Leakage Bias: Inserting pause states only in unwritten or all-zero states masks data-pattern-dependent leakage (bitline-to-cell coupling vs. cell-to-substrate junction leakage), yielding false positive retention times.
1. MCU Interrupt Latency Jitter: FreeRTOS tick preemption during the variable pause execution window expands nominal pause times by up to several milliseconds, corrupting retention Shmoo plot boundary extraction.
1. Parasitic Refresh via Floating Wordlines: Firmware floating the row address strobes or wordline drivers during extended variable pause states enables subthreshold charge pumping into the 28 fF storage node, artificially prolonging retention decay.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-01` | **March C- Algorithmic Coverage and Deterministic Variable Pause Calibration** | Keysight MSOX6004A Mixed Signal Oscilloscope (4 GHz, 20 GSa/s), Agilent 16902B Logic Analyzer with active high-Z probe leads (<0.7 pF), Keysight 34465A 6.5 Digit DMM monitoring supply rails. | 1. Initialize ESP32 hardware timer with 10 ns tick resolution derived from 80 MHz APB clock. 2. Configure Variable Pause Register to 10.000 ms. 3. Execute Step 1: ↕(w0) across all 64K addresses. 4. Execute Step 2: ⇑(r0, w1) while triggering logic analyzer on wordline transition. 5. Trigger variable pause state with wordlines clamped low (V_WL = 0.0 V) and capture pause interval duration on MSOX6004A. 6. Execute Step 3: ⇑(r1, w0). 7. Execute Step 4: ⇓(r0, w1). 8. Trigger second variable pause state of 10.000 ms. 9. Execute Step 5: ⇓(r1, w0). 10. Execute Step 6: ↕(r0). 11. Sweep pause register from 1 ms to 200 ms in 1 ms increments, recording bit-flip error maps per iteration. | `All March C- state transitions must strictly adhere to the defined addressing sequence without skipped addresses. Pause interval duration measured by oscilloscope must match the register programmed value within ±0.05% (error < 5 µs at 10 ms pause). Zero bit-flip errors observed on calibrated reference SRAM block; DRAM retention decay curve must show monotonic failure inflection between 64 ms and 128 ms at 25°C.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-02` | **Automated VDD vs Retention Time Shmoo Telemetry Sweep** | Keithley 2450 SourceMeter (SMU) on DRAM VDD rail (measuring voltage and current down to 10 pA resolution), Keysight 34972A LXI Data Acquisition Switch Unit with K-type thermocouple attached to DUT package, ESP32 USB-UART high-speed telemetry link (921600 baud). | 1. Set thermal chamber to 85°C; soak for 15 minutes. 2. Program SMU VDD stepping loop from 1.20 V to 2.00 V in 20 mV increments. 3. At each VDD step, execute March C- with variable pause register swept from 1 ms to 100 ms in 2 ms steps. 4. Record number of bit-flip fail addresses, failure coordinates (row, col), and DUT quiescent current (I_DDQ) via SMU. 5. Telemetry engine generates 2D matrix of VDD vs Pause Time, color-coding pass (0 bit flips), partial failure, and complete array failure. 6. Repeat test cycle 3 times to verify reproducibility. | `Telemetry engine must log complete 41 x 50 grid (2,050 Shmoo points) without communication timeout or packet checksum errors. Measured retention time threshold at VDD = 1.80 V and 85°C must be >= 64 ms with array bit failure rate < 10^-5. I_DDQ during pause phase must not exceed 2.5 µA at 1.80 V.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 approved chemical splash goggles and face shield, ESD-safe cleanroom nitrile gloves (minimum 6 mil thickness, dual-layer), Static-dissipative cleanroom lab coat (Class 10,000 / ISO 7 compliant), Closed-toe ESD-safe footwear with conductive heel grounding straps
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing immediately; flush skin with copious water and mild soap for at least 15 minutes. Inhalation: Move affected personnel to fresh air; administer CPR if breathing ceases; provide oxygen if breathing is labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting without medical guidance; rinse mouth with water; seek immediate emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: All solvent cleaning of test boards and DUT socket fixtures must be conducted within a certified laminar flow chemical exhaust hood with face velocity of 100 ± 10 FPM (0.5 m/s); general testing lab must maintain at least 12 air changes per hour (ACH) with continuous volatile organic compound (VOC) monitoring.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent wipe materials and liquid IPA effluent must be collected in dedicated, grounded, self-closing FM-approved flammable waste containers; dispose of via certified hazardous waste remediation contractor under EPA/local environmental guidelines; no discharge into municipal wastewater drains.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (SEMI C12) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type I (>18.2 MOhm-cm at 25°C) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: DUT ceramic / open-cavity package contacts and test socket pins solvent-cleaned (IPA degreased, dry N2 blow-dried), free from copper/tin oxidation and particulates (organic contamination < 10 ng/cm²).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: DUT pins post-characterization inspected under optical microscope (50x) exhibiting zero pin deformation, no solder bridging, and contact resistance verified < 50 mOhm across all bus lines.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure limits causes atmospheric oxidation and moisture adsorption on open-cavity wire bonds and socket interfaces, inducing contact impedance spikes (>1 Ohm) that create reflection-induced bitline voltage sag and spurious bit-flip artifacts during March C- execution.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Delivery and empirical signoff of the deterministic March C- pattern sequence and variable pause register firmware integrated onto the ESP32 platform, capable of executing high-resolution VDD vs Retention Time Shmoo sweeps on the 180nm open-source DRAM chip test vehicle across operational voltage (1.2V-2.0V) and temperature (25°C-85°C) regimes.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `march_c_shmoo_telemetry_firmware_v2.bin`
- [ ] `dram180_retention_shmoo_matrix_85c.csv`
- [ ] `firmware_timing_verification_oscilloscope_report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Variable pause timer execution jitter measured across 10,000 consecutive cycles on GPIO hardware probe** | `0 ns` | ±50 ns | Keysight MSOX6004A high-resolution pulse width jitter histogram analysis triggered on pause entry/exit GPIO strobe |
| `ASSERT-02` | **March C- sequence full-address algorithmic coverage and fault syndrome isolation accuracy** | `100.0%` | 0.0% | Hardware logic analyzer state trace capture correlated against golden algorithmic fault dictionary |
| `ASSERT-03` | **DRAM retention boundary identification resolution at VDD = 1.80 V, Temp = 85°C** | `64.0 ms` | ±1.0 ms | Automated Shmoo script bisection search evaluating bit error count across step intervals |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Firmware compiles with zero warnings, executes continuous 24-hour uninterrupted Shmoo telemetry runs over 3 independent test silicon packages at 85°C without FreeRTOS watchdog reset or telemetry dropouts, and demonstrates 100% agreement between hardware-reported bit-flip locations and physical cell array fail maps verified via automated wafer-level ATE comparison.
