# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## March C- State Machine Register Architecture & Timing Parameter Specification

**Context Module:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller > Automated $V_{DD}$ vs Retention Time Shmoo Plot Telemetry Engine > Variable Retention Pause & March Pattern Bit-Flip Audit Firmware > March C- Pattern Sequence & Variable Pause Register Firmware Architecture > March C- State Machine Register Architecture & Timing Parameter Specification  
**Generation:** Gen 2 (µm) / 180nm CMOS  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Knowledge Document:** [march_c_state_machine_spec.md](./docs/knowledge/march_c_state_machine_spec.md)

---

### 1. Structural Architecture & FSM Execution Flow

The March C- test engine incorporates a variable retention pause step between upward and downward addressing passes to perform data retention audits and detect transition faults (TF), unlinked address decoder faults (AF), stuck-at faults (SAF), and coupling faults (CF):

```text
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│    IDLE / READY     │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│    M0: AnyDir w0    │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│   M1: UpDir r0 w1   │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│   M2: UpDir r1 w0   │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│   Variable Pause    │
│       t_pause       │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│  M3: DownDir r0 w1  │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│  M4: DownDir r1 w0  │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│    M5: AnyDir r0    │
│                     │
└──────────┬──────────┘
           │
           │
           ▼
┌─────────────────────┐
│                     │
│  DONE / Status Reg  │
│                     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

#### Capacitance Budget Context (fF)
```text
                    180nm DRAM Capacitance Budgets (fF) 
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 C_b Max (Bitline)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
 C_b Min (Bitline)┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒              │
                  │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒              │
C_s (Storage Node)┤█████                               │
                  │█████                               │
                  └┬────────┬────────┬───────┬────────┬┘
                  0.0     62.5     125.0   187.5  250.0 
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### Step 1: Memory-Mapped Register Space Configuration
Allocate the March C- FSM control and telemetry registers within the test controller boundary:

| Register Name | Offset | Width | Reset Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `MARCH_CTRL` | `0x00` | 32-bit | `0x00000000` | `[0]` Run/Start, `[1]` Pause Enable, `[2]` Step Mode, `[3]` Soft Reset, `[7:4]` Current Element State (`M0`-`M5`) |
| `MARCH_TIMING` | `0x04` | 32-bit | `0x00040804` | `[7:0]` $t_{RAS}$ min ticks, `[15:8]` $t_{RP}$ precharge ticks, `[23:16]` $t_{RCD}$ delay ticks |
| `MARCH_PAUSE` | `0x08` | 32-bit | `0x00000FA0` | Pause duration parameter ($t_{\text{pause}}$) programmed in units of clock cycles or timer ticks (up to $> 64\text{ ms}$) |
| `MARCH_ADDR_LO` | `0x0C` | 32-bit | `0x00000000` | Array start base address (Row/Col pointer) |
| `MARCH_ADDR_HI` | `0x10` | 32-bit | `0x0000FFFF` | Array upper bound limit (Row/Col pointer) |
| `MARCH_ERR_CNT` | `0x14` | 32-bit | `0x00000000` | Machine telemetry accumulator: cumulative bit-flip error count |
| `MARCH_FAIL_ADDR`| `0x18` | 32-bit | `0x00000000` | Telemetry latch: exact address of the first detected bit-flip mismatch |

#### Step 2: Timing Parameter Setup
1. Configure core timing parameters inside `MARCH_TIMING` to match 180nm folded bitline sense amplifier timing constraints:
   - Ensure bitline precharge ($t_{RP}$) and row-activation ($t_{RAS}$) cycle timings accommodate the folded bitline parasitic loading $C_b = 150\text{ fF to } 250\text{ fF}$ across 256/512 cells per bitline.
   - Maintain bitline-to-cell capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ strictly between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (nominal $C_s = 28\text{ fF}$, baseline range $25\text{ fF to } 30\text{ fF}$).
2. Program `MARCH_PAUSE` with calibrated duration $t_{\text{pause}} = 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to execute data retention stress testing.

#### Step 3: FSM March C- Pattern Execution
1. Assert `MARCH_CTRL[0]` to initiate the autonomous state machine:
   - **M0**: Write background data `0` through all addresses in any order: $\Uparrow\Downarrow (w0)$.
   - **M1**: Ascending scan order: read `0`, write `1`: $\Uparrow (r0, w1)$.
   - **M2**: Ascending scan order: read `1`, write `0`: $\Uparrow (r1, w0)$.
   - **PAUSE**: Transition to idle retention hold for duration $t_{\text{pause}}$ (wordlines deasserted, array bias preserved).
   - **M3**: Descending scan order: read `0`, write `1`: $\Downarrow (r0, w1)$.
   - **M4**: Descending scan order: read `1`, write `0`: $\Downarrow (r1, w0)$.
   - **M5**: Final read verification scan in any order: $\Uparrow\Downarrow (r0)$.
2. The state machine signals completion by raising `MARCH_CTRL[31]` (`DONE`) and asserting an interrupt line to the telemetry engine.

#### Step 4: Bit-Flip Audit & Shmoo Point Telemetry Extraction
1. Poll `MARCH_CTRL` until `DONE` flag is set.
2. Read telemetry registers `MARCH_ERR_CNT` and `MARCH_FAIL_ADDR`.
3. If `MARCH_ERR_CNT == 0`, log PASS status for the current $(V_{DD}, t_{\text{pause}})$ coordinate; otherwise, record fail count and fail address to map defect coordinates.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

1. **Storage Node Capacitance ($C_s$):**
   - **Target:** $\mathbf{25\text{ fF to } 30\text{ fF}}$ per cell (Nominal: $\mathbf{28\text{ fF/cell}}$) using a stacked crown or cylinder capacitor with high-k dielectric (EOT $= 3\text{ nm to } 4\text{ nm}$).
2. **Bitline-to-Cell Capacitance Ratio ($C_b / C_s$):**
   - **Target:** $\mathbf{5:1\text{ to } 9:1}$ (maximum ceiling $\mathbf{< 10:1}$) with folded bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ fF to } 250\text{ fF}$ across 256 or 512 cells per bitline.
3. **Data Retention Hold Time ($t_{\text{ret}}$):**
   - **Target:** $\mathbf{> 64\text{ ms}}$ at $\mathbf{85^\circ\text{C}}$ operating junction temperature with total leakage kept $\mathbf{< 1\text{ fA/cell}}$.
4. **Physical Cell Area Footprint:**
   - **Target:** $\mathbf{0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2}$ ($8F^2$ folded bitline footprint at feature size $F = 180\text{ nm}$, transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}, W = 220\text{ nm}$).

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Data cited:* Unit cell geometry $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; minimum storage capacitance of $28\text{ fF}$ per cell; sub-threshold and junction leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; crown-shaped polysilicon / MIM stacked capacitor over bitline (COB).
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Data cited:* 1T1C architecture with $8F^2$ or $6F^2$ layout; minimum capacitance budget $25\text{ to } 30\text{ fF}$ per cell ensuring retention $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; stacked capacitor with equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) of $3\text{ to } 4\text{ nm}$; bitline and wordline pitch of $360\text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$.
- **Source: 1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**
  - *Data cited:* Folded bitline $8F^2$ footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $F = 180\text{ nm}$); storage node capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF to } 30\text{ fF}$ (nominally $28\text{ fF}$); bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ fF to } 250\text{ fF}$ (for 256 or 512 cells per bitline); capacitance ratio $C_b / C_s$ maintained between $5:1$ and $9:1$ ($< 10:1$ upper limit).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integrating an automated March C- BIST/test state machine into the MCU telemetry loop requires synchronous handshake across the SPI/parallel memory bus interface. If the register map decouples the tRCD, tRP, and tRAS timing parameters from the core clock domain without synchronizer FIFOs or gray-coded address pointers, meta-stability will trigger invalid bitline sensing pauses, corrupting the retention Shmoo plot boundary telemetry.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: March C- algorithmic coverage {Up(w0); Up(r0,w1); Up(r1,w0); Down(r0,w1); Down(r1,w0); Down(r0)} strictly guarantees isolation of address decoder faults, stuck-at faults, transition faults, and unlinked inversion coupling faults. However, in an open-source 180nm stacked capacitor (COB) architecture with 28 fF capacitance budget, write-recovery timing (tWR) and wordline overdrive fall times (tFALL_WL) must be programmable down to 5 ns steps in the state machine registers to prevent false passes on write-disturb and sub-threshold drain leakage testing at 85°C.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-tight timing step-sizes (<1 ns) for the March C- state machine on standard COTS ESP32 GPIOs and discrete level shifters will lead to yield rejection or erratic telemetry due to pin capacitance (C_L > 15 pF) and PCB trace delay skew. Timing registers must accommodate realistic propagation delays from COTS drivers, or include an on-chip programmable DLL/delay-line macro supported by open MPW fab offerings.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable schedule requires direct co-validation of the timing register register-transfer-level (RTL) model with the automated VDD vs retention Shmoo plot firmware within Sprint 4. Unresolved ambiguities in register addressing, read-strobe widths, or variable pause duration registers will block the motor controller thermal chamber integration tests.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. State-machine race condition between wordline deactivate (tRAS timeout) and precharge activation (tRP) causing catastrophic bitline shoot-through and destructive cell discharge.
1. Address counter rollover phase jitter during Down(r0,w1) sequences causing false detection of coupling faults on adjacent 8F^2 folded bitline pairs.
1. Variable pause register overflow during extended retention-time audits causing premature state abort and truncated Shmoo data sets.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-1-01` | **March C- State Machine Timing Register Latency & tRCD/tRP Parameter Compliance Verification** | Keysight MSOX6004A 2.5 GHz Oscilloscope with 10:1 active differential probes (<0.8 pF load), Rohde & Schwarz RT-ZVC04 Multi-Channel Power Probe, ESP32-WROOM-32D Development Board running March C- telemetry firmware build v2.1.0. | 1. Reset state machine via MCU GPIO pulse (active low, 100 ns). 2. Assert BIST_START register bit via SPI write. 3. Monitor state-machine transition pin strobes (ACT, PRE, RD, WR) on oscilloscope channels 1 to 4 with 10 GSa/s sampling. 4. Trigger on initial Up(r0,w1) execution boundary and record 100,000 consecutive cycle timings. 5. Measure time delta from ACT rising edge (50% VDD) to RD rising edge (tRCD_meas) and PRE rising edge to ACT rising edge (tRP_meas). 6. Increment register values in 2.5 ns steps from 10.0 ns to 50.0 ns and record linearity error. | `Measured tRCD and tRP transition intervals must match programmed register values within ±0.75 ns absolute jitter; state transition error count over 100,000 March C- cycles must be exactly 0.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-1-02` | **Variable Retention Pause Register Dynamic Range & Bit-Flip Fault Extraction Shmoo Sweep** | Keysight 33622A Waveform Generator, Keithley 2450 SourceMeter (VDD supply monitoring with 10 nA resolution), Espec Thermal Chamber set to 85°C ± 0.5°C, Logic Analyzer (Logic Pro 16). | 1. Set March C- PAUSE_DUR register to 10 ms (representing initial refresh pause baseline). 2. Trigger March C- Down(r0,w1) bit-flip evaluation pass and log fail count via MCU telemetry engine. 3. Increment PAUSE_DUR register exponentially from 10 ms to 5000 ms across 50 discrete logarithmic steps. 4. At each step, sweep VDD from 2.00 V down to 1.20 V in 20 mV decrements. 5. Capture bit failure bitmap array and log retention fail threshold boundaries directly into host telemetry CSV. | `State machine must cleanly resume execution from pause without skipped address cycles (verified by 16-bit address continuous countdown sequence); Shmoo plot must resolve retention limits with monotonic degradation profile (R^2 > 0.985) and zero register stall timeouts across all 50 pause steps.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level-2 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (ASTM D6319), ANSI Z87.1 UV-blocking & Impact Side-Shield Safety Eyewear, ESD-safe dissipative static control coat (surface resistance 10^6 - 10^9 ohms/sq), Conductive heel grounding straps with 1 Megohm resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact with IPA: Flush eyes immediately with copious amounts of clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids apart; obtain medical attention. Skin contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and water; remove contaminated dissipative clothing. Inhalation: Move personnel to fresh clean air environment immediately; administer oxygen if respiration becomes labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop chemical fume extractor with activated carbon cartridge and HEPA stage maintaining laminar face velocity >= 100 fpm (0.51 m/s); laboratory room air exchange minimum 12 volume turnovers per hour under positive differential pressure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA rinse solutions must be segregated into designated flammable solvent hazardous waste carboys; seal tightly and label per EPA Title 40 CFR 261.21 (D001 ignitable); never drain down cleanroom sewer systems.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.8%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly etched contact pads and metal-1 interconnect strapping post-solvent clean (no organic residues, organic film thickness < 0.5 nm via spectroscopic ellipsometry).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Enclosed in hermetic test socket fixture under continuous dry N2 purge (RH < 5%, oxygen level < 50 ppm) or vacuum transfer carrier prior to microprobe landing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Native oxide (Al2O3) growth and atmospheric moisture chemisorption on probe contact pads exceeding 2.0 nm thickness, inducing contact resistance non-linearities (R_contact > 15 ohms) that distort high-frequency March C- state machine timing strobe transitions.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete RTL architecture and timing parameter specification for the open-source 180nm DRAM March C- test state machine, featuring programmable sub-nanosecond timing delay registers, variable pause retention audit control, and verified Shmoo plot boundary extraction across 1.2V-2.0V VDD and 25°C-85°C thermal envelopes.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `march_c_state_machine_reg_spec_v2.pdf`
- [ ] `timing_param_shmoo_telemetry_dataset.csv`
- [ ] `state_machine_probe_jitter_constellation.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **March C- state machine timing register propagation delay linearity error across tRCD, tRP, and tWR ranges** | `0.50` | ±0.20 ns | High-bandwidth 2.5 GHz oscilloscope time-interval error (TIE) histogram analysis across 100,000 BIST cycles |
| `ASSERT-02` | **State machine retention pause duration accuracy from 10 ms to 5000 ms** | `100.0` | ±0.5 % | Precision frequency counter/timer gated interval measurement synced to MCU BIST_PAUSE_BUSY strobe |
| `ASSERT-03` | **March C- sequence fault-detection coverage for stuck-at, transition, and unlinked inversion coupling faults on 64-kbit DRAM array** | `100.0` | +0.0% / -0.0% | Automated synthetic fault-injection netlist simulation correlated with physical probe bitmap error logs |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All quantitative assertions verified across 5 distinct test macro dies at both 25°C and 85°C; complete absence of state machine lockup or timing jitter violations; signoff approval recorded by Lead Systems Engineer, Circuit Design Lead, and Fab Integration PM.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Variable Pause Refresh-Suppression Timer & BIST Microcode Core Implementation

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Coupling an ESP32 closed-loop controller firmware domain to an on-chip 180nm BIST microcode core requires strict synchronization and clock-domain crossing (CDC) isolation. Driving variable retention pause via asynchronous register writes risks metastability in the refresh inhibition state machine, potentially truncating precharge cycles or corrupting row-hammer mitigations during high-frequency March C- sequences.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm planar node, DRAM storage cell capacitance (~25-35 fF) retention is dominated by junction leakage (band-to-band tunneling and trap-assisted recombination) and subthreshold leakage through the access transistor. The variable pause suppression timer must guarantee microsecond-granularity pause step intervals (100 µs to 10 s) with sub-1% jitter to prevent statistical blurring of retention tail distributions and unrefreshable bit-flip mapping.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing custom microcode ROM/SRAM for the BIST engine in 180nm CMOS demands dedicated silicon area and verified foundry standard cells. If reliant on external COTS ESP32-WROOM-32E modules for pattern orchestration, procurement delays, transceiver pin-level speed limitations (GPIO slew rates < 50 MHz), and socket mechanical wear on test fixtures threaten qualification throughput.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Balancing research test flexibility with tapeout schedule constraints is critical. The engineering team must avoid feature creep in the BIST microcode instruction decoder; firmware architecture should prioritize hardwired March C- primitives with parameterized pause registers over a fully Turing-complete micro-sequencer to preserve the Q3 milestone.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Refresh timer race condition causing unintentional self-refresh trigger during active retention pause state, invalidating empirical cell decay timing.
1. Access transistor gate dielectric breakdown or threshold drift during prolonged pause-state bias stress, masking retention leakage with gate leakage.
1. ESP32 GPIO timing skew and capacitive ringing exceeding setup/hold margins on external BIST control lines, corrupting March C- state machine transitions.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-2-01` | **Variable Retention Pause Suppression Timer Linearity and Jitter Verification** | Keysight DSOX6004A 6 GHz Digital Storage Oscilloscope, Rohde & Schwarz HMP4040 Programmable DC Power Supply, Rigol DG4162 Arbitrary Waveform Generator, ESP32-WROOM-32E Test Fixture. | 1. Initialize ESP32 test engine and configure the BIST register via SPI/parallel bus with pause suppression times spanning 1.0 ms to 1000.0 ms in logarithmic steps (1.0 ms, 5.0 ms, 10.0 ms, 50.0 ms, 100.0 ms, 500.0 ms, 1000.0 ms). 2. For each step, trigger a March C- sequence with refresh suppression enabled. 3. Measure the high-pulse duration and edge-to-edge jitter of REFRESH_SUPPRESS_ACTIVE signal over 1,000 consecutive iterations on the oscilloscope. 4. Log measured interval mean, standard deviation, and maximum deviation across all programmed values. | `Measured pause duration error must be ≤ ±0.2% of programmed value across all ranges; peak-to-peak timing jitter must remain < 50 ns (≤ 0.005% at 1 ms baseline); zero instances of spurious refresh clock pulses detected during suppression high window.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-2-02` | **March C- Bit-Flip Detection and Shmoo Boundary Extraction under Modulated VDD** | Keysight E36313A Precision Triple-Output DC Power Supply, NI-DAQ USB-6363 Telemetry Interface, Agilent 16902B Logic Analyzer, Temptronic TP04300 ThermoStream Thermal Chamber (-40 °C to +125 °C). | 1. Sweep DUT core supply voltage VDD from 1.80 V down to 1.10 V in 20 mV increments using the programmable power supply. 2. At each voltage step, sweep the retention pause register from 10 ms to 500 ms in 10 ms increments. 3. Execute the full March C- pattern; the internal BIST comparator flags and logs bit-flip error counts and failing row/column addresses. 4. Stream telemetry packets to host PC and generate the 2D Shmoo plot (VDD vs. Retention Pause Time). | `BIST microcode correctly reports 100% data pass (0 bit flips) across all 64 kb array addresses at nominal VDD = 1.80 V with pause ≤ 64 ms at 85 °C; Shmoo boundary monotonic transition profile verified with telemetry packet checksum failure rate = 0.00%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-blocking safety glasses, Cleanroom nitrile gloves (Class 100/ISO 5 compatible, minimum 6 mil thickness), ESD-safe dissipative lab coat, Grounding heel straps and ESD wrist strap with 1 MOhm current-limiting resistor
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of eye contact with IPA, rinse immediately with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes at the eyewash station. In case of inhalation, remove subject to fresh air immediately; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. In case of skin exposure, flush with soap and water and remove contaminated clothing.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop chemical cleaning and flux-off degreasing must be performed under an active certified ductless laminar flow fume hood with minimum 100 fpm face velocity; test chamber thermal exhaust vented directly to exterior building facilities.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent waste (IPA) must be segregated in dedicated, clearly labeled flammable-liquid safety cans with flame arrestors; no disposal into sanitary sewer drains; hazardous organic liquid waste scheduled for EPA/DOT-compliant solvent recycling or high-temperature incineration.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DI Water)** | `7732-18-5` | Type 1 Reagent Grade (18.2 MOhm·cm resistivity) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Die bonded, aluminum ultrasonic wire-bonds intact, leadframe pristine with zero organic residue or oxidation on contact pads (contact angle < 15° with DI water).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hermetically encapsulated or dry-box stored packaged IC with desiccated silicone conformal coat cured, leadframe pins free from corrosion and tin-whiskers.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric humidity absorption induces intermetallic corrosion at gold-aluminum wire bond interfaces (Kirkendall void acceleration) and alters board-level high-impedance leakage paths, causing spurious retention measurement failures.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full physical and functional signoff of the Variable Pause Refresh-Suppression Timer and BIST Microcode Core within the 180nm DRAM test vehicle, validating deterministic sub-1% timer accuracy, automated March C- execution, and direct Shmoo telemetry extraction via ESP32 interface.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `bist_microcode_core_layout_gds_v2_1.gds`
- [ ] `march_c_shmoo_retention_telemetry_dataset.csv`
- [ ] `timer_linearity_jitter_validation_report.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-MCU-SHMOO-01` | **Refresh suppression timer duration accuracy across full programmable dynamic range (1 ms to 1000 ms)** | `100.00%` | ±0.20% | High-bandwidth digital oscilloscope edge time-interval analysis over 1,000 continuous trigger events |
| `ASSERT-MCU-SHMOO-02` | **March C- address sequencing and fault coverage verification under continuous BIST execution** | `100.00%` | 0.00% (Zero fault escape on stuck-at, transition, and coupling fault injections) | Automated logic analyzer trace decode matched against Golden RTL simulation vector outputs |
| `ASSERT-MCU-SHMOO-03` | **Telemetry throughput rate and packet delivery reliability over ESP32 UART interface during continuous 24-hour burn-in** | `921600 baud (100.00% packet integrity)` | Zero dropped frames; packet CRC32 error rate < 1e-8 | Host automated telemetry daemon CRC-checking and frame counter audit over 86,400 consecutive test cycles |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Physical DRC/LVS clearance of the BIST core silicon IP in 180nm design rules, 100% validation of all quantitative assertions on hardware test fixtures, zero unhandled CDC warnings in gate-level timing simulations, and formal signoff by Council Lead Researchers.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): RTL Design of Variable Pause Refresh Timer & BIST Microcode Sequencer

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > Automated VDD vs Retention Time Shmoo Plot Telemetry Engine [Firmware & Software] > Variable Retention Pause & March Pattern Bit-Flip Audit Firmware [Firmware & Software] > March C- Pattern Sequence & Variable Pause Register Firmware Architecture [Circuit Design] > Variable Pause Refresh-Suppression Timer & BIST Microcode Core Implementation [Circuit Design] > RTL Design of Variable Pause Refresh Timer & BIST Microcode Sequencer [Circuit Design]
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Wirebond Shear >= 18 gf, ATE Functional Yield >= 90%, Coplanarity <= 0.08 mm.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Dage 4000 Bond Tester & Advantest Wafer Prober / CMM.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: FPGA DDR PHY state machine must rigorously implement JEDEC initialization sequences (200 us CKE low, precharge all, MRS registers). Skew across high-speed DDR DQ/DQS matched traces must hold <= 10 ps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: PCB transmission line characteristic impedance must hold strictly at 50-ohm single-ended / 100-ohm differential (+/- 5%). Eye diagram opening at receiver must maintain >= 65% horizontal width and >= 200 mV vertical height.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Xilinx/Intel FPGA development carrier boards and high-speed SMA fixtures are standard COTS. Make is strictly restricted to custom daughtercard PCB layout, Verilog DDR PHY controller RTL, and firmware.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 32-60 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Jitter or power rail ripple on FPGA PLL induces intermittent read/write pattern errors during high-speed diagnostic telemetry sweeps).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Clock-to-data skew violating tIS/tIH setup/hold timing margin during DDR write bursts.
1. Power distribution network impedance resonance causing core VDD droop > 100 mV during simultaneous output switching.
1. Asynchronous clock domain crossing metastability in memory controller telemetry FIFO.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

Probe DQ0-DQ7 and DQS differential strobe lines directly at DRAM test daughtercard receiver pins. 2. Accumulate 1,000,000 signal transitions into persistence eye diagram. 3. Execute March C- sequence: (w0), up(r0, w1), up(r1, w0), down(r0, w1), down(r1, w0), (r0). 2. Sweep retention pause times from 1 ms to 128 ms between write and read phases. 3. Stream per-address failure bitmap via UART/USB to telemetry logging engine. | `March C- 100% address pass at nominal 64 ms refresh window (Pass); Zero bit error rate (BER < 1e-12) (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Anti-static ESD smock and grounded conductive wrist strap (1 MOhm safety resistor), Safety glasses with side shields during soldering and PCB prototyping, Nitrile gloves during circuit board solvent cleaning
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burn first aid station: Cold sterile water irrigation, hydrogel burn dressing. For flux vapor irritation, move to well-ventilated fresh air.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Mixed-Signal Transient Co-Simulation & Timing Verification of Refresh Inhibit Window

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > Automated VDD vs Retention Time Shmoo Plot Telemetry Engine [Firmware & Software] > Variable Retention Pause & March Pattern Bit-Flip Audit Firmware [Firmware & Software] > March C- Pattern Sequence & Variable Pause Register Firmware Architecture [Circuit Design] > Variable Pause Refresh-Suppression Timer & BIST Microcode Core Implementation [Circuit Design] > Mixed-Signal Transient Co-Simulation & Timing Verification of Refresh Inhibit Window [Circuit Design]
**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Wirebond Shear >= 18 gf, ATE Functional Yield >= 90%, Coplanarity <= 0.08 mm.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Dage 4000 Bond Tester & Advantest Wafer Prober / CMM.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Co-simulation between digital RTL (ESP32/BIST microcode controller running March C-) and analog SPICE netlists (folded-bitline sense amplifier, wordline driver, and 1T1C storage cell array at 180nm) faces acute convergence issues and timescale divergence. The digital controller operates on a microsecond-to-millisecond retention pause timescale, while bitline differential sensing (delta V = 100 mV to 150 mV) and sense amp cross-coupled latching (SAN/SAP assertion) require picosecond-scale transient resolution. Verifying the refresh-inhibit window requires behavioral modeling of long pause intervals coupled with transient SPICE evaluation at the exact boundaries of inhibit assertion and de-assertion to prevent race conditions without incurring prohibitive simulation runtimes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm with VDD = 1.8V, disabling auto-refresh during the variable pause window risks bitline float and subthreshold leakage degradation (target I_off <= 10 pA/um at V_GS = 0V, V_thn = 0.55V). If the wordline (WL) falls prematurely or fails to reach full boost level, or if the bitline equalization network (V_DD/2 = 0.9V) floats during prolonged inhibit, trapped charge on C_s (25 fF) deteriorates below the minimum differential sensing margin (50 mV minimum latching threshold). Transient co-simulation must specifically sweep temperature (up to 85°C junction) and process corners (SS, TT, FF) across the maximum pause register duration to guarantee differential signal development delta V >= 100 mV upon resume.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: The ESP32-based shmoo telemetry engine relies on standard commercial off-the-shelf microcontrollers and external DAC/ADC interface boards. Sourcing mixed-signal co-simulation tool licenses (e.g., Cadence Spectre-Xcelium or open-source Verilog-A / ngspice / dssim co-simulation environments) along with calibrated BSIM4 foundry models for open 180nm PDKs introduces tooling friction. If using open-source flows (cocotb + ngspice/xyce), automated harness scripts must be rigorously pinned to specific commit hashes to ensure reproducible regression across multi-site testbenches.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The verification of the refresh-inhibit window sits on the critical path connecting firmware microcode validation and physical silicon sign-off. Milestone gating requires automated pass/fail assertion reports from the mixed-signal harness within 48 hours of register spec freeze. Any ambiguous boundary conditions or meta-stability during pause-state entry/exit directly risks silicon refabrication costs ($15,000+ per multi-project wafer run) and a 12-week schedule delay.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Metastable Bitline Readout: Wordline activation upon exiting the refresh inhibit window occurs before the bitline equalization switch fully turns off, causing BL and /BL imbalance and corrupting the stored 25 fF cell charge.
1. Sneak Subthreshold Leakage Discharge: At elevated junction temperature (85°C), subthreshold leakage across access transistor (W/L = 2.0 um / 0.18 um) exceeds 50 pA/um during an extended inhibit window, discharging cell voltage below the sense amplifier differential resolution limit (50 mV).
1. Control Boundary Asynchrony / Race Condition: BIST March C- microcode issues a wordline strobe concurrently with the asynchronous timer de-asserting the refresh-inhibit flag, causing glitch-induced partial wordline turn-on and catastrophic multi-row disturb.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-2-2-01` | **Mixed-Signal Transient Timing Verification of Refresh Inhibit Assertion & De-Assertion Boundaries** | Mixed-signal simulator (Ngspice v42+ coupled with Cocotb/Verilog-A harness), High-resolution waveform viewer (GTKWave), Virtual current and voltage probes on WL[0], BL, /BL, EQ, and SAN/SAP nets. | 1. Assert digital refresh-inhibit register flag via BIST testbench harness at t = 10.0 us. 2. Advance transient simulation through variable pause duration (10 ms hold in behavioral low-power state). 3. Apply wake-up strobe to de-assert refresh inhibit and trigger row read/refresh cycle on WL[0] at t = 10.01 ms. 4. Record differential bitline voltage (V_BL - V_/BL) at 50 ps timestep resolution during sense amplifier enable (SAN pull-down, SAP pull-up). 5. Measure setup time between EQ turn-off and WL turn-on, and hold time before SAN assertion. | `Setup time from EQ falling below 0.18V to WL rising above 1.62V must be >= 2.5 ns. Wordline risetime (10% to 90%) must be <= 1.2 ns. Sense amp differential voltage delta V at SAN assertion must be >= 100 mV with zero bit-flip errors observed on the March C- readout data bus.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-1-2-2-02` | **Variable Retention Pause Duration vs VDD Voltage Shmoo Characterization Co-Simulation** | Automated Python-driven Ngspice/Verilog transient co-simulation batch runner, parametric sweep data logger, virtual automated shmoo telemetry matrix generator. | 1. Configure parametric outer loop: sweep VDD from 1.50V to 2.00V in 50 mV steps. 2. Configure parametric inner loop: sweep refresh inhibit pause duration from 1.0 ms to 100.0 ms in logarithmic intervals (1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 50.0, 100.0 ms). 3. For each (VDD, pause_time) coordinate, run mixed-signal transient simulation executing March C- read audit. 4. Measure residual cell storage voltage immediately prior to WL assertion, and monitor sense amplifier differential latching outcome (pass = correct bit 1 read, fail = latched to 0 or metastable). 5. Generate 2D shmoo retention plot data matrix. | `At nominal VDD = 1.80V, 85°C (TT corner), retention pause time must sustain >= 32.0 ms with zero bit flips. Critical cell residual voltage before sensing must remain >= 1.15V (guaranteeing delta V >= 95 mV across C_BL = 250 fF). Shmoo boundary must exhibit monotonic degradation without abrupt discontinuity caused by timer logic glitches.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level 1 ESD-safe anti-static wrist strap (1 MOhm series resistor), ANSI Z87.1 approved clear safety glasses, Powder-free cleanroom-grade nitrile gloves (4 mil thickness)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact with IPA solvent, flush affected skin immediately with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes and remove contaminated garments. In case of eye contact, flush thoroughly at certified eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmologic evaluation if irritation persists. In case of nitrogen asphyxiation hazard, evacuate victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Standard electronics lab bench environment equipped with local dedicated ductless fume extraction / solvent vapor canopy hood rated at minimum 100 FPM face velocity for benchtop IPA substrate cleaning. Clean dry air (CDA) or nitrogen line pressure regulated at 20-30 PSI with safety relief valves.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA cleanroom wipes and contaminated swab applicators must be disposed of in dedicated, airtight, FM-approved flammable waste containers lined with static-dissipative polyethylene bags. Liquid IPA effluent must be collected in closed HDPE carboys labeled 'Hazardous Flammable Solvent Waste' for licensed chemical disposal. Do not drain to municipal sewers.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `>= 99.8%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `>= 99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `48 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-simulation / post-layout extracted SPICE netlist (including parasitics R_BL, C_BL, R_WL, C_WL) verified against DRC/LVS rules; physical testboard coupon cleaned with IPA, nitrogen blow-dried, free of ionic contaminants and flux residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Simulated and validated netlist state tagged in repository; physical hardware interface test fixture stored in sealed moisture-barrier ESD bag with active color-indicating silica gel desiccant at < 10% RH under dry nitrogen purge.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric exposure (> 120 min in high humidity > 60% RH) induces surface moisture adsorption and copper/solder pad oxidation on physical shmoo interface boards, inducing parasitic pin-to-ground leakage paths (> 100 nA) that skew bitline telemetry measurements and mimic DRAM cell leakage.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful sign-off of mixed-signal transient co-simulation establishing deterministic timing closure for the refresh inhibit window across all PVT corners (FF, TT, SS at -40°C to +85°C, VDD = 1.62V to 1.98V). Complete parametric shmoo telemetry matrix validating variable retention pause limits from 1 ms to 64 ms without sense amplifier readback corruption, meeting 180nm open-source DRAM target specifications.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram180_refresh_inhibit_transient_timing_report.pdf`
- [ ] `shmoo_telemetry_vdd_vs_retention_pause_raw.csv`
- [ ] `transient_cosim_eye_margin_waveform_snapshot.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-01` | **Differential bitline signal delta V developed across C_BL = 250 fF upon exiting maximum 32 ms refresh inhibit window at 85°C TT corner** | `115.0 mV` | +/- 15.0 mV | Automated Ngspice transient node probe difference V(BL) - V(/BL) sampled exactly at SAN latch activation strobe edge. |
| `ASSERT-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-02` | **Timing margin between bitline equalization de-assertion (EQ falling below 10% VDD) and wordline assertion (WL rising above 10% VDD)** | `3.20 ns` | +/- 0.50 ns | Digital-analog mixed-signal cross-trigger timing analysis in GTKWave / automated Python waveform parsing script. |
| `ASSERT-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-03` | **Maximum retention pause duration achieving 100% March C- data retention pass rate across 1024-cell macro at nominal 1.80V, 25°C** | `64.0 ms` | +/- 4.0 ms | March C- microcode execution bit-audit telemetry log parsed from co-simulation output vector. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 3 quantitative assertions strictly met across Monte Carlo (N=200) and 3-sigma PVT corners; zero assertion violations in mixed-signal test harness; timing margins verified with positive slack (> 1.0 ns) on all refresh inhibit control signals; formal sign-off approval recorded from Systems Engineer and Lead Circuit Designer.

**Target Generation**: Gen 2 (µm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: Wirebond Shear >= 18 gf, ATE Functional Yield >= 90%, Coplanarity <= 0.08 mm.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Dage 4000 Bond Tester & Advantest Wafer Prober / CMM.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-layout SDF back-annotation reveals critical setup-time race conditions between the variable-pause refresh suppression counter and the March C- telemetry serial packetizer under extreme PVT corners (1.62V VDD, 125°C junction temperature). Without a dedicated asynchronous FIFO or synchronized handshake domain crossing between the BIST core clock (50 MHz) and the ESP32 telemetry UART interface (3.3V logic level, 921600 baud), bit-flip coordinate telemetry drops framing bytes during high-density fail bursts.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm planar node equivalent geometries (minimum gate length 150 nm, active diffusion width 0.15 µm), gate-level post-layout timing sign-off must strictly incorporate parasitic capacitance extraction (PEX) for bitline capacitance (C_bl) and storage node leakage (I_leak). If interconnect RC extraction on the column multiplexer fails to model metal 1 pitch coupling (0.34 µm pitch), hold-time violations will corrupt data retention telemetry counters during zero-refresh pause states, masking true sub-threshold storage dielectric decay with digital bus race conditions.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: The ESP32-WROOM-32D controller module and high-speed bidirectional level translators (TI TXS0108E) specified for automated Shmoo telemetry acquisition exhibit lead times exceeding 12 weeks with notable unit-to-unit threshold variation. Automated test equipment (ATE) breadboard test fixtures must use socketed commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) ICs screened for 1.8V to 3.3V transceiver jitter (<50 ps RMS) to prevent supply chain substitutions from invalidating timing sign-off.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The delivery schedule allocates only 5 business days for complete physical layout verification, PEX generation, and 100,000-cycle gate-level simulation across slow-slow (SS) and fast-fast (FF) corners. Without automated batch scripts running in parallel on high-throughput compute nodes, post-layout SDF timing extraction will bottle-neck tape-out sign-off milestones and delay mask data preparation (MDP).

The Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been authored and documented in [`docs/knowledge/sop_bit_flip_telemetry_and_retention_metrology.md`](./docs/knowledge/sop_bit_flip_telemetry_and_retention_metrology.md).

---

### Process Execution Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Initialize ESP32    │
│   March C- Sequence    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘

┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Execute Pause      │
│     Interval Step      │
│        t_pause         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘

```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Environmental & Fixture Preparation:**
   - Mount the packaged 180nm DRAM device under test (DUT) onto the high-speed socket of the ESP32 test interface.
   - Stabilize the DUT in a thermal chamber at **$85^\circ\text{C} \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Power supplies: set nominal array core $V_{DD}$, bitline precharge reference $V_{BLP} = V_{DD}/2$, and wordline boost voltage $V_{PP}$.
2. **Telemetry Link & Frame Integrity Check:**
   - Establish high-speed telemetry link (UART/SPI) with packet CRC verification and timestamp resolution $< 1\ \mu\text{s}$.
3. **March C- Algorithm Execution with Variable Pause Intervals:**
   - Command the ESP32 firmware to run March C- pattern stages: $\{\updownarrow (w0); \Uparrow (r0, w1); \Uparrow (r1, w0); \Downarrow (r0, w1); \Downarrow (r1, w0); \updownarrow (r0)\}$.
   - Insert programmable retention pause intervals ($t_{\text{pause}}$) between write and read stages, sweeping from **$1\text{ ms}$ to $256\text{ ms}$** (e.g., $1, 10, 32, 64, 128, 256\text{ ms}$).
4. **Automated $V_{DD}$ vs. $t_{\text{pause}}$ Shmoo Characterization:**
   - Step $V_{DD}$ in $50\text{ mV}$ decrements/increments across the operational boundary.
   - On read discrepancy, stream bit-flip telemetry logs: `[Timestamp, Row, Col, Expected_Bit, Read_Bit, VDD, t_pause]`.
5. **Array Retention Boundary Determination:**
   - Calculate retention boundary limit ($t_{\text{ret\_boundary}}$) defined by zero bit-flip threshold across all addresses at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

### Context Citations
- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:** Access transistor $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; stacked capacitor Crown structure with W-plug contact; ONO / $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ stack ($\kappa > 15$); $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF/cell}$; leakage current $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets:** $8F^2$ folded bitline cell area ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$); storage capacitance $C_s \ge 25\text{ fF to } 30\text{ fF}$; bitline parasitic capacitance $C_b = 150\text{ fF to } 250\text{ fF}$ for 256/512 cells/BL; $C_b / C_s$ kept between $5:1$ and $9:1$ (must not exceed $10:1$).
- **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:** Data retention requirement $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$; EOT $= 3\text{ nm to } 4\text{ nm}$; gate dielectric dry oxidation $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$; wordline and bitline pitch $= 360\text{ nm to } 400\text{ nm}$.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The closed-loop ESP32 motor controller UART telemetry buffer risks data packet drops during multi-kilobit burst March C- fail-dumps if hardware flow control (RTS/CTS) is omitted; telemetry transmission latencies directly warp the real retention pause window unless an independent, hardware-latched monotonic timer register on the FPGA/MCU test fixture governs pause intervals strictly decoupled from serial logging I/O.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm/Gen 2 micrometer boundary, storage capacitor sub-threshold leakage and access transistor junction leakage demonstrate severe thermal exponential dependencies (Arrhenius relationship doubling retention decay every 10°C). Failing to synchronize array retention boundary metrology with localized micro-thermocouple telemetry will lead to false-positive retention cliffs, confusing dielectric pinhole leakage with junction leakage.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: COTS ESP32-WROOM-32 modules exhibit lot-to-lot ADC non-linearities and reference voltage drifts up to 8% when regulating or monitoring array VDD shmoo rails, mandating external precision 16-bit DAC/ADC frontends (such as ADS1115 or DAC8562) with calibrated instrumentation references rather than onboard ESP32 analog peripherals.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The deliverable schedule requires direct correlation between optical gate/dielectric film thickness data (ellipsometry Psi/Delta logs) and retention boundary bit-flip maps within 48 hours of dice packaging to prevent testing unviable dies produced from drifted furnace oxidation runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Telemetry FIFO saturation on burst bit-flip error logging leading to truncated error address maps and uncalibrated pause duration measurement.
1. Thermal drift on uncooled test socket causing ambient temperature shifts to masquerade as early array retention cell degradation during VDD voltage scaling.
1. Coupled ground bounce across probe card power rails induced by full-array concurrent write/read transitions during March C- pass execution.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Hardware-Timed VDD Stepping & Refresh Inhibit Pause Engine Implementation

**Category**: Circuit Design | **Generation**: Gen 2 (µm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Coupling VDD stepping with refresh inhibit pause intervals introduces significant power supply transient noise on the core VDD rail. Rapid VDD switching via external DAC/LDO without closed-loop slew-rate limiting risks inductive rail collapse (L*di/dt) or overshoot, inadvertently flipping bitline precharge reference V_BLP (VDD/2) and corrupting unselected DRAM storage nodes prior to read activation.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: During extended refresh pause experiments, access transistor subthreshold leakage and junction leakage deplete the cell charge Q_s = C_s * (V_cell - V_BL). Stepping VDD down simultaneously reduces the cross-coupled regenerative sense amplifier signal margin Delta V = (C_s / (C_BL + C_s)) * (V_cell - VDD/2). If the hardware pause engine fails to synchronize the restoration phase (SAP pullup to stepped VDD and SAN pulldown to GND) within 1-2 ns of wordline overdrive (V_PP = 2.6-2.8V), false latching and destructive readouts will dominate over actual cell retention limits.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specifying ultra-low-noise, high-bandwidth programmable power supplies and fast analog multiplexers for automated sub-millivolt VDD stepping can encounter lead times exceeding 16 weeks; the engine design must leverage standard, multi-sourced COTS instrumentation or commodity precision DACs (e.g., DAC8562) with onboard ESP32 timer capture modules to avoid bench integration stalls.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Test characterization iterations for full-array retention pause shmoo sweeps risk severe schedule bottlenecks if executed sequentially across multi-voltage regimes; hardware-timed refresh inhibit engines must execute automated autonomous batch sweeps with onboard logging to avoid multi-day test rack occupancy.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dynamic rail droop during rapid VDD transition induces V_BLP offset shifts, triggering false differential latching during sense amplifier activation (SAN/SAP timing mismatch).
1. Asynchronous refresh inhibit gating glitches the internal row refresh counter, causing unmitigated retention fault cascades across adjacent inactive wordlines.
1. LDO/DAC settling ringing during the pause-to-read transition injects common-mode bitline bounce exceeding the 100 mV differential signal window.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-2-01` | **Hardware-Timed VDD Step Settling and Slew-Rate Verification under Inhibit Pause** | Keysight DSOX6004A 2.5 GHz Oscilloscope, 10:1 Low-Capacitance Active Probe, Keithley 2602B SourceMeter, ESP32 GPIO Timer Capture Rig | 1. Program ESP32 hardware timer to assert DRAM refresh inhibit pause signal for 100.0 ms. 2. Concurrently step core VDD from 1.800 V to 1.200 V in 50 mV decrements with programmed dwell time of 5.0 ms per step. 3. Trigger oscilloscope on the refresh inhibit assertion edge and record VDD rail transient response, ripple, and settling time. 4. Verify voltage stability prior to issuing read burst commands across Row 0 to 255. | `Settling time to within +/- 2.0 mV of target VDD step must be <= 12.0 us; peak overshoot/undershoot transient rail noise must not exceed 25.0 mV peak-to-peak; zero unprogrammed refresh pulses emitted during inhibit window.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-2-02` | **Automated Shmoo Retention Pause Bit-Flip Characterization vs VDD Scaling** | ESP32 MCU Controller running March C- Bit-Flip Telemetry Engine, Precision Programmable Supply (0.800 V to 2.000 V), Tektronix Logic Analyzer TLA7012 | 1. Initialize memory array with March C- background at nominal VDD = 1.800 V. 2. Gate refresh inhibit pause for a logarithmic duration sweep from 1.0 ms to 1000.0 ms. 3. Step VDD to target operating level (sweep 1.800 V down to 1.000 V in 25 mV steps). 4. At conclusion of pause window, restore VDD to 1.800 V within 50 us and trigger sequential row reads across 64 kb array. 5. Record fail bit count and address map via ESP32 telemetry UART stream. | `Bit-flip error detection latency <= 10.0 us post-pause; retention time at VDD = 1.800 V must exceed 64.0 ms with zero bit failures; bit failure inflection curve must map monotonically against stepped VDD with <= 1.5% measurement repeatability error across 10 consecutive runs.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: ANSI Z87.1 certified ESD-safe UV/clear safety spectacles, Class 0 ESD dissipation grounding wrist strap with 1 MOhm series resistor, Powder-free cleanroom-compatible nitrile gloves (4 mil)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of IPA eye contact, immediately flush eyes with copious volumes of clean water at emergency eyewash station for at least 15 minutes while holding eyelids open; seek medical evaluation. For skin contact, wash thoroughly with soap and water. If inhaled in high concentrations causing dizziness, remove individual to fresh air.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Benchtop localized laminar flow hood with minimum face velocity of 0.45 m/s (90 fpm) and dedicated VOC exhaust ducting during board-level solvent defluxing.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Collect spent IPA solvent in closed, flammables-rated, grounded steel waste containers; dispose through licensed hazardous chemical solvent waste management streams in compliance with local environmental regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, 2-Propanol)** | `67-63-0` | Semiconductor Grade VLSI | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2 Gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 5.0 | `99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `120 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `72 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-fabricated 180nm ceramic dual in-line package (CDIP) or open-cavity test coupon with pristine ENIG (Electroless Nickel Immersion Gold) test landing pads, free from organic residue and particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Defluxed, IPA-cleaned, N2-purged, dry package seated in zero-insertion-force (ZIF) characterization test socket with contact resistance < 50 mOhm.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive atmospheric humidity exposure leads to moisture absorption and galvanic oxidation on bitline/VDD Kelvin sense contacts, causing uncontrolled parasitic series resistance and erroneous millivolt-level VDD step droop.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Implementation and physical characterization of an ESP32 hardware-timed VDD stepping and refresh-inhibit engine capable of sub-millivolt power rail stepping, microsecond-accurate refresh pause intervals, and automated shmoo telemetry matrix acquisition for 180nm open-source DRAM 1T1C cell retention analysis.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `dram_vdd_shmoo_telemetry_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `hardware_timed_pause_engine_schematic.pdf`
- [ ] `vdd_step_transient_oscilloscope_capture.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **VDD stepping dynamic settling time to within +/- 2 mV of programmed setpoint under full bitline precharge active load** | `10.0 us` | +/- 2.0 us | High-bandwidth active oscilloscope probe measurement on VDD decoupling terminal triggered by DAC step strobe. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Hardware timer refresh-inhibit pause duration jitter and timing uncertainty across 1.0 ms to 1000.0 ms test windows** | `50.0 ns` | <= 15.0 ns | Logic analyzer hardware timestamping on ESP32 refresh-inhibit gate GPIO line referenced against 100 MHz reference clock. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Minimum baseline cell retention time at nominal VDD = 1.800 V and T = 25.0 deg C prior to first single-bit March pattern failure** | `64.0 ms` | +/- 4.0 ms | Automated binary search retention pause test with March C- verification across full 64 kb array. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 10 consecutive, automated, zero-abort VDD-versus-pause-time shmoo characterization sweeps covering VDD from 1.000 V to 1.800 V (25 mV resolution) and pause times from 1.0 ms to 256.0 ms, producing fully populated CSV error matrices with correlation coefficient R^2 >= 0.985 against analytical 1T1C charge leakage models.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Precision DAC $V_{DD}$ Step Regulator & Control Interface Circuit Design

**Module Hierarchy**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > ESP32 Closed-Loop Motor Controller [Electronics & Firmware] > Automated $V_{DD}$ vs Retention Time Shmoo Plot Telemetry Engine [Firmware & Software] > Variable Retention Pause & March Pattern Bit-Flip Audit Firmware [Firmware & Software] > Hardware-Timed $V_{DD}$ Stepping & Refresh Inhibit Pause Engine Implementation [Circuit Design] > **Precision DAC $V_{DD}$ Step Regulator & Control Interface Circuit Design [Circuit Design]**  
**Technology Generation**: Gen 2 (180 nm / 0.18 µm)  
**Action Type**: Make  
**Document Ref**: `SOP-DRAM180-CKT-042`

---

### System Architecture Flow (termaid)

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    ESP32 Controller    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
      SPI Bus│
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    12-bit / 16-bit     │
│     Precision DAC      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
   V_ref Step│
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     High-Bandwidth     │
│    Low-Noise OpAmp     │◄──────╮
│         Buffer         │       │
│                        │       │
└────────────┬───────────┘       │
             │                   │
 Gate Control│                   │
             ▼                   │
┌────────────────────────┐       │
│                        │       │
│  P-MOSFET / LDO Pass   │       │Kelvin Sense
│        Element         │       │
│                        │       │
└────────────┬───────────┘       │
             │                   │
             │Regulated V_DD     │
             ▼                   │
┌────────────────────────┐       │
│                        │       │
│  180nm DRAM V_DD Core  │       │
│          Rail          ├───────╯
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Bitline Signal Development vs. Core $V_{DD}$ (plotext monochrome)

Signal development differential voltage $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right)$ across stepped $V_{DD}$ levels (assuming cell $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$, bitline $C_{BL} = 250\text{ fF}$):

```text
Bitline Signal Development Delta V (mV) vs Stepped V_DD
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
```

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **Digital Control Bus & DAC Interface Setup**:
   - Route high-speed SPI from ESP32 (`SCK`, `MOSI`, `CS_N`, `LDAC_N`) to a 16-bit precision voltage-output DAC operating with an ultra-low-drift $2.500\text{ V}$ reference ($\le 5\text{ ppm/}^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Set SPI clock rate to $10\text{ MHz} - 20\text{ MHz}$ to enable single-command updates within $< 2\ \mu\text{s}$.
   - Ensure the DAC full-scale dynamic output range covers $0.0\text{ V}$ to $2.5\text{ V}$, mapping nominal $1.8\text{ V}$ to digital code `0xB851` ($47185_{10}$) with sub-$1\text{ mV}$ step resolution ($38.15\ \mu\text{V/LSB}$).

2. **Analog Error Amplifier & Voltage Translation Stage**:
   - Buffer DAC output through a rail-to-rail precision operational amplifier configured as an adjustable active series pass-element driver with Kelvin sense feedback.
   - Configure local phase compensation with a series RC lead-lag network ($R_c = 100\ \Omega$, $C_c = 470\text{ pF}$) across the amplifier feedback loop to ensure $> 60^\circ$ phase margin under capacitive bitline charging transients.

3. **High-Current Series Pass Element & Kelvin Sensing Layout**:
   - Drive a low-$R_{DS(on)}$ P-channel power MOSFET pass element or low-dropout regulator stage capable of $> 500\text{ mA}$ peak current delivery during folded bitline sense amplifier pull-down ($SAN$) and equalization phases.
   - Route true 4-wire remote Kelvin sense traces ($V_{\text{SENSE+}}$, $V_{\text{SENSE-}}$) directly from the 180nm DRAM chip core power pad array back to the inverting input of the error amplifier to nullify parasitic $I \cdot R$ drops on supply traces.

4. **Decoupling Network & Fast-Stepping transient Optimization**:
   - Place a distributed multi-stage ceramic decoupling network at the DUT socket: $10\ \mu\text{F}$ (X7R) for bulk reserve, $100\text{ nF}$ (C0G/X7R) for high-frequency suppression, and $1\text{ nF}$ (C0G) mounted within $2\text{ mm}$ of the DRAM package power pins.
   - Limit peak $dV/dt$ slew rate to $50\text{ mV/}\mu\text{s}$ via DAC software profiling or output RC shaping to prevent latch-up or uncontrolled false bit-flips during automated stepping sequences.

| **AC-02** | Effective Step Resolution (LSB) | $\le 1.0\text{ mV}$ | Automated SPI step ladder readback |
| **AC-03** | Step Settling Time ($100\text{ mV}$ step to $\pm 0.1\%$) | $\le 50\ \mu\text{s}$ | DSO with 10x passive probe on DUT Kelvin node |
| **AC-04** | Output Voltage Ripple & Noise ($10\text{ Hz} - 20\text{ MHz}$) | $\le 5.0\text{ mV}_{p-p}$ | AC-coupled 500 MHz oscilloscope with $50\ \Omega$ termination |

### Citations & Literature Context Integration

- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
  - Cell geometry: Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Capacitance budget: Minimum $C_s \ge 28\text{ fF}$ per cell (ONO or $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ dielectric) with sub-threshold/junction leakage $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$. This dictates the precise charge retention margin across degraded $V_{DD}$ steps.
- **[High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture]**:
  - Threshold voltage loss mechanism: Access NMOS $V_{th} \approx 0.5\text{ V} - 0.7\text{ V}$. Without wordline overdrive ($V_{PP} \ge 2.5\text{ V} - 2.8\text{ V}$), maximum write level degrades to $V_{DD} - V_{th} = 1.8\text{ V} - 0.6\text{ V} = 1.2\text{ V}$ (a $33\%$ loss in stored charge). The stepped regulator characterization isolates this threshold cliff.
- **[Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout]**:
  - Precharge equalization level is $V_{DD}/2$.
  - Signal development: $\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right) \approx 100\text{ mV} - 150\text{ mV}$ at nominal $1.8\text{ V}$ ($C_{BL} \approx 250\text{ fF}$, $C_s \approx 25\text{ fF} - 28\text{ fF}$). Low-noise $V_{DD}$ step regulation ($< 5\text{ mV}_{p-p}$ ripple) is mandatory to prevent false evaluation during $SAN$ latch activation.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: The step regulator must achieve dynamic settling times under 5 microseconds across a 0.8V to 2.2V programmable span into a capacitive decoupling load of 47 uF to prevent skewing the hardware-timed retention pause intervals during Shmoo telemetry profiling.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Because the 180nm DRAM access transistor relies on VPP overdrive (2.5V-2.8V) relative to VDD (nominal 1.8V), stepping VDD below 1.2V without dynamic clamp coordination risks severe wordline-to-drain stress and uncontrolled charge leakage through the access transistor.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: COTS high-precision 16-bit DACs (such as AD5686 or DAC8564) and low-noise operational amplifiers are subject to distributor allocation; the PCB footprint must provide dual-sourcing options between TSSOP and QFN packages to mitigate assembly halts.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Design review must freeze the I2C/SPI telemetry interface timing closure by Sprint 3 to avoid blocking the downstream automated March pattern bit-flip audit firmware integration milestones.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Regulator overshoot exceeding 2.4V during rapid voltage stepping, triggering gate-oxide breakdown in the 1.8V peripheral MOS devices.
1. Phase-margin degradation due to high ESR/capacitance of the DUT load causing continuous high-frequency oscillations (100 kHz - 2 MHz) on the DRAM VDD rail.
1. Ground bounce on the analog sense line causing spurious read errors during active burst operations.

The industrial Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for **Hardware-Timed Refresh Inhibit & Low-Jitter Pause Gating Implementation** has been generated and saved to [`sop_hardware_timed_refresh_inhibit_low_jitter_pause_gating.md`](./docs/sop_hardware_timed_refresh_inhibit_low_jitter_pause_gating.md).

### Summary of SOP Key Sections

```text
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│   1. Synchronous Boundary Detect      │
│      (Wait for t_RAS / t_RP Idle)     │
└───────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│   2. Glitch-Free Clock/Pulse Gating   │
│      (Deassert Auto-Refresh Trigger)  │
└───────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│   3. Hardware Counter-Timed Pause     │
│      (Precise Retention Window t_PAUSE)│
└───────────────────┬───────────────────┘
                    │
                    ▼
┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
│   4. Deterministic Gating Release     │
│      & Burst Audit Resumption         │
└───────────────────────────────────────┘
```

#### 1. Implementation Steps & Physical Parameters
- **Synchronous Inhibit Gating at Precharge Boundary**: Dual-stage synchronizer and clock-gating latch assert on the falling clock edge following precharge equalization ($EQ = 1$, $V_{BL} = V_{\overline{BL}} = V_{DD}/2$) and wordline deassertion ($WL = 0\ \text{V}$, isolated from boosted $V_{PP} = 2.6\ \text{V} - 2.8\ \text{V}$).
- **Hardware-Timed High-Resolution Pause Engine**: Down-counter hardware timer decrements the retention interval while holding sense amplifiers in balanced standby ($SAN = SAP = V_{DD}/2$) and preventing $dV_{DD}/dt$ supply bounce coupling into floating cell capacitors ($C_s \ge 25\ \text{fF} - 30\ \text{fF}$).
- **Low-Jitter Resume & Audit Strobe Synchronization**: Deterministic release aligned to the positive clock edge triggers immediate March pattern audit with regenerative sense amplification ($SAN \to \text{GND}$, followed by $SAP \to V_{DD}$ with calibrated $1\ \text{ns} - 2\ \text{ns}$ delay).

#### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria
- **Pause Gating Edge Jitter ($t_{\text{jitter}}$)**: $\le 50\ \text{ps RMS}$ ($\le 200\ \text{ps peak-to-peak}$) verified via high-bandwidth DSO.
- **Refresh Glitch Suppression Margin**: $0\ \text{V}$ runt pulse / $100\%$ glitch-free command deassertion.
- **Pre-Gating Array Quiescent State**: $WL = 0\ \text{V}$, $V_{BL} = V_{\overline{BL}} = V_{DD}/2 \pm 15\ \text{mV}$.
- **Post-Pause Sense Activation Delay ($\Delta t_{SAN\text{-}SAP}$)**: $1.0\ \text{ns} \le \Delta t \le 2.0\ \text{ns}$.

#### 3. Literature Citations
- **Folded Bitline Sense Amplifier Circuit Design for DRAM Cell Readout**: Governs bitline equalization to $V_{DD}/2$ and signal development:
  $$\Delta V = \left(\frac{C_s}{C_{BL} + C_s}\right) \cdot \left(V_{\text{cell}} - \frac{V_{DD}}{2}\right) \approx 100\ \text{mV} - 150\ \text{mV}$$
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**: Governs $8F^2$ footprint ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ at $180\ \text{nm}$), $C_s \ge 25\ \text{fF} - 30\ \text{fF}$, and $C_{BL} = 150\ \text{fF} - 250\ \text{fF}$ with capacitance ratios bounded to $5:1 - 9:1$.
- **Cross-Coupled Regenerative Sense Amplifier Timing & Charge Restoration**: Governs boosted $V_{PP} = 2.6\ \text{V} - 2.8\ \text{V}$ gate overdrive and two-stage regenerative latch timing ($SAN$ pulldown followed by $SAP$ pullup with $1\ \text{ns} - 2\ \text{ns}$ delay).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Hardware refresh inhibition requires deterministic pause gating synchronously aligned to tRFC and row-cycle boundaries. If the ESP32 timer gating circuit deasserts refresh asynchronously relative to the DRAM internal refresh counter or sense amplifier precharge phases (EQ to VDD/2), mid-cycle bitline charge injection or floating bitline states will cause artificial cell corruption uncorrelated with dielectric leakage. Gating synchronization must employ a dual-stage synchronizer flip-flop clocked by the DRAM master clock domain with worst-case jitter under 50 ps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm node with a 1T1C folded bitline structure, storage node capacitance (Cs) is 25-28 fF and bitline capacitance (Cb) is 150-250 fF, producing a sensing delta V of only 100-150 mV. During intentional refresh inhibit pauses up to 1000 ms for retention Shmoo mapping, subthreshold leakage of the access NMOS and junction leakage across the storage diffusion node will discharge Cs below the sense amplifier latching threshold. Any digital jitter or switching bounce (>20 mV) on the inhibit control line coupled into VDD or VBB will prematurely corrupt marginal weak cells.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Implementing low-jitter hardware-timed gating on COTS ESP32 controller test fixtures requires discrete fast-switching logic buffers (e.g., 74LVC1G series or discrete PECL/LVDS transceivers) and precision RF coaxial cabling (SMA to microstrip pigtails). Sourcing automotive-grade -40°C to 125°C rated precision surface-mount pulse-forming gates and ultra-low jitter crystal oscillators (TCXO < 1 ps RMS phase jitter) must be secured across multiple distributors (DigiKey, Mouser, LCSC) with minimum 16-week safety stock.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The Shmoo telemetry engine schedule is on the critical path for Gen 2 silicon characterization. Designing custom discrete hardware gating logic must not expand firmware testing cycle time beyond the allocated sprint window. A clear interface boundary—using hardware timer PWM/capture-compare pins on ESP32 routed through matched 50-ohm traces to the probe card—must be frozen before tape-in to avoid PCB re-spins.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Asynchronous refresh gating assertion during an active row precharge/restore phase, resulting in incomplete latching and systematic bit-line pattern destruction.
1. Ground bounce and power-rail supply collapse on testboard during simultaneous refresh inhibit release across array blocks, causing false retention-fail reads.
1. Clock jitter and duty-cycle distortion on the ESP32 timer output exceeding 250 ps, introducing timing measurement uncertainty in retention Shmoo plots.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-2-2-01` | **Hardware Refresh Inhibit Timing Jitter and Edge Determinism Verification** | Keysight Infiniium 4 GHz Real-Time Oscilloscope (50-ohm DC coupled), PicoScope 6000E Arbitrary Waveform Generator, Keysight N2795A 1 GHz active probe, Keysight 34465A DMM | 1. Configure ESP32 hardware timer to generate a 50 ms active-high refresh inhibit pulse repeating every 100 ms. 2. Connect active differential probes across the refresh inhibit pin and the DRAM master clock. 3. Acquire 100,000 trigger cycles on the oscilloscope at 20 GSa/s with persistence enabled. 4. Measure rising/falling edge propagation delay skew, peak-to-peak jitter, and RMS phase jitter using jitter analysis software. 5. Verify inhibit deassertion coincides strictly with the falling edge of DRAM master clock. | `Peak-to-peak jitter on the refresh inhibit gate signal must be <= 45 ps (target <= 30 ps); RMS jitter must be <= 5.0 ps; gate propagation delay relative to master clock edge must remain between 1.20 ns and 1.80 ns across all 100,000 cycles.` |
| `TC-MCU-COTS-SHMOO-2-2-2-02` | **Variable Retention Pause Duration Accuracy & March-C Fault Bit Shmoo Readout** | ESP32 Closed-Loop Automated Test Rig, Keithley 2450 SourceMeter (VDD supply), High-Speed Logic Analyzer (Saleae Logic Pro 16, 500 MSa/s), Temperature Chamber at 25.0°C and 85.0°C | 1. Program ESP32 Shmoo telemetry engine to sweep VDD from 1.80 V down to 1.20 V in 20 mV steps. 2. At each voltage step, apply hardware refresh inhibit pauses stepped logarithmically from 1 ms to 2000 ms (1 ms, 2 ms, 5 ms, ..., 2000 ms). 3. Upon hardware-timed pause completion, re-enable refresh and immediately execute March C- read audit pass at full speed. 4. Record bit-flip fail counts, physical fail addresses, and elapsed pause intervals to telemetry host via UART DMA. 5. Correlate pause accuracy against calibrated hardware timer counter. | `Hardware pause duration error must be < 0.01% (+/- 100 ns absolute maximum); zero retention bit failures detected at 25°C for pause times <= 64 ms at VDD = 1.80 V; Shmoo bitmap boundaries must demonstrate monotonic retention-time vs VDD decay profile without stochastic dropouts.` |
